Research §5 mitigation path, escalate only on probe evidence: raise `sliceCount`, ensure downstream TAA is enabled (it integrates the frame-index slice rotation already wired), then a 2-iteration à-trous on `BilateralBlur1D`. - **NEW-WEBGPU-IMAGERY-CACHE-KEY-CROSS-LAYER-COLLISION — ROOT-FIXED (SHIPPED in Batch 686, C9-12A hardening review F5); originally FILED (2026-07-16, C9-12A Principle-9 spinoff); premise CONFIRMED by code inspection.** **Resolution:** `imageryCacheKey(imagery)` (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts`) now prefixes a stable per-`ImageryLayer` WeakMap id — `L{layerId}_x_y_level` (`imagery.key` still wins if ever assigned); BOTH derivation sites (`resolveImageryProjection` + `getOrCreateImageryTexture`, incl. the `_merc` suffix variants and the identity-guarded cleanups, which capture the derived key by value) route through the one helper, so the merc/reproj guard risk called out below is closed by construction. Memory stays deduped for shareable sources — the C9-12A realization table BELOW the cache keys on source identity, not this string. **Runtime gate (Batch 686):** two-GridImagery-layer reconciliation probe — `imageryRealizationsCreated`=**2** (the collision would leave 1: the second layer cache-hits the first's entry and never uploads), per-layer mip-job labels `Globe L1_1_0_1`/`Globe L2_1_0_1`, shares=62, liveBytes=699,048 (exactly 2×349,524), zero errors; full C9-12A gate suite re-green (crossBackend 0.46%, terrain-selection exact hash). Historical filing below, kept for trace. The WebGPU per-renderer `_imageryTextureCache` (direct-upload + merc/reproj) keys entries on `imagery.key` falling back to an `x_y_level` string (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts` `resolveImageryProjection`/`getOrCreateImageryTexture`), and `imagery.key` is **never assigned in-tree** — so the key carries NO layer/provider component. Two geographic-provider ImageryLayers whose tiles share the same tile x/y/level can therefore alias each other's cached GPUTexture on the `projection.variant === "geo"` cache-hit branch. **What C9-12A did/didn't fix:** the C9-12A realization fingerprint (`sourceId·revision|descriptor`) fixes aliasing for SHAREABLE (immutable) sources — two layers with distinct source objects get distinct realizations even at the same coordinate. It does NOT fix the owned/reproj cache-entry key itself. **Why deferred, not folded in:** FAR-205's acceptance requires "two layers/providers/maps at identical coordinates never alias"; the general fix is to prefix the cache key with a per-layer/provider id (or the imagery-layer's `_imageryCache` id). Folding a silent owned-key change into C9-12A would violate the campaign's one-concern-per-slice rule and risk the merc/reproj dual-texture cleanup identity guards (which are keyed off the same string). **Repro to build first (Principle 8):** two `GridImageryProvider` layers with different `color` on the same globe; assert each tile samples its own layer's texture (currently the second layer may sample the first's cached texture at shared coordinates). **Prerequisites:** a stable per-ImageryLayer id reachable from `getOrCreateImageryTexture` (the `tileImagery.readyImagery.imageryLayer` chain). **Effort:** ~1 session (key-prefix + cleanup-guard update + a 2-layer parity probe). **Impact:** correctness for multi-layer geographic imagery; latent today because most stacks use one geographic base layer. **Trace:** C9-12A guide Traps #3; `FORK_ARCHITECTURE_REMEDIATION_PLAN_2026-07-13.md` FAR-205 acceptance (lines 556-571).

- **NEW-WEBGPU-OCEANNORMAL-PER-CALL-REUPLOAD — ✅ RESOLVED (2026-07-19, Batch 717).** Fixed exactly as the fix sketch below prescribed: a source-identity memo (`_oceanNormalMapSource` / `_oceanNormalMapView`) on the oceanNormal single-slot cache in `_createWaterOceanMaterialBindGroupInner`, mirroring the in-file `_materialTextureCache` idiom, with the guard reset alongside the texture destroys in the renderer teardown. **This was the dominant WebGPU CPU cost, not a minor perf item.** Measured on a static settled default scene (9 draw commands, 6 tiles), `requestRenderMode=false` on BOTH backends so every call does real work: WebGPU `scene.render()` **10.5 ms → 0.9 ms (11.7× faster)**; WebGPU/WebGL cost ratio **17.5× → 1.5×**; in the as-shipped `requestRenderMode` lane WebGPU went from 10.6 ms to **1.1 ms vs WebGL 1.2 ms (now FASTER than WebGL)**. V8 sampling profile before: `copyExternalImageToTexture` = **47% of all CPU self-time** (2456 ms/150 frames) plus `generateMipmaps` 94 ms, `createView` 143 ms, `createBindGroup` 165 ms, `createTexture` 40 ms; after: **all five absent from the top-18**, and the WebGPU profile is 68.7% idle vs WebGL's 69.1% (i.e. at parity). Correctness re-verified per the frozen-ocean warning below — `probe-webgpu-ocean-waves`: brightness gpu/gl **0.996**, wave-detail gpu/gl **1.204**, WebGPU temporal wave delta **1.818** (>0.3 = animating), PNGs read and clean. New diagnostic tooling landed with the fix: `probe-cpu-sampling-profile.mjs` (V8/CDP sampling profiler over the render loop — this is what localized it, after the in-engine per-pass profiler accounted for only 0.117 ms of the 10.5 ms frame), `probe-webgpu-frame-breakdown.mjs`, `probe-request-render-asymmetry.mjs`, `probe-backend-isolation.mjs`. **Original filing follows.** — **FILED (2026-07-17, Batch 685 C9-12A reconciliation spinoff); premise CONFIRMED by runtime instrumentation + code inspection.** The per-tile water/ocean bind-group path re-uploads the ocean normal map EVERY call: `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.createTileCommands` unconditionally rebuilds `bindGroup2Final` via `_createWaterOceanMaterialBindGroup` per tile per pass (both the material and no-material branches, ~L1734-1748), and `_createWaterOceanMaterialBindGroupInner` (~L2084-2108) calls `uploadImageSource(this, source, "oceanNormal", this._oceanNormalMapCache)` with **no cache-hit guard** — and `uploadImageSource` itself never checks its cache before creating a texture (callers own the guard). Every call therefore creates a fresh `GPUTexture` + `copyExternalImageToTexture` + a 9-level mip chain, and the fresh VIEW identity in turn defeats the group-2 bind-group cache key for the next frame (self-perpetuating). **Measured (Batch 685, GridImagery 3-altitude route, 540 rendered frames):** 20,155 `Globe oceanNormal` mip-prep enqueues ≈ 37/frame (≈ per tile per frame); the overwritten cache entries orphan their textures to GC-paced destruction (VRAM churn, no explicit destroy — the C9-12A owned-retirement hook only binds to imagery-owned entries). **PRE-EXISTING, not a C9-12A regression:** the call path and the missing guard are identical on clean main, where each call ALSO paid a private `generateMipmapsAndSubmit` `queue.submit` (~37 private submits/frame when an oceanNormalMap is present); C9-12A merely coalesces those into the one frame-owned `"ImageryMipPreparation"` submit (strictly fewer submits, same texture churn). The C9-01 audit lane did not surface this because its route/terrain had no `oceanNormalMap` bound. **Fix sketch (its own slice):** a source-identity memo mirroring the in-file `_materialTextureCache` pattern (`cached.source === value → reuse view`, ~L2046-2048) on the oceanNormal single-slot cache, with an explicit invalidation when `tileProvider.oceanNormalMap`/`_webgpuSource` identity changes; must keep ocean waves animating (frozen-ocean is a real failure class) and re-verify the group-2 bind-group cache hit-rate + water probes (`probe-water*`, ocean-brightness lanes) both backends. **Impact:** correctness-adjacent perf (per-frame texture creates + 8 mip render passes × ~tiles, GC-paced VRAM churn) on any scene with a water-mask terrain / ocean normal map. **Effort:** S-M. **Batch-686 note:** the renderer-destroy inline destroys of the oceanNormal/water-mask caches are now F7-stamped (`noteInlineTextureDestroy`) so a mid-frame teardown can no longer race a pending frame-owned mip job into a validation error; the per-frame re-upload storm itself is unchanged. **Trace:** Batch 685 shares-count reconciliation instrumentation (`WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md` C9-12A, 2026-07-17).

- **NEW-WEBGPU-SPLAT-DATA-PRODUCER — FILED (2026-07-18, C10-04-SPLAT-ASYNC-SORT STOP-AND-BLOCK #1 verdict); premise CONFIRMED by fresh repo-wide producer trace + two independent prior notes.** The WebGPU Gaussian-splat feature renderer (`WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts`) has **no production data producer** — in production it never receives splat data and therefore never draws. **Trace (2026-07-18):** the production chain `Cesium3DTileContentFactory` → `GaussianSplat3DTileContent.fromGltf` → `tileset.gaussianSplatPrimitive = new GaussianSplatPrimitive(...)` loads glTF/SPZ splat data (via `GltfLoader`/`GltfSpzLoader`) into snapshot buffers; but `GaussianSplatPrimitive.update()` (`:1186`) resolves the FR and, when the WebGPU FR is ready, calls `fr.update(this, frameState)` and **returns at `:1197`**. Everything that packs render data — `commitSnapshot` (`:407`, writes `_positions`/`_indexes`/`gaussianSplatTexture`), `GaussianSplatTextureGenerator`, `buildGSplatDrawCommand` (`:1967`, builds the WebGL `usampler2D` attribute texture + VertexArray + `DrawCommand`) — sits in the WebGL continuation reached AFTER the FR-return (`resolveSteadySort:681` → `commitSnapshot`), so under WebGPU **none of it runs**. The FR reads only `primitive._splatData || primitive._renderResources?.splatBuffer` (`WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:1231`) and nothing else off the primitive (not `_positions`, not `gaussianSplatTexture`). **Both fields are never assigned anywhere in production JS/TS:** `git grep '_splatData ='` = 0 hits (excluding `_splatDataGeneration`); `git grep '_renderResources ='` = 0 hits; `_renderResources` is **never referenced** in `GaussianSplatPrimitive.js`. Result: `splatData === undefined` → the buffer-build branch (`revision !== cache.lastRevision && splatData`, `:1233`) never fires → `cache.splatBuffer` stays null, `cache.splatCount` stays 0 → `maybeSortSplats` (`:914`) returns at its `count === 0` guard. **The only exerciser** is `Tools/visual-regression/probe-splat-sort.mjs`, which synthetically injects a 3-splat interleaved `_splatData` `Float32Array` onto a hand-rolled fake primitive object. This matches two prior in-tree notes: Batch 288 (`WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md:894`) — "the renderer never actually drew before — no `_splatData` producer is wired, so these were dormant"; and the C10-09 worker (`:60`) — "production `_splatData` has no JS producer — C10-04 territory". **What the missing producer must do (the C10-04 unblock):** a WebGPU-path data commit (the WebGPU analog of `commitSnapshot`/`buildGSplatDrawCommand`) that packs the loaded snapshot — model-space `positions` + (`rotations`,`scales`→3D covariance) + `colors` + `shData` — into the tightly-packed **16-float/splat interleaved record** the FR expects (`posHigh(3)+posLow(3)+covA(3)+covB(3)+color(4)` = 64 B, layout documented `WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts:118-138`), assign it to `primitive._splatData` + `primitive._splatCount`, and run it BEFORE/within the WebGPU FR dispatch. It must also expose model-space positions (a `Float32Array(count*3)`, or derivable from the record) because the C10-04 worker sort and the eye-space-z depth key both need them. **Prerequisites:** decide where the WebGPU splat-commit lives (a WebGPU branch in `GaussianSplatPrimitive.update` before the `if (fr) return`, or inside the FR consuming the snapshot buffers directly); a real `.spz`/glTF-splat 3D Tileset asset (the Sandcastle splat demos reference remote iTwin/example assets — none is offline in-tree) OR a faithful synthetic-scene builder. **Effort:** L (multi-session feature — this is the WebGPU half of the Gaussian-splat rendering path, not a perf slice). **Impact:** WebGPU Gaussian-splat rendering is currently probe-only; the log-depth (Batch 288), sort-consume (Batch 288), and velocity (C10-09) work all sit on this dormant path. Until this producer lands, `WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer` is SCAFFOLDED-not-SHIPPED for production (FEATURE_INVENTORY §B splat line annotated). **Trace:** C10-04 STOP-AND-BLOCK verdict (`QUEUE_2026-07-16_CAMPAIGN10.md` §3.2 C10-04 row, BLOCKED 2026-07-18); guide `CAMPAIGN10_EXECUTION_GUIDE_2026-07-16.md` H4 STOP-AND-BLOCK #1.

- **NEW-WEBGPU-SHADERDEFINE-WIDTH-EXPANSION (aka `C10-08b` / C11-149) — FILED (2026-07-18, C10-08-MODEL-SHADER-SPECIALIZATION-AXES Phase-0 STOP-AND-BLOCK #0 verdict); premise CONFIRMED by full registry read + preprocessor/pipeline-cache trace.** The `ShaderDefine` bitmask registry (`WebGPUShaderDefines.ts`) is a **Uint32 and is EXHAUSTED** — bits **0 through 30 are all occupied with no gaps and no reclaimable/deprecated entries** (`GEODETIC_NORMAL = 1<<0` … `MODEL_METADATA_MAT_TRANSPORT = 1<<30`, verified by reading all 31 JSDoc'd entries). **Only bit 31 remains, and it is the JS sign bit** (`1<<31 = -2147483648`), usable only via `>>> 0` coercion at every arithmetic site and NEVER as a material-mask bit (a material bit ≥ 29 overflows `computeKey`'s `md << 3` pipeline-key packing, `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:317-318`). **Why this blocks new specialization work:** the model-shader specialization the fork needs (C10-08 and the 6-7 model uber-shader axes ranked in guide H5 — shadow mode, IBL mode, per-KHR-extension bits, velocity, skinning/morph/instancing) can only achieve source-level dead-branch stripping (the register/occupancy win) through the **shared `//>>ifdef` preprocessor**, which **throws at preprocess time on any flag that does not resolve to a registered global `ShaderDefine` bit** (`WebGPUShaderPreprocessor.ts:111-116`, `resolveDefineBit` → undefined → Error). There is NO model-local `//>>ifdef`. The two model-local alternatives both fail the charter: (a) **WGSL pipeline-overridable `override` constants** are not threaded into the render pipeline path (only `WebGPUComputePipelineCache` passes `constants:`; `WebGPURenderPipelineCache`/`WebGPUModelPipelineCache` do not), they are pipeline-level so they do NOT manifest as distinct `(sourceId,defines[,keySalt])` module-cache entries (breaking the acceptance's cache-keying rule), and adding them edits the shared module source → the 215 KB `ModelPBRComplete` module hash changes for EVERY model scene (breaks the "defines=0 byte-identical to today" charter, INV-08-5/T-08-f); (b) **keySalt-routed** specialization only disambiguates already-different source strings — it cannot STRIP the base branch without either editing the base source (breaking byte-identical) or running a private model-only text-substitution namespace, which guide H5 Step-0(c) EXPLICITLY forbids ("fragments the specialization infrastructure and violates the shared-registry contract. Surface, don't route around."). **Therefore any new specialization axis genuinely requires a new global define bit, and the register is full.** **The fix (this item):** widen the define representation beyond Uint32 — a hi/lo Uint32 pair OR a Number/BigInt mask — cross-cutting the `WebGPUShaderModuleCache` key math (`((defines>>>0)*0x100)+sourceId`, which represents the full Uint32 exactly today and **build-breaks on a 33rd bit** — G9:68-71), `computeKey`'s `md << 3`, `MATERIAL_DEFINE_MASK`, `WebGPUShaderPreprocessor` flag resolution, `effectiveDefines`, and **every** `(x & BIT)` / `defineKeyToNames` site (add-only, never reorder/renumber existing bits). **Prerequisites:** none (pure infra). **Effort:** M (one focused slice; C11 owns it as C11-149, HARD prerequisite for any new define bit per `campaign11_planning/_PLANNING_STATUS.md:49-50/82-84` and `CAMPAIGN11_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md:67`). **Impact:** unblocks C10-08 + the entire model uber-shader specialization program (the structural reason model-heavy WebGPU scenes trail WebGL per-material GLSL, guide H5 "Architecture today"); also unblocks any other subsystem needing a 33rd+ define (enhanced-ocean `ENHANCED_OCEAN` gate, tiles TILE-ARCH-SHADER-STRATEGY). **Sequencing note (deviation surfaced for maintainer ratification):** guide H5 / the C10 queue / C11-plan G9 (`:1074/1087`) originally sequenced "C10-08 banks bit 31 → C10-08b widens → remaining axes." The C10-08 Phase-0 verdict (2026-07-18), per the governing orchestrator directive ("do not consume the last bit; if only bit 31 remains, STOP and report BLOCKED on define-width"), **flips that dependency**: do C10-08b (this item) FIRST, then promote ALL model axes (including shadow) cleanly on the widened register — banking the fragile sign-bit for one axis is throwaway motion since the widening is required for the other 6-7 axes regardless. **Trace:** C10-08 Phase-0 verdict (`QUEUE_2026-07-16_CAMPAIGN10.md` §3.2 C10-08 row, BLOCKED 2026-07-18); `WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md` C10-08 entry (2026-07-18); guide `CAMPAIGN10_EXECUTION_GUIDE_2026-07-16.md` H5 Step-0 + T-08-a.

## 2026-08-01 — MOON-ALBEDO-MIP-LOD (surfaced during C12-24, the 2K NASA albedo ingest)

- **MOON-ALBEDO-MIP-LOD — OPEN, correctness/quality (blocks any moon albedo above 2K, and makes an existing shimmer worse at the current default).** Neither backend mipmaps the moon texture. WebGL: `Scene/Material.js` never calls `generateMipmap()` and the sampler is plain `LINEAR` — the gap is in the shared Material image path, not in `Moon`/`EllipsoidPrimitive`, so every image material shares it. WebGPU: `WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer._loadRealMoonTexture` creates the texture with the default `mipLevelCount` 1, the sampler (same file, moon cache init) sets no `mipmapFilter`, and `Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/Moon.wgsl` deliberately samples with `textureSampleLevel(tex, samp, uv, 0.0)` because `computeEllipsoidColor` is called from **non-uniform control flow** (the inside-face branch depends on the outside-face result), which forbids implicit-derivative `textureSample`.
  - **Why it now matters:** C12-24 raised the default albedo from 256×128 to 2048×1024. At the *default* camera the moon disc is only ~16 px across (0.52° in a ~36° vertical FOV at 1080 p) while the visible hemisphere of a 2048-wide equirect is 1024 texels — roughly **64:1 minification sampled at mip 0**, versus ~8:1 for the old map. That is a pre-existing aliasing/shimmer condition made measurably worse under camera motion, even though the swap is a large win at the zoomed views C12-24 was raised for (~5.4:1 at a 190 px disc vs the old map's 0.67 texels/px). Mitigation available today with zero code: `Moon.Variant.SMALL`.
  - **Proposed fix (both backends, lockstep):** generate mips on both sides, add `mipmapFilter: "linear"` to the WebGPU moon sampler and a mipmap minification filter on the WebGL Material texture, and feed the WGSL **one CPU-computed LOD uniform** — `lod = clamp(log2((texWidth / 2) / discDiameterPx), 0, maxLod)`, where `discDiameterPx` follows from the moon's angular radius and the pixel angular size. The moon is a distant sphere, so that LOD is effectively constant across the disc: no screen-space derivatives are needed and the non-uniform-control-flow restriction is sidestepped entirely. This IS a shader change ⇒ **lockstep pair + a `SHADER_PAIRS_LOCKSTEP.md` row**, and the WebGL half needs the Material-level mipmap support first (cross-cutting — scope it deliberately).
  - **Effort:** M. **Tracked as `C12-33`** in `QUEUE_2026-07-19_CAMPAIGN12.md`. **Trace:** `Tools/moon-albedo-bake/README.md` §6.2.

- **MOON-ALBEDO-KTX2 — OPEN, tooling-blocked (size/VRAM optimization).** The C12-24 albedo ships as JPEG q90 4:4:4 (563,276 B) because **no KTX2/Basis encoder exists in this repo or on the build machine**: `toktx`, `ktx` and `basisu` are all absent from `PATH`, and the installed `ktx-parse` is a container parser, not a BasisU/UASTC encoder. A UASTC or ETC1S KTX2 would cut both the download and the VRAM footprint (the JPEG decompresses to 8 MB of `rgba8unorm`; a transcoded BC7/ASTC would be ~2 MB). `Tools/moon-albedo-bake/bake-lroc-color.mjs` is already structured so only the encode stage changes. Note the consumer side is not free either: `Moon.textureUrl` flows through `Resource.fetchImage()` on WebGPU and `Material`'s image path on WebGL, neither of which transcodes KTX2 today. **Effort:** S (encode) + M (consumer paths). **Trace:** `Tools/moon-albedo-bake/README.md` §6.1.

## 2026-07-19 — OCEAN-WAVE-OCTAVE-LOD (surfaced during OCEAN-WAVES PERF AUDIT for C11-158)

- **OCEAN-WAVE-HIGHLAT-HORIZON-BAND — FILED (2026-07-24, Batch 757 orchestrator high-lat sweep during the C11-172 landing).** At ~53N/178E (Bering basin, open water, 50 m camera) a corduroy aliasing band remains just under the horizon on WebGPU (far-band Laplacian variance ~25 vs ~1.8 at the 25N/-150 gate site): the ×15 m ripple octave's cos(lat)-compressed zonal wavelength (~9 m at 53N) sits near-Nyquist on the still-resolvable min footprint axis, so it renders as barely-resolved structured striping rather than fading. Near-field waves there are natural (lapVar 4.4, animating 6.1). The hardware-aniso footprint clamp (max(minAxis, maxAxis/8), landed Batch 757) is correct but does not address this — the content is genuinely near-Nyquist on the resolvable axis. **Fix directions (pick after visual tuning):** (a) tighten `OCEAN_OCTAVE_FADE_LO/HI` globally; (b) latitude-compensate the per-octave repeat counts (divide zonal repeats by cos(lat) so metric wavelength is lat-invariant — also fixes the documented 2× meridional factor); (c) accept + document as sea-state character. Evidence PNGs in the Batch-757 scratchpad (`highlat2-low-webgpu.png`). **Effort:** S (tuning) to M (lat-compensation with seam care at the poles). **Trace:** C11-172 landing, probe-ocean-wave-lod.mjs header note.

- **OCEAN-WAVE-OCTAVE-LOD — ✅ RESOLVED-SUPERSEDED by C11-172 (Batch 757, 2026-07-24).** The maintainer's expanded C11-172 subsumed and outgrew this entry: the landed physical-wavelength redesign gives per-octave pixel-footprint attenuation (the fade this entry proposed) PLUS a hard cutoff that skips all three fetches across the far field (a larger saving than the 3→2→1 octave gating sketched here), and the mip-aware `textureSampleGrad` sampling removed the aliasing that made the octaves visible noise. The WebGL 2-octave path got the matching policy (calibrated by `czm_getWaterNoise`'s internal divisors). Original filing below, kept for trace. — **OCEAN-WAVE-OCTAVE-LOD (historical) — OPEN, optimization (cheap win, ~1/3 of the wave-march texture-fetch cost at mid-altitude with no visible change).** The WebGPU enhanced-ocean wave march `sampleOceanWaveNormals` (`Shaders/WebGPU/Globe/GlobeTerrain.wgsl` ~L2221) does **3 fixed octaves** = 3× `textureSampleLevel(oceanNormalMap)` per ocean fragment (uv×400 "swells", uv×200 "medium", uv×800 "wind ripples" blended 0.6/0.3/0.1), plus an ENU mat3 build + foam + GGX/Fresnel specular + SSS. Cost is **per-fragment-linear in octave count** (confirmed: 3 texture fetches ↔ 3 octaves) and runs for **every** ocean fragment where `tile.flags.z` (showOceanWaves) is set and `coastCoverage>0`, gated by `globe.showWaterEffect` (default true) + a water-mask terrain provider + `oceanNormalMap` (default `waterNormalsSmall.jpg`). **Measured GPU cost** (probe `Tools/visual-regression/probe-ocean-waves-perf.mjs`, HEAD `8622c2ce54`, Edge/Vulkan timestamp-query, 100%-ocean nadir @ ~18–20 km, r5×2 views): scene color pass **+0.29–0.36 ms (+18–22 %)**, whole GPU frame **+0.40–0.44 ms (+14–15 %)** vs waves-OFF — statistically unambiguous (>3× the OFF-state timestamp noise of 0.001–0.14 ms), lighting-independent (Pacific-night ≈ Indian-daylit).
  - **Proposed optimization:** altitude/distance-gate the octave count in `sampleOceanWaveNormals` (3 octaves < ~50 km → 2 octaves 50–200 km → 1 octave 200 km–~1 Mm), **reusing the existing `waveIntensityFade` distance ramp** already computed in `computeEnhancedOcean`. The high-frequency ×800 "wind ripple" octave (weight 0.1) is sub-pixel beyond a few km, so dropping it at range is visually inert. Estimated saving ~0.1 ms/frame at mid-altitude ocean; larger for ocean-dominant flyovers. A mip-bias / analytic-derivative LOD on the `oceanNormalMap` sample is an alternative/companion.
  - **WebGL parity note:** the WebGL classic path (`GlobeFS.glsl::computeWaterColor`, same `showWaterEffect` gate, both default true) uses **2 octaves** (high-alt + low-alt blend) vs WGSL's 3 — so an octave-LOD that lands at 2 octaves mid-range also *reduces* the fork's WGSL-only 3-octave divergence (documented in the GlobeTerrain.wgsl convention ledger ~L3824). If applied to both backends, keep them in lockstep.
  - **C11-158 cross-ref (CRITICAL premise correction):** the C11-158 field `globe.enableEnhancedOcean` (default true) does **NOT** gate this GPU cost — it appears nowhere in `Renderer/WebGPU/**` or the WGSL; it only sets CPU-side color params (`oceanDeepColor`/`oceanFresnelPower`/`oceanReflectivity`/`oceanFoamThreshold`/`oceanDarkening`) to `undefined`/0 when false, after which the shader falls back to hardcoded defaults and **still runs the full 3-octave march**. Defaulting `enableEnhancedOcean=false` therefore changes ocean *coloring* at **~0 GPU saving**. The actual GPU lever is `showWaterEffect` / the flags.z wave gate. Audit report: `Tools/visual-regression/output/ocean-waves-perf-audit-2026-07-19.md`.

## 2026-07-26 — AURORA + SPACE WEATHER (Atmospheric-Effects Phase F) — SEEDED by maintainer ask

- **EPIC-AURORA-SPACE-WEATHER — SEEDED (2026-07-26).** Maintainer ask: *"add effects for Northern Lights and being able to trigger solar & magnetic storms. If there is open source data on space weather similar to atmospheric weather we should look into that as well."* Planning home: [`ATMOSPHERIC_EFFECTS_ROADMAP.md`](ATMOSPHERIC_EFFECTS_ROADMAP.md) **Phase F** — the only unbuilt phase in that roadmap (A–E all shipped, Batches 415–423 + 442). **NOT RESEARCHED YET** — no feasibility pass has been run; everything below is scoping to be verified, not findings.

  **This SUPERSEDES the scattered aurora backlog entries** — `FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:1133` and `:1135`, `WEBGPU_MIGRATION_BACKLOG.md:708` and `:722`, `CELESTIAL_ATMOSPHERE_DESIGN.md:65`, plus the archived 2026-03-31 audit rows. All of them scope it as *"procedural shader on the sky dome, 2–3 days, P2"*. **That architecture is wrong for this fork and the estimate is downstream of the error:** on an orbitable globe the aurora is a **volumetric emission shell at 100–400 km** that must stand *above the limb* from space and *overhead* from the ground; a sky-dome texture cannot do both. Do not re-scope from those entries.

  **Rendering shape (to verify).** Line emission with fixed colours — 557.7 nm green (atomic O, ~100–150 km, dominant), 630.0 nm red (atomic O, >200 km, the storm-time crown), 427.8 nm blue/violet (N₂⁺, lower edge). Curtains follow **geomagnetic field lines** (hence the vertical rays); the oval is centred on the **geomagnetic** pole ~11° off the geographic one, so a geographic-latitude oval sits visibly wrong. A **tilted-dipole** approximation is expected to be sufficient for oval placement and curtain direction — full IGRF almost certainly unnecessary for a visual. Sibling of the existing volumetric raymarchers (emissive, additive, unlit, depth-tested against the globe), NOT of the screen-space post-process effects. **Night gate:** reuse the solar-elevation edge the star field already derives (`computeStarDayFade` / the `SkyBrightness` sun term) rather than inventing a second definition of "dark".

  **Storms (the trigger half).** The dominant visual consequence of geomagnetic activity is **equatorward expansion of the oval** — roughly ~67° magnetic latitude when quiet toward ~50° in a severe storm, which is what makes aurora visible from mid-latitudes. So "trigger a storm" is principally **one scalar (Kp or Dst) driving oval latitude + intensity + red-crown fraction**, with optional substorm onset brightening/poleward surge. Design as a storm-state scalar with a manual override plus an optional data source, mirroring the established `effects.auto` master. **A synthetic/manual driver ships FIRST** — the effect must be demonstrable and testable with no network call.

  **Open data — the licensing looks unusually clean, to be confirmed.** The atmospheric-weather ingest already established the pattern (NOAA NWS EDR → normalized scalars, `WEATHER_DATA_INGEST_ROADMAP.md`); the space-weather analogue is **NOAA SWPC**, and as a **US federal product it should be public domain** — the same basis that made the weather ingest and the EGM2008 geoid bundle-safe. Candidates: **Kp planetary index** (the storm scalar, near-real-time JSON); **OVATION Prime auroral probability grid** (SWPC publishes a lat/lon forecast grid — potentially close to a drop-in for the oval, sampled like `weatherTex`); **solar wind** from DSCOVR/ACE (speed, density, and **Bz** — southward Bz is the real storm-onset signal); **GOES X-ray flux** for flare class (the *solar* half of the ask). ⚠ **`Dst` (Kyoto WDC) is NOT a US federal product and does not inherit public-domain status — its licence must be checked before any use.** Kp from SWPC is the safe default. House rule stands: nothing bundled whose terms are not stated in `LICENSE.md`'s Bundled Engine Assets section, and the renderer consumes normalized scalars so live / baked-historical / synthetic drivers are interchangeable.

  **Known trap, inherited from the C12 eclipse work.** A faint additive signal spread over a large band is **invisible to a band-mean statistic** — the star-reveal lane burned three cycles on exactly this (10 stars × ~4 px over 138k band px ≈ 5.7e-5 against a 1e-4 floor: *the floor was right, the statistic was wrong*). Any aurora acceptance gate must use point/structure metrics or an isolated-component difference, never a mean over the band.

  **Sequencing.** Independent of the T/Td/RH weather ingest (different physics, different data spine), so it does **not** queue behind weather Phases 1–2. Its real prerequisite is a trustworthy night-side gate, which the C12 celestial work has now established. **Effort:** unestimated pending a feasibility pass — the volumetric-shell + geomagnetic-oval shape suggests M–L for a first visible slice, materially more than the superseded "2–3 days" entries claim. **Campaign placement:** undecided; NOT C13 (clouds-only). Candidate as an Atmospheric-Effects Phase-F slice or a rider on a celestial campaign, since it shares the night gate and the additive-emission measurement problem with C12.

## 2026-07-06 — NS-LARGE-LAKE-WATER-MASK (BUG 3): flat Great Lakes = provider DATA limitation, NOT a shader gate

- **NS-LARGE-LAKE-WATER-MASK — ✅ ROOT-CAUSED as a DATA limitation (no code fix; honest doc note per Principle 9 + the task off-gate "if a data limitation, no code change beyond an honest doc note").** User report (2026-07-06, split-screen): large inland lakes (Great Lakes, Great Salt Lake) render FLAT with NO animated water-mask wave/specular effect on BOTH backends, while true oceans animate. **Premise is REAL** (lakes ARE flat — confirmed by reading the PNG pair), but the cause is upstream data, not a fixable shader/gate bug. **Empirical root cause** (`probe-large-lake-water.mjs`, queries `terrainProvider.requestTileGeometry(...).waterMask` DIRECTLY at points inside each water body, Cesium World Terrain, level 11): the provider's water mask marks the Great Lakes as **LAND** while marking true ocean as water —
  - Lake Superior (−87.5, 47.6): mask **0** (uniform 1×1 "all-land" tile)
  - Lake Michigan (−87.0, 43.3): mask **0**
  - Lake Huron (−82.4, 44.8): mask **0**
  - Great Salt Lake (−112.5, 41.15): mask **0**
  - N. Atlantic ocean control (−60, 40): mask **255** (uniform "all-water")
  - Nebraska land control (−99.8, 41.5): mask **0**

  The globe FS/WGSL water effect is correctly gated on the mask value (`mask ~0 → coverage 0 → no effect`) and BOTH backends read the identical per-tile mask, so both correctly render lakes flat. **There is NO shader gate excluding lakes and NO backend divergence** — the effect *would* show if the provider marked lakes as water. This matches Cesium World Terrain's known behavior (its water mask derives from a global shoreline/ocean dataset that classifies inland lakes as land). Consistent with the Batch-247 note (line ~171: "world-terrain water-mask wave material … tracked under the collections/material backlog") and PARITY-GLOBE-RIVER-WATER-INTENSITY (line ~93).
  - **What the fix would require (deferred, NOT this task):** a **supplementary client-side lake water-mask source** — rasterize an inland-lake polygon dataset (e.g. Natural Earth `ne_10m_lakes` / HydroLAKES, license-clean) into the per-tile water mask (compositing OR into the provider mask before `createWaterMaskTextureIfNeeded`), wired identically for WebGL (`u_waterMask` upload in `GlobeSurfaceTile.js`) and WebGPU (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.getOrCreateWaterMaskTexture`). This is a substantial feature (dataset ingest + per-tile composite + both-backend byte-identical verification), ~1–2 sessions. **A coverage heuristic was explicitly REJECTED** — any "mark dark/low pixels as water" rule would fake waves on non-water land (rivers, wet fields, dark forest), which the task charter forbids ("Do NOT fake waves on non-water pixels").
  - **Trace:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-large-lake-water.mjs` (retained — STEP (i) samples the provider mask + documents the data result, STEP (ii) captures the Lake Michigan PNG pair). Tree left clean apart from this note + the probe.
  - **✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-10 (C7-LAKE-WATER-MASK — the WaterClassificationProvider Phase-1 seed).** The supplementary lake-mask source described above SHIPPED: `Scene/WaterClassificationProvider.ts` (`LakeWaterClassificationProvider`) OR-composites Natural Earth 1:10m lake polygons (PUBLIC DOMAIN, global + North America supplement; preprocessed by `Tools/build-lake-water-mask.mjs` into the bundled ~900 KiB `Assets/WaterMask/ne10mLakes.bin`) over the provider mask at the single shared upload point (`GlobeSurfaceTile.js` → `createWaterMaskTextureIfNeeded`, Batch 512), expanding the 1-byte all-land fast path to 256×256 only when a lake rasterizes into the tile — both backends consume identical texels by construction. Opt-in `globe.lakeWaterMask`, DEFAULT OFF, byte-identical off (probe off-gate 0.000% on every view/backend); the default-flip is a user decision after visual review. Known limits: Caspian absent (Natural Earth classes it as ocean), ImageBitmap-shaped masks pass through un-augmented, dataset is 1:10m cartography (small lakes coarse; the ~30m public-domain SRTMSWBD raster is the tracked v2 upgrade — research lane R-LAKE-SRTMSWBD). Acceptance probe `probe-lake-water-mask.mjs` (baseline/accept modes, frame-number-pinned wave phase). See FEATURE_INVENTORY §B.1 (WaterClassificationProvider seam).

  diagnostic found: WebGPU renders billboard/label **atlas content vertically flipped** vs WebGL, in
  **ALL scene modes (3D, 2D, CV)** — NOT SCENE2D-specific and NOT globe-related. Visible only on
  asymmetric content: the probe's "TEST" label is upright on WebGL and upside-down/mirrored on WebGPU in

  it. Because CesiumJS labels ARE billboards (glyphs packed into the shared `TextureAtlas`), this is a

  image is affected. Root cause: mismatch between the shared `TextureAtlas` GPU-texture upload
  orientation and the WGSL billboard UV mapping. WebGL `Shaders/BillboardCollectionVS.glsl:141`
  (`textureCoordinates = textureCoordinatesBottomLeft + direction * textureCoordinatesRange`) maps the
  screen-up corner (`direction.y=1`) to atlas **V-max**; `Shaders/WebGPU/Collections/BillboardCollection.wgsl`
  `QUAD_UVS` (lines 289–296) maps the screen-up corner to **V=0.0**. Fix = reconcile the UV mapping
  against the actual atlas upload flipY (`Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUTexture.ts` / `TextureAtlas` path), then
  re-verify across the main + SDF (`BillboardCollectionSDF.wgsl`) + pick (`BillboardCollectionPick.wgsl`)
  variants, all three scene modes, AND an **asymmetric** billboard image (not just the label glyph — a
  UV-only flip must not merely trade the label flip for a billboard flip). Reproducer:
  `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs`. **Effort:** ~1 session (shader + atlas-orientation reconcile +
  cross-variant/cross-mode probe with an asymmetric image added).

## 2026-07-05 — TAKRAM-9: cloud-aware god rays (Batch 581)

- **TAKRAM-9-CLOUD-AWARE-GODRAY** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 581, queue row Q20 of `NEXT_QUEUE_2026-07-04.md`). The WebGPU screen-space god-ray generate pass historically gated the light shaft on scene DEPTH alone (`GodRayGenerate.wgsl`: `isSky = step(far*cutoff, linearDepth)`). Because the procedural cloud pass composites into scene color with **no depth write**, cloud pixels read as "sky" and leaked their bright color into the shaft as if the sun were unobstructed — the whole cloudy foreground blew out to white. This batch feeds the cloud renderer's per-pixel screen-space TRANSMITTANCE into the god-ray pass so dense clouds attenuate the shaft (crepuscular rays that stream through cloud gaps). **Producer** (`WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts` + `ProceduralClouds.wgsl`): a NEW `fragmentCloudMaskMain` entry point re-marches the shell(s) for the current view and emits ONLY the view-ray transmittance `Πᵢ(1-αᵢ)` into a dedicated full-res `r8unorm` target; rendered by a lazily-built mask pipeline (reuses the shipped cloud BGL + shader module) in a pass AFTER the composite pass. Gated behind `setCloudTransmittanceCapture(context, true)` — the shipped single-deck/multi-deck/half-res composite passes are UNTOUCHED, so the default cloud render is byte-identical. `getCloudTransmittanceView` returns the view rendered THIS frame (guarded by `maskRenderedThisFrame` so a culled frame reports null). **Consumer** (`WebGPUGodRayEffect.ts` + `GodRayGenerate.wgsl`/`_f16`): generate BGL gains binding-4 `cloudTransTex`; the per-sample sky contribution is multiplied by `textureSampleLevel(cloudTransTex, stepUV).r`. When cloud-aware is off, the effect binds a 1×1 white `r8unorm` (255 → exactly 1.0) fallback → the multiply is a byte-identical no-op (no uniform/flag change needed). **Wiring** (`WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts`): opt-in via `scene.godRayCloudAware = true` (needs `scene.godRayEnabled` AND `globe.showProceduralClouds`); the per-frame configure requests capture + pushes the mask view, else releases capture + clears the view. Default OFF (flag absent) → capture never enabled, no mask pipeline/texture allocated, white fallback bound → fully byte-identical. **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-cloud-godray.mjs` (NEW) — low oblique horizon view, sun ahead, broken clouds: (1) shafts exist (off→gr diff 80.6), (2) cloud-aware LIVE (gr-noca→gr-ca diff 37.1), (3) cloud-aware DIMS the shaft (mean 0.838→0.693 — clouds block instead of leaking), (4) OFF deterministic (0.0), (5) mask produced ONLY when cloud-aware (ca=true, noca=false), (6) 0 device errors. **Read the PNGs:** gr-noca blows the whole foreground to white; gr-ca shows discrete crepuscular beams streaming through cloud gaps onto now-visible terrain — the intended result. **Off-gate proven empirically:** stashed the 6 source files, rebuilt pristine, captured the god-rays-ON/cloud-aware-OFF frame → byte-identical to the changed build (maxAbsChannel=0, nDiffChannels=0). Standing `probe-cloud-dials` GREEN (cloud path unaffected). tsc clean.

## 2026-06-16 — Track V-C: bright-star catalog starfield (Batch 313)

> **2026-07-26 provenance/data correction:** the shipped-history row below
> predates the catalog audit. Its “public-domain”, “~230”, and
> “vmag ≲ 3.6” phrases are withdrawn. The live table contains 263 factual
> records spanning visual magnitude -1.46 through 5.0. BSC5 is freely
> available, but no public-domain dedication or redistribution licence has
> been located; `C12-09` / DR-02 tracks written clearance and the source
> docblock carries the full rationale.

- **NEW-STARS-BRIGHT-CATALOG** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 313). A real Yale Bright Star Catalog (BSC5, public-domain) starfield that AUGMENTS the static `SkyBox` star cubemap on WebGPU with physically-placed, time-correct HDR stars fed through the existing bloom. **Data** `Scene/BrightStarCatalog.js` — a compact embedded subset of the ~230 brightest naked-eye stars (vmag ≲ 3.6), each `[raJ2000°, decJ2000°, vmag, B−V]`. **Renderer** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUStarFieldRenderer.js` (FeatureRendererKey.STAR_FIELD=51) — uploads the catalog ONCE to a per-instance GPU buffer (direction + Pogson intensity + blackbody RGB + size boost) and draws it as instanced point sprites (6 verts × N stars) into the scene framebuffer with PREMULTIPLIED-ADDITIVE blend so bright stars overflow 1.0 and feed the bloom bright-pass. **Technique** (implemented fresh; credited in `StarField.wgsl` to Pogson + Ballesteros + Takram research notes): magnitude→brightness via the Pogson scale (flux gamma-compressed into a `[LO,HI]` band so the faintest stars stay visible while the brightest overflow → bloom + a magnitude-driven `sizeBoost`); B−V color index → blackbody temperature (Ballesteros 2012) → Planckian-locus RGB (Tanner-Helland fit), renormalized so brightness lives in the Pogson term, not the hue. **TEME/J2000 → fixed:** catalog directions are inertial; the renderer rotates them into the Earth-fixed frame each frame via `Transforms.computeTemeToPseudoFixedMatrix` (the SAME matrix SkyBox uses) baked into a translation-free view-projection, so constellations land at the correct RA/Dec for the scene clock. A camera-altitude-gated daytime fade (smoothstep over solar-altitude-sine) dims the field at ground level when the sun is up but keeps it visible above ~100 km. **Wiring / augment-not-replace:** `SkyBox` owns a backend-agnostic `StarField` (`Scene/StarField.js`, FR-seam, never imports `Renderer/WebGPU/`); `Scene.updateEnvironment` drives `skyBox.starField.update(frameState)` and stores the returned command on `environmentState.starFieldCommand`, which `SceneRenderer.js` injects AFTER `skyBoxCommand`. **Why after:** the cubemap is an alpha-over draw injected after the binned ENVIRONMENT commands; an opaque cubemap would overwrite a binned-only starfield. The renderer pushes a binned copy too (frustum guarantee on sky-only views) AND returns a distinct inject instance; Scene only routes the inject when a `skyBoxCommand` exists (so the catalog draws exactly once — binned-then-wiped + injected when a cubemap is present, binned-only otherwise). **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-stars-catalog.mjs` (NEW) — camera aimed at Sirius's computed Earth-fixed direction for a pinned clock; with the cubemap ON (augment path), starField ON adds 4527 bright pixels vs 0 OFF, maxLum=255 (bright stars saturate → bloom), Sirius lands a 923-px center cluster vs 104 when aimed at a blank patch (RA/Dec correctness), raising `intensity` grows the bright count (Pogson liveness), the SkyBox cubemap hook stays intact, 0 console errors. Read the PNG — Sirius is the big central disc with the winter constellations at correct relative positions and warm/cool stars by B−V. Standing gates green (collections-regression, bloom-parity, logdepth-zfight, collections-far-camera, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check 26/26).
- **NEW-STARS-BRIGHT-CATALOG-WEBGL-FALLBACK** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 324). WebGL now draws the SAME physical bright-star catalog as WebGPU via a dedicated GLSL point-sprite `STAR_FIELD` feature renderer, closing the night-sky divergence between the backends. **Shared math extracted (REUSED, not duplicated):** the B−V→blackbody-RGB conversion (`bvToRgb`), the Pogson-magnitude→HDR-brightness per-instance packing (`buildStarInstanceData`), and the camera-altitude-gated daytime fade (`computeStarDayFade`) moved out of `WebGPUStarFieldRenderer.ts` into a new backend-neutral `Scene/StarFieldMath.ts`; BOTH renderers import them, so the two backends place/color/brighten the IDENTICAL stars from the IDENTICAL `BrightStarCatalog.js` records — only the draw path differs (GLSL vs WGSL). The WebGPU renderer's runtime is byte-for-byte unchanged (the extraction is a pure refactor; its probe still passes A–F). **WebGL renderer** `Renderer/WebGLStarFieldRenderer.js` — builds an instanced `VertexArray` (per-vertex quad corner at attribute 0 + the 4 per-instance star attributes at locations 1–4 with `instanceDivisor=1`, sharing one 32-byte-stride vertex buffer) + `ShaderProgram` (`Shaders/StarFieldVS/FS.glsl`) + a premultiplied-additive (`ONE/ONE` add), depth-test-DISABLED, no-cull `RenderState`; returns one instanced `DrawCommand`. **Shaders** `StarFieldVS.glsl` rotates the inertial catalog direction into the Earth-fixed frame with the `czm_temeToPseudoFixed` automatic uniform (same rotation SkyBox uses), places the star at the far-frustum distance in eye space (`czm_viewRotation` + `czm_entireFrustum.y`) and projects normally so the dead-ahead star isn't far-plane-clipped (WebGL's `[-1,1]` NDC z is prone to that when pinning `clip.z=clip.w`), then offsets the sprite corner in clip space; `StarFieldFS.glsl` is a 1:1 GLSL port of the WGSL radial-falloff fragment (premultiplied output). **Wiring:** registered as the WebGL `STAR_FIELD` FR via a lazy loader in `Renderer/Context.js` (avoids a static Renderer→Scene import cycle; warms up over the first frames like the WebGPU async pipeline); executed by `Scene/EnvironmentRenderer.js` right AFTER the SkyBox cubemap and BEFORE sky-atmosphere/sun/moon, mirroring the WebGPU injection order. **Backend-agnostic gate fix:** `StarField.update` now records `wasBinned` (true only when the FR pushed a binned commandList copy — WebGPU); `Scene.updateEnvironment` drops the returned command only when `wasBinned && !skyBoxCommand` (WebGPU double-draw avoidance), so the WebGL command — which is never binned — always executes, even with the cubemap off. (Previously the cubemap-existence gate silently suppressed WebGL stars.) **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-starfield-webgl-parity.mjs` (NEW) — camera aimed at Sirius for a pinned clock, cubemap OFF so the catalog renders alone: WebGL goes 0→4342 bright star pixels (was an inert no-op), and the WebGL pattern matches WebGPU EXACTLY — bright-block IoU = 1.000, center-box 903=903, 0 console errors on both. Read the PNGs — the WebGL frame is indistinguishable from WebGPU's (same Sirius disc, same constellation positions, same warm/cool stars by B−V). `tsc --noEmit` clean; `gulp build` exit 0; SkyBox (20) + Sun (10) specs green on Edge.
- **C12-29 S6 architecture supersession (2026-07-26):** the two preceding
  shipped-history rows describe the command wiring as it existed in Batches
  313/324. The live architecture now creates one cached command in each
  backend feature renderer and returns it through
  `environmentState.starFieldCommand`, in the shared pre-atmosphere slot.
  WebGPU no longer pushes a second binned copy; Scene no longer scans or
  repairs the command list. Batch 761's injected-environment predicate
  preserves the sky-only frustum guarantee. The same ownership rule now
  applies to the WebGPU sky atmosphere and sun: their feature renderers return
  cached commands and Scene decides whether they are visible and where they
  execute.
  - The old "visible above ~100 km" text is historical. Both star paths now use
    `computeAtmosphericColumnFactor(cameraHeight)`: the original low-altitude
    day fade is restored continuously from 60 to 111 km, then becomes exact
    identity above the scattering shell. `cameraHeight` is ellipsoidal height
    supplied by Scene, not ECEF magnitude minus a hard-coded Earth radius.
  - Star modulation and cloud occlusion are valid only for celestial imagery.
    `CubeMapPanorama.isStarMap` defaults false and `SkyBox` is the explicit
    opt-in, protecting generic and Google Street View panoramas from the
    default-on star law.
  - `Moon.update` now precedes `frameState.skyBrightness`, so the estimator
    consumes current-frame direction/phase even in a one-frame
    request-render-mode clock step. Hidden/absent Moon resets the scalar phase
    contribution instead of leaking a previous frame.
  - WebGPU Sun motion is uniform-only: immutable quad directions back a stable
    vertex buffer, and its bind group/draw command remain cached across clock
    ticks. Only a genuine texture, format, pipeline, or device invalidator
    rebuilds those resources.
  - Probe "same-task capture" means the render and read of the **live GPU
    canvas** are fused. The PNG byte snapshot is synchronous; decoding that
    immutable snapshot is allowed to await. The shared Acorn validator rejects
    unawaited direct/alias captures and floating promise chains, and
    `settleThen` rechecks its completion predicate after the final animation
    frame before taking the snapshot.
- **NEW-STARS-BRIGHT-CATALOG-FULL-DEPTH** (S, optional) — the embedded subset is 263 records through magnitude 5.0; the renderer reads `data.length / STRIDE`, so deepening to mag ~6 (full naked-eye, ~5000 stars) or the whole BSC5 (~9110) needs only appending rows (or loading a rights-reviewed catalog asset). Bloom carries essentially all the perceived quality from the bright few hundred, so this is cosmetic density, not correctness.

## 2026-06-16 — Track V-A1: full-Bruneton atmosphere LUTs (Batch 306)

- **NEW-ATMO-BRUNETON-FULL-LUTS** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 306). Extended `WebGPUAtmosphereLUT` from the transmittance + single-scattering pair to the full Bruneton precomputed set by adding multiple-scattering + irradiance. WGSL (`Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/AtmosphereLUT.wgsl`): two new entry points `computeMultipleScattering` (256×128, same `(cosViewZenith × altitude)` parameterization as inscatter — gathers the single-scattering radiance over a Fibonacci-sphere of directions, phases incoming→view, integrates higher orders along the view ray) and `computeIrradiance` (256×64, `(cosSunZenith × altitude)` — direct sun term `transmittance·max(cosSunZenith,0)` + cosine-weighted hemisphere integral of the inscattered sky). Both read transmittance + single-scatter as SAMPLED inputs via a new `@group(1)` block (their OWN `extParams` uniform copy at g1/b0, so they never touch group 0 → the original two write-only entry points' auto-layout is untouched); both self-bound via `textureDimensions()` (the shared params uniform carries the transmittance height 64, which would clip the 128-row MS LUT). TS (`WebGPUAtmosphereLUT.ts`): allocate `multipleScatter` (256×128) + `irradiance` (256×64) sun targets + `COPY_SRC` on the LUT textures (probe readback); new `dispatchAtmosphereExtendedLUT(host, encoder, device)` builds the group-1 sampler/BGL/bind-group and chains both passes. `WebGPUPerformanceManager` exposes `dispatchAtmosphereExtendedLUT` + `getAtmosphereExtendedLUTViews`. `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js` chains the extended dispatch right after the sun transmittance/inscatter dispatch (gated on `sunOk` + method presence). Credit: Bruneton & Neyret 2008 + Hillaire 2020 + Takram three-geospatial (MIT) in the shader header. **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-atmo-luts.mjs` — MS LUT non-trivial (max 48.3, mean 6.3) and brightens the sky-band ~19× over single-scatter; irradiance positive (max 127.8) and falls off with sun zenith (123→84→82); 0 NaN/neg/validation errors; existing sky still renders (bloom-parity globe pixel unchanged). Standing gates green (collections-regression, bloom-parity, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check).
- **NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING** (M, surfaced Batch 306 per Principle 9) — ✅ **SHIPPED (Batch 367, item 370).** Added a lazy `get computeEngine()` to `WebGPUContext` (mirroring the `renderBundleManager` getter): instantiates `WebGPUComputeEngine` on first access once `_device` exists, wired to the central compute-pipeline cache + async-resource monitor, dropped on device loss (both `onDeviceInvalidated` + the device-invalidated cache-clear chain). The `PerformanceManagerContext.computeEngine?` interface + all `dispatchCompute` call sites already read `this._context.computeEngine`, so every dormant compute path (atmosphere LUT bake, frustum cull, point-cloud sort/LOD, GPU sort keys, Hi-Z, normal-from-depth, polygon SDF) now lights up. **No visible change by design:** `ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT=false` gates the sky FS off the LUT read, so the bake now RUNS but is visually inert (no double-apply with the analytic aerial-perspective path). **Verified:** `probe-compute-engine-wired.mjs` (NEW) — `context.computeEngine` non-null via the production frame path + 0 console errors (the now-running dispatch is clean); baseline-isolated didn't-break: `probe-camera-track` meanDiff **2.005% WITH 370 == 2.005% WITHOUT** (stashed WebGPUContext + rebuilt + re-ran), so the globe/atmosphere is unregressed. **Files:** `WebGPUContext.ts`. (Original analysis retained below.) Consequence: the sky-atmosphere inscatter LUT bake does NOT actually run at runtime today (the `NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE` note's "the bake itself still runs every frame" is stale — it's dormant), and the Batch-306 MS+irradiance dispatch is likewise dormant until this is wired. The shader logic is fully verified via `probe-atmo-luts.mjs` building the pipelines directly on the raw device. **Fix:** instantiate `WebGPUComputeEngine` on `WebGPUContext` (lazy getter `get computeEngine()` mirroring `renderBundleManager`, dropped on device loss), so the existing `dispatchCompute` callers light up. **Impact:** unblocks runtime consumption of ALL precompute LUTs + GPU compute tasks; this would let NEW-ATMO-AERIAL-PERSPECTIVE-POSTPROCESS sample a *runtime-populated* transmittance LUT for its extinction (today it computes extinction analytically — see below — so it does NOT block aerial perspective from shipping, only the LUT-sampled optimization). **Estimated effort:** 1 session (wiring + a compute-dispatch smoke probe that asserts the LUT textures are non-zero through the production path).

Also: the WebGPU sun `fs` lacks `czm_gammaCorrect` (HDR-only — `gammaCorrect.glsl` is `#ifdef HDR`); a no-op in the default non-HDR path, only diverges with `scene.highDynamicRange=true`. Same batch.

- **NEW-WEBGPU-TIMEDYNAMIC-POINTCLOUD-CONTENT-LOAD-ZERO** — ✅ **CLOSED (Q5-TIMEDYNAMIC-POINTCLOUD-ZERO, 2026-07-04).** The headline premise ("loads ZERO content on WebGPU", `boundingSphere` never ready) was **STALE** — already fixed by Batch 465, which (a) removed the `TimeDynamicPointCloud.update` mis-delegation of `this` to the WebGPU point-cloud renderer and (b) added `computeWebGPUReadyState` in `PointCloud.js` so the WebGPU feature-renderer path sets `_ready` + a world-space `boundingSphere` from parsed positions. `probe-timedynamic-pointcloud-load.mjs` confirms WebGPU renders content (39.9k non-black px) with `boundingSphere` ready at **frame 1** (radius 4.063, identical to WebGL). The ONE genuinely-remaining gap was **memory accounting**: `_geometryByteLength` stayed 0 on the WebGPU path (`createResources`, which sums the vertex-buffer sizes, never runs when the feature renderer builds its own instance buffer), so `totalMemoryUsageInBytes === 0` and the memory-based frame eviction (`> maximumMemoryUsage`) never tripped → unbounded frame accumulation over long playback. Fix: `computeWebGPUReadyState` now sums the parsed typed-array byte lengths (positions + colors/normals/batchIds/styleable, mirroring WebGL's per-attribute accounting), giving WebGPU `totalMemoryUsageInBytes === 165000` at frame 1 — **exactly matching WebGL**. WebGL path untouched (`computeWebGPUReadyState` only runs behind the `getFeatureRenderer(POINT_CLOUD)` gate). **Probe:** `probe-timedynamic-pointcloud-load.mjs` (GATE PASS: renders + bs-ready + mem>0 + 0 device errors).

- **NEW-WEBGPU-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-BGL-INCOMPAT** (M, surfaced Batch 373 per Principle 9) — now that `NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING` (Batch 367) lit up the dormant compute paths, the SkyAtmosphere LUT bake actually DISPATCHES at runtime — and it emits a WebGPU validation error every frame it runs: `The current pipeline ([ComputePipeline "perfmgr:atmosphereLUT:computeTransmittance_Pipeline"]) was created with a default layout, and is not compatible with the [BindGroup "AtmosphereLUT_BG_Sun"/"AtmosphereLUT_BG_Moon"] ... that was not created by the pipeline` → an invalid `[CommandEncoder "SkyAtmosphere LUT dispatch"]` → uncaptured GPU error on Queue.Submit. So the `computeTransmittance` (and likely the other AtmosphereLUT entry points') pipeline is created with `layout: "auto"` while its bind group is built from an EXPLICIT `AtmosphereLUT_BGL` — the two layouts must match. **Repro:** any scene that triggers the sky-atmosphere LUT dispatch on `?renderer=webgpu` (seen in `probe-morph-normals.mjs`'s console gate: `fatal=4`). **Fix:** either build the AtmosphereLUT compute pipelines with an EXPLICIT `pipelineLayout` made from `AtmosphereLUT_BGL` (preferred — matches the extended MS/irradiance passes' group-1 pattern), OR build the bind groups from `pipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0)`. Check all `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl` entry points (`computeTransmittance`, `computeInscatter`, and the Batch-306 `computeMultipleScattering`/`computeIrradiance`) — the extended pair already uses an explicit group-1 BGL, so the bug is likely only in the original transmittance/inscatter write-path pipelines. NOTE: `probe-compute-engine-wired.mjs` (Batch 367) reported 0 errors — it likely didn't trigger the sun/moon AtmosphereLUT dispatch path, so this regression slipped through; that probe should be extended to assert the AtmosphereLUT dispatch is validation-clean. **Estimated effort:** 0.5 session. Visually inert today (the LUT is baked but `ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT=false` gates the sky FS off the read — see `NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE`), but the per-frame uncaptured GPU error is real console noise + a latent correctness landmine for when the LUT read is re-enabled.

## 2026-06-16 — Track V-A2: unified aerial-perspective post-process (Batch 311)

- **NEW-ATMO-AERIAL-PERSPECTIVE-POSTPROCESS** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 311). A fullscreen post-process pass that applies ONE depth-correct atmosphere over the whole composited scene (terrain, 3D tiles, glTF models, geometry), unifying the per-tile ground-atmosphere drape — the "post-process lighting for the terrain" Takram-talk headline. **WGSL** (`Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AerialPerspective.wgsl`): per pixel, (1) recover eye-space distance from the renderer-wide LOG depth (`logDepthToEyeDistance`, inlined `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance`); sky pixels (raw depth ≥ `skyCutoff`) pass through untouched so the sky/atmosphere shell shows through; (2) recover the world-space view ray as `inverseViewRotation × normalize(inverseProjection·NDC_at_near)` — the eye-space **direction** rotated to world, NOT a `pFar−pNear` world-position difference (that suffers FP32 catastrophic cancellation at Earth scale → NaN ray → black scene; this was the key bring-up bug); use the **near** plane (clip-z 0) for the inverse-projection unproject because the scene projection is near-finite/far-INFINITE so clip-z 1 maps to w≈0 → NaN; (3) march the camera→fragment segment for analytic single-scatter (Rayleigh + Mie, HG phase vs the sun, parity port of `AtmosphereCommon.glsl::computeScattering`); (4) EXTINCTION = `exp(−(βR·ODr+βM·ODm))` from the *marched* optical depth (NOT a transmittance-LUT ratio: for horizontal/downward rays both endpoints have a near-opaque path-to-TOA so a LUT ratio collapses to a meaningless ~0/0 → black). Compose `sceneColor·T + inscatter`. **Why analytic, not LUT-sampled:** the single-inscatter LUT's Y-up baked-sun parameterization can't represent view–sun azimuth (`ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT=false`, `NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE`) AND the compute engine that bakes the LUTs is dormant (`NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING`) — so the analytic march is both correct AND runtime-functional today. The transmittance LUT view is still bound (group 0 binding 2, white 1×1 placeholder until populated) + `sampleTransmittance` kept for the V-A3 sun-radiance/derived-lighting follow-on. **TS** (`WebGPUAerialPerspectiveEffect.ts`, `PostProcessEffect`): output texture + pipeline + 56-float uniform (camera WC, sun WC, βR/βM + scale heights, mie-g/near/far/thickness, intensity/inscatterScale/skyCutoff, inverseProjection, inverseView); `setFrameData` packs per-frame, `setTransmittanceView` pushes the LUT. Runs FIRST in the post-process `execute()` chain (before AO/bloom/tonemap) so the haze participates in bloom + tonemap, mirroring how WebGL applies the ground atmosphere in the globe FS before post-process. Wired through `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline` (add/getter/hasActiveStages/execute/resize/destroy/recreate-reset) + `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.configure` (lazy-init + per-frame `updateAerialPerspectiveFrameData` from `uniformState`). **Composition decision (DOCUMENTED):** the post-process is the SINGLE owner of distance haze when active; the in-globe ground-atmosphere + fog drape is gated OFF (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB` + `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB` read the new `frameState.aerialPerspective` flag Scene publishes, same dormant-gate pattern as `taaEnabled`) so the two don't double-apply. Opt-in via `scene.aerialPerspective = true` (default OFF → full backwards compat; WebGL ignores it). **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-aerial-perspective.mjs` — low oblique Rockies view; aerial perspective ON vs OFF: globe still renders (493910 non-black px), far band brightens +0.26 AND desaturates −0.028 (the depth-correct haze signature), no double-darkening (mean 0.44 ≥ 0.6×OFF), 0 console errors. Read the PNGs — distant terrain washes into a soft blue-grey haze toward the horizon while the foreground keeps detail, resembling the Takram reference. Standing gates green (collections-regression, far-camera, bloom-parity, logdepth-zfight, csm-soft-shadow, csm-cast-dispatch, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check).
- **NEW-ATMO-AERIAL-PERSPECTIVE-NEARFIELD-TUNE** (S, surfaced Batch 311 per Principle 9) — the default look (intensity 1, inscatterScale 1, `atmosphereLightIntensity` 50 from the SKY shell) hazes the near foreground a touch heavily (the bright sky-intensity drives the inscatter); a future pass could (a) calibrate the inscatter against the GROUND-atmosphere intensity (~10) + the WebGL `1−exp(−fExposure·x)` tonemap for a softer near-field, and (b) make `scene.aerialPerspectiveConfig.{intensity,inscatterScale}` mutable at runtime (today the config is read only at lazy-init; `setIntensity`/`setInscatterScale` exist on the effect but no scene-side sync wires them per-frame). Not blocking — the depth-correct fade is already visually correct. **Estimated effort:** 0.5 session + a WebGL-vs-WebGPU numeric ground-haze parity probe. (At HIGH sun the near foreground + a near surface MODEL read noticeably blue — the daytime Rayleigh inscatter looking up through the full atmosphere column dominates the near field; this is the near-field-tune item, NOT a V-A3 derived-lighting issue, whose derived sun is correctly near-white at noon — see V-A3 below.)

## 2026-06-16 — Track V-A3: atmosphere-derived sun + sky lighting + mixed mask (Batch 312)

- **NEW-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 312). Derives the directional SUN light (colour + intensity) and a SKY-IRRADIANCE ambient from the atmosphere so discrete glTF MODELS are lit consistently with the V-A2 aerial-perspective haze + the sky shell — the Takram-talk "light-source lighting for the ISS" half of the mixed-lighting pattern (terrain keeps the V-A2 post-process Lambertian; models use light-source PBR, both driven by ONE coherent atmosphere). **New module** `Scene/AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js` (backend-neutral, pure math): a short CPU Beer-Lambert sun-ray optical-depth march (same Rayleigh + Mie coefficients/scale-heights `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl` bakes + V-A2's `AP_*` use) → `exp(−(βR·ODr+βM·ODm))` gives the sun's transmitted colour (near-white at the zenith; blue+green extinguish first toward the horizon → warm sunset hue) + a horizon-falloff intensity (dims to ~0 as the sun sets). The sun ZENITH is measured against the **local up at the viewed site** (camera position direction), NOT the pole axis — passing a fixed +Z up made the colour ~constant over a day (the key bring-up bug; fixed by threading `localUpWC`). Plus a desaturated cool sky-irradiance ambient (Rayleigh tint blended 75% toward neutral grey, day/night-aware, ~0.2 magnitude at midday to match the historical flat ambient floor). **Why analytic, not LUT-sampled:** mirrors the V-A2 decision exactly — the Bruneton transmittance/irradiance LUTs (Batch 306) exist but the compute engine that bakes them is dormant (`NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING`), so the analytic CPU path is both physically correct AND runtime-functional today; this module is the documented seam to swap to direct transmittance(sun)+irradiance(sky) LUT reads when the compute engine lands (public shape — colour+intensity+ambient — stays identical). **Wiring** (`Scene.js::updateFrameState`, gated on `aerialPerspective===true && isWebGPU && scene.light instanceof SunLight`): re-derives into a PRIVATE `_atmosphereDerivedLight` (SunLight) each frame and swaps it into `frameState.light` ONLY while aerial perspective is on — `scene.light` is never mutated (turning the flag off restores it untouched); publishes the ambient on the new `frameState.atmosphereSkyIrradiance`. Models pick up the sun for free (the WebGPU model renderer already reads `frameState.light.color`/`.intensity`); `WebGPUModelRenderer.js` reads `frameState.atmosphereSkyIrradiance` for its `ambientColor` (falls back to the historical neutral 0.2 floor when the flag is off / on WebGL). Sun direction is the previous frame's `uniformState.sunDirectionWC` (one frame stale — visually indistinguishable, same trick as `computeSkyBrightness`). **Mixed mask / no double-lighting:** the V-A2 post-process applies extinction+inscatter (NOT Lambertian shading — it has no normal buffer) over the whole scene incl. model pixels, so a lit model also correctly hazes with distance — that is real aerial perspective, not double-LIGHTING. **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-atmo-lighting.mjs` (NEW) — a 4000×-scaled CesiumMilkTruck on the globe near Denver, two sun states with aerial perspective ON: derived sun HIGH=`rgb 1.00,0.98,0.95 I=1.97` (near-white, full) vs LOW=`rgb 1.00,0.84,0.68 I=1.20` (warm, dimmed); model lit pixels shift warm (R/B 0.64→1.27) AND the model+sunlit terrain are BOTH warm at low sun (model R/B 1.27, globe R/B 1.70 — consistently lit); ON warmer than OFF (derived-light liveness); WebGL renders the scene (it ignores the flag); 0 console errors. Read the PNGs — the low-sun frame is a coherent golden sunset bathing model + terrain together (the headline result), the high-sun frame's blue is the V-A2 daytime inscatter (NEARFIELD-TUNE), not the derived sun. Standing gates green (collections-regression, pickmodel-instanced, model-ibl, bloom-parity, logdepth-zfight, csm-soft-shadow, csm-cast-dispatch, collections-far-camera, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check 26/26).
- **NEW-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING-LUT-CONSUMPTION** (S, surfaced Batch 312 per Principle 9) — when `NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING` lands and the Bruneton LUTs bake at runtime, swap the analytic CPU terms in `AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js` for direct LUT reads: the sun colour from the TRANSMITTANCE LUT (altitude × cosSunZenith) and the sky ambient from the IRRADIANCE LUT — more accurate (multiple-scattering-aware) and shareable with a GPU-side path. The module's public shape already matches; this is a body swap behind the same signature. **Estimated effort:** 0.5 session (after the compute engine is wired) + extend `probe-atmo-lighting.mjs` to assert the analytic vs LUT terms agree within tolerance.
  - **BLOCKED — premise reassessed (C4-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING-LUT, 2026-07-04).** The gate `NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING` (Batch 367) and the `NEW-WEBGPU-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-BGL-INCOMPAT` fix (Batch 396) are both in — the transmittance/irradiance LUTs now bake at runtime as GPU textures. **But the "body swap behind the same signature" is architecturally impossible as written:** `computeAtmosphereDerivedLighting` is a *synchronous per-frame CPU function* called in `Scene.js::updateFrameState` whose result is written straight into `frameState.light` (a `SunLight` color+intensity) for the CURRENT frame. The LUTs are **GPU-only** — `WebGPUAtmosphereLUT` exposes only `GPUTexture`/`GPUTextureView` (no `mapAsync`/readback, no CPU mirror; confirmed no Scene-side CPU consumer of `transmittanceView`/`irradianceView` exists). A CPU "LUT read" therefore requires either (a) an async GPU→CPU `mapAsync` readback each frame — a pipeline stall + inherently ≥1 frame stale + not same-signature (must go async), or (b) relocating the derived-lighting computation into a GPU pass where the model PBR shader samples the transmittance LUT by sun-zenith — a substantial `WebGPUModelRenderer`/`ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` change, NOT a same-signature swap of `AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js`. Additionally there is **no CPU correctness gap to close today:** the analytic path already evaluates the exact Bruneton *single-scatter* Rayleigh+Mie transmittance the LUT stores; the only value-add (multiple-scattering-aware irradiance) is only realizable on the GPU-side path (option b). **Re-scoped:** this is NOT an S body-swap. Reclassify as an M GPU-side task = "model PBR samples the atmosphere transmittance/irradiance LUTs directly (sun radiance + MS ambient), retiring the CPU analytic derived-light" — dependent on the model renderer, not on `AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js`. No runtime change landed for C4-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING-LUT; tree left clean. **⏸ PARKED (formally, 2026-07-09 Campaign-7 batch 0):** the re-scoped M GPU-side task (model PBR samples the transmittance/irradiance LUTs directly, retiring the CPU analytic derived-light) is held until `C7-DPH47-ATMOSPHERE-RESOLVER` (queue #12, DP-H47-ATMOSPHERE-RESOLVER-INCREMENT) lands and clarifies the atmosphere-uniform seam the model consumer would read through. Not a standalone Campaign-7 queue item; blocked on that resolver, not deferred-forever. **UPDATE 2026-07-11:** the seam now EXISTS — `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAtmosphereUniforms.ts` (`resolveAtmosphereScattering` / `resolveDynamicLighting`), landed by C7-DPH47-ATMO-RESOLVER (see DP-H47 below). The model consumer (`WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapManager.ts`) now reads its scattering params through that seam, so the re-scoped GPU-side derived-light task can pick it up as the canonical read point.
