- **NEW-CODEMOD-DROPPED-TERRAIN-GETTERS** — ✅ RESOLVED (Batch 256, FQ-3). The Batch-243 `@memberof`-stripping codemod (point 4 of NEW-CI-BUILDTS-GREEN above) didn't just remove redundant `@memberof` lines — in `Cesium3DTilesTerrainData.js` (commit `5230b95e8a`) it **deleted the entire `get credits()` and `get waterMask()` getters** along with their `@memberof`-tagged doc-blocks, while the constructor kept populating `this._credits` / `this._waterMask`. Real runtime correctness bug (not a test artifact): `GlobeSurfaceTile.js:660/:905` read `.waterMask` (→ undefined → `createWaterMaskTextureIfNeeded` never runs → ocean/water rendering breaks for quantized-mesh-as-3D-Tiles terrain); `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1034-1035` read `.credits` (→ undefined → per-tile terrain attribution silently dropped, a legal-attribution concern). Isolated to this one file — Heightmap/QuantizedMesh/GoogleEarthEnterprise terrain-data all kept their getters. **Fix:** restored both ES6 getters at the end of the primary class body in the cleaned style (no `@memberof`, `@readonly`); added a regression-guard spec (`exposes credits and waterMask as prototype getters`) asserting both prototype descriptors have a `get` fn, so a future codemod can't silently drop them again. Verified by `probe-terraindata-getters.mjs` (Edge, built bundle: both getters present & round-trip, matching HeightmapTerrainData) + `gulp test --includeName Core/Cesium3DTilesTerrainData` 35/35. See WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG Batch 256. **Lesson:** a codemod that removes doc-tag lines can swallow the adjacent code member if the member shares the doc-block — audit codemod diffs for dropped getters/setters, not just dropped comments.

## 2026-06-11 — Dual-axis Ultra-Review findings (49 new IDs)

Source of record: [audits/2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW.md](audits/2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW.md) (full report) + `audits/2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW_findings.json` (all 195 confirmed-real findings with per-finding verdicts). Produced by the `webgpu-ultra-review` workflow (53 agents, adversarial-verified). Axis A = WebGPU vs our-WebGL; Axis B = our-WebGL vs upstream fork drift. The 2 CRITICALs were orchestrator-spot-checked against live code (both CONFIRMED REAL); medium/low await per-item check at fix time.

### CRITICAL (2 — verified)

- **NEW-PICKDEPTH-CAPABILITY-READBACK** (A) — ✅ PARTIALLY SHIPPED (Batch 221). Added `GraphicsContext.supportsSynchronousReadback` capability getter (WebGL true / WebGPU false) and switched the two `defined(context.readPixels)` backend-proxy checks (`PickDepth.update`/`getDepth`, `InstancingPipelineStage`) to it — `readPixels` is a required abstract method both backends implement, so `defined()` was always true and wrongly took the WebGL branch. This fixes `PickDepth` to take the async path + the **`InstancingPipelineStage` typed-array drop** for WebGPU instanced models, and removes the wrongly-allocated WebGL pick framebuffer on WebGPU. ~~**Remaining (see NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-DEPTH-RECONSTRUCTION below):** the depth VALUE reconstruction is still wrong on WebGPU, so `pickPosition` returns undefined (safe) rather than a position.~~ Layer 3 (the reconstruction) ✅ SHIPPED Batch 252 — see NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-DEPTH-RECONSTRUCTION below. **FULLY RESOLVED.** NOTE the review under-scoped this as "one getter" — it was a 3-layer fix (capability getter → async architecture → log-depth reconstruction).
- **NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-DEPTH-RECONSTRUCTION** (A, HIGH — split from the above, Batch 221) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 252). `pickPosition`/`pickPositionWorldCoordinates`/camera-zoom-to-cursor return REAL world positions on WebGPU (was: garbage antipode at ~85,000 km, then SAFE undefined since Batch 221). The fix exploits the renderer-wide log-depth landing (Batch 251): the shared packed `globeDepth.globeDepthTexture` is now known fork-wide to carry LOG depth encoded against the FULL camera frustum, so `Picking.pickPositionWorldCoordinates` skips the per-slice `unprojectDepth` loop on contexts without sync readback and reconstructs ONCE with the untouched camera-frustum clone (gated on new capability getter `GraphicsContext.pickDepthFullFrustumLogEncode` — WebGPU mirrors `_logDepthWriteEnabled`, so the kill switch auto-restores the SAFE undefined state). The sync bridge: `PickDepth.getDepth` arms `_readDepthAsync` (now with the missing top-left y-flip for `copyTextureToBuffer` + 3-channel unpack matching the WGSL pack) and returns the one-frame-stale `_lastDepthValue` cache, validity-bounded by ±4 px and ≤4 RENDERED frames (update-count clock, so requestRenderMode keeps the cache valid) — number|undefined, never a Promise (consumers are all synchronous). `SceneTransforms.drawingBufferToWorldCoordinates` now feeds window depth straight through as NDC z when `Matrix4._depthRangeType === "webgpu"` ([0,1] clip range — `2d-1` broke the w reconstruction). Bonus both-backend fix: `SSCCInputHelpers.handleZoom` degenerate-axis guard (bit-identical center/target picks → `cross = 0` exactly while `dot < 1.0` → `Quaternion.fromAxisAngle` NaN throw). Evidence: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pickposition-webgpu.mjs` rewritten from SAFE-state assert to parity assert — WebGL vs WebGPU dLon/dLat = 0.00000°, dH = 4.1 m (≤100 m tol), cold-cache frame 0 undefined → converges frame 1 (≤3 tol), wheel-zoom-to-cursor descends 2,000,000 m → 3,411 m on target with 0 console errors; gates probe-collections-regression / probe-orbital-catalog / sandcastle-smoke all PASS. Remaining interlocking siblings (NOT covered): NEW-PICK-RAY-ASYNC (offscreen ray-pick PickDepth instances never receive `update()` on WebGPU — `getDepth` still returns undefined there) / NEW-PICK-METADATA-READBACK (separate readback architecture). **RECONCILIATION (Batch 257, 2026-06-13):** the "FULLY RESOLVED" claim above was scoped to the GLOBE-surface depth path and did NOT cover picking over an OPAQUE Model/Primitive — that surface returned the globe behind/below the model because scene depth was never re-packed into `globeDepthTexture` after the OPAQUE pass (only after globe + 3D-tiles). Fixed as **DP-H45** (see the Data-pipeline pillar entry below) by adding a post-OPAQUE `executeUpdateDepth` re-pack in `WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts`. Probe: `probe-pickposition-model-webgpu.mjs`. So the Batch-252 reconstruction was correct depth *math* on the globe but read a *stale* (pre-opaque) packed depth over models — the DP-H45 fix completes the opaque-surface coverage.
- **NEW-OIT-COMPOSITE-FORMAT** (A) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 222). `WebGPUOIT._createCompositePipeline` now takes the target format (was hardcoded `rgba8unorm`), and `executeComposite` rebuilds the composite pipeline on demand when `targetFormat` (the real `context._sceneColorFormat`: `bgra8unorm` default / `rgba16float` HDR) differs from the pipeline's `_compositeFormat`. The composite pipeline's color-target format now matches the attachment by construction, so the MRT-OIT composite can no longer fail WebGPU's format-match validation. Verified no-regression on a translucent OIT scene (0 console/validation errors); full positive verification of the MRT-OIT path needs a Gaussian-splat/forced-OIT scene (that path is fallback-only).
- **NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY** (A, A13 from the 2026-06-11 ULTRA_REVIEW) — ⚠️ NEARLY CLOSED (Batch 303). The capability-getter-per-feature convention (CLAUDE.md §2: Scene rendering logic branches on `context.supportsX`, never `isWebGPU`/`rendererType`) is the canonical replacement for backend branches; the 2026-05-02 audit migrated the 15-branch / 11-file backlog the 2026-04-30 audit found. Batch 303 swept Scene + non-renderer code for residuals: migrated the one branch that re-appeared after the audit — `ComputeInstanceCollection.js:542` `!context.isWebGPU` → `!context.supportsComputeShaders` (the CPU-fallback gate; the getter is the precise capability — a future WebGL compute extension flips it and skips the fallback automatically). **Remaining residuals are intentionally NOT migrated:** (1) `ViewportQuad.js:144` `if (context.isWebGPU)` — divides on shader-SOURCE FORMAT (WGSL `ShaderSource` vs GLSL) + uniform-map shape, which a capability getter can't express; it is BLOCKED on the Materials API per-backend shader-source virtual method (a separate workstream — `Material` must return per-backend sources). Surfaced per Principle 9 as the concrete next step for a true fix. (2) `isWebGPUDrawCommand` checks (`Scene.js:3038`, `:5030`) are a COMMAND property, not a context branch (the 2026-04-30 audit itself classified these as non-violations). (3) Debug/external queries (`CesiumDebug`, `SceneDebug` label, `Picking.js` pragma-wrapped one-time warning, the `getDebugSnapshot` label) are legitimate per CLAUDE.md §2 ("external/extension code CAN query context type"). (4) Renderer-layer construction dispatch (`Texture3D.js:87` returns a `WebGPUTexture3D`; `ContextFactory`/`ContextRegistry`/worker host pick the backend) is the resource/factory layer that is PERMITTED to know the backend. Verified: `grep` of `Source/Scene` + non-renderer code shows no remaining `isWebGPU`/`rendererType===` branch in rendering logic except the ViewportQuad blocker; `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; collections-regression green.
- **NEW-MATERIAL-PER-BACKEND-SHADER-SOURCE** (A, surfaced Batch 303 per Principle 9 — the blocker behind the last `NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY` residual) — `ViewportQuad.js:144` (and any future `Material`-driven primitive on WebGPU) still branches on `context.isWebGPU` to pick between a WGSL `ShaderSource` + Float32Array uniform map and a GLSL `ShaderSource` + the material's `_uniforms` map. This CANNOT be expressed as a capability getter because the divergence is in the shader-SOURCE artifact itself, not a runtime capability. The clean fix: give `Material` a per-backend shader-source virtual method (e.g. `material.getShaderSource(context)` / `material.getUniformMap(context)`) so the caller is backend-agnostic and the WGSL/GLSL selection lives inside the material abstraction (mirrors how `GraphicsContext.createViewportQuadCommand` already virtualizes command creation). Until this lands, `ViewportQuad`'s single `isWebGPU` branch is the sanctioned exception. **Estimated effort:** 1 session (Material API surface + the ~3 built-in material shader pairs that have WGSL twins).

### HIGH — Axis A (WebGPU vs WebGL)

- **NEW-PICK-RAY-ASYNC** — ✅ sampleHeight/clampToHeight SHIPPED (Batch 284); pickFromRay (arbitrary ray) explicitly scoped out. Ray picks used the offscreen-render sync end()→stale-depth path on WebGPU. **History:** Batch 254 (FQ-5) landed only the honesty half — a `oneTimeWarning("WebGPU.rayPick.unsupported", …)` while all three still returned undefined. **Batch 284 makes the high-value half WORK:** `Scene.sampleHeight`/`Scene.clampToHeight` on WebGPU no longer route through the offscreen ray render (whose PickDepth instances never receive `update()`, and whose target depth is LOG-encoded against the MAIN camera, not the offscreen one). Instead `Picking._reconstructHeightSurfaceWebGPU` reuses the main scene's already-rendered depth: project the cartographic/cartesian target into the live view via `SceneTransforms.worldToWindowCoordinates`, reject off-screen positions, then read the surface beneath that pixel via `Picking.pickPositionWorldCoordinates` (the proven Batch-252 full-frustum log reconstruction). Same one-frame-stale sync-cache contract (cold query → undefined + arms readback → converges 1-2 frames). sampleHeight returns the reconstructed surface's height; clampToHeight returns the surface Cartesian3. Limitation: resolves only for positions currently visible in the view, and the reconstructed point lies on the CAMERA ray through the pixel (not the geodetic-normal ray) — near-nadir views match within a few metres, oblique views drift more. **pickFromRay over an ARBITRARY ray stays scoped out** (the offscreen object readback still works → hit object, but `position` is undefined): it now emits `oneTimeWarning("WebGPU.pickFromRay.noPosition", …)` instead of the old shared rayPick warning, and does NOT throw. Building arbitrary-ray async position would need an offscreen GlobeDepth pack + per-view async readback — a separate multi-day item; defer until a consumer needs it. Evidence: `probe-pick-ray-async.mjs` (new, canonical gate) — WebGPU sampleHeight cold→converge frame 1, dH 3.5 m vs WebGL, clampToHeight at exact (-75,40), pickFromRay undefined+warning no-throw, 0 errors; `probe-sampleheight-webgpu.mjs` rewritten from the SAFE-undefined assertion to the working-parity assertion; pickposition / model-pickposition / collections-regression / sandcastle-smoke all green.
- **NEW-PICK-METADATA-READBACK** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 285). `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel` (consumed by `Picking.pickMetadata` + `Picking.pickVoxelCoordinate`) returned `_lastReadPixels.slice(...)` — the pixel from the most recent REGULAR `scene.pick()` COLOR pass, a STALE pixel from a DIFFERENT pass — and had no re-entrancy guard, so a rapid re-pick could read a half-written staging buffer. **Fix (mirrors PickDepth.getDepth's async contract):** `readCenterPixel` now arms its OWN 1x1 `copyTextureToBuffer` readback of the current center pixel of `_colorTexture` (fresh per-readback staging buffer, destroyed after unmap, never colliding with the color-path `_stagingBuffer`), guarded by a new `_centerReadbackInFlight` flag so an in-flight readback isn't re-read, and returns a one-frame-stale cache keyed to (center coord ±2 px + a `_updateCount` frame stamp advanced once per `begin()`, ≤4 picks stale). A cold query returns `[0,0,0,0]` (caller decodes "no metadata / no voxel") and arms the readback; a re-pick at the same spot 1-2 frames later returns the correct value. `bgra8unorm` byte order is normalized to `[R,G,B,A]` so the decoders see the same layout WebGL's `readPixels` produces. **`Picking.js` reorder:** `pickMetadata` + `pickVoxelCoordinate` now call `context.endFrame()` BEFORE `readCenterPixel` so the metadata/voxel render encoder is submitted ahead of the readback copy (the submission-order hazard documented in `_pickAsyncWithMode`); no-op on WebGL (endFrame only unbinds the default FBO; the pick FBO content persists and readCenterPixel re-binds it). **Bonus fix found during bring-up:** the WebGPU Voxel COLOR pipeline (`WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts`) was missing the `multisample.count = context._msaaSamples` bake every other scene-FB renderer applies, so on any MSAA scene (default msaaSamples=4) WebGPU dropped every voxel color draw with "Attachment state of [Voxel color pipeline] is not compatible with [Scene Framebuffer Render Pass]" — added the bake + cache-invalidation on sample-count change (pick/velocity pipelines stay single-sample). **Verify:** `probe-pick-metadata.mjs` — drives `readCenterPixel` over a known-pickable opaque Box's pick FBO: WebGPU converges to the same non-zero pick color `[1,0,0,0]` WebGL reads synchronously (proving current-pass read, not stale), the `_centerReadbackInFlight` guard exists + clears after each readback, 0 validation/console errors across 20 rapid re-reads; WebGPU Voxel Pick sandcastle loads with 0 errors (was throwing the attachment-state validation error). **Asset gaps (documented, not papered over):** (1) the WebGPU VoxelRenderer is a SCAFFOLDED placeholder ray-marcher (FEATURE_INVENTORY §B — `VoxelPrimitive.update` returns early, no real voxel data / traversal), so `scene.pickVoxel` can't yet reach `pickVoxelCoordinate` on WebGPU — the LIVE voxel-coordinate parity check is blocked by that deferred functionality (`C-R9-VOXEL-CELL-PICK`), NOT by this readback fix; (2) no zero-dependency local `EXT_structural_metadata` asset exists (all metadata gallery demos use ion tiles), so `pickMetadata`'s full decode path is covered by the shared-readback Box assertion plus the documented manual-gap note. gates: collections-regression / pick-basic / pickposition-webgpu / compute-instance-pick / pickmodel-instanced / logdepth-zfight / sandcastle-smoke all PASS.
- **NEW-TONEMAPPER-STRING-MAP** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 223). `mapTonemapType` read non-existent `_tonemapping.type`/`_tonemappingType` and switched on NUMBERS, so it always returned the default (PBR_NEUTRAL) — `scene.postProcessStages.tonemapper` was a silent no-op. Fixed to read `collection._tonemapper` (the real field) and switch on the STRING `Tonemapper` enum. Verified end-to-end: each string maps to the correct WebGPU `TonemapMode` (REINHARD→0, ACES→1, FILMIC→2, MODIFIED_REINHARD→3, PBR_NEUTRAL→4) which matches the `Tonemapping.wgsl` operator selection.
- **NEW-POSTPROCESS-HDR-INTERMEDIATES** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 225). The four built-in effects (`addBloom`/`addAmbientOcclusion`/`addDepthOfField`/`addGodRay`) passed `canvasFormat` to the effects' `initialize`, so in HDR they allocated 8-bit (bgra8unorm) intermediates that clamped highlights before tonemap. Fixed to pass `this._intermediateFormat || canvasFormat` (rgba16float in HDR, == canvasFormat in SDR → no-op for the common path). Also reset the built-in effects in `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.initialize()` on any recreate (HDR toggle / resize) — they were created once (`if (this._bloomEffect) return`), so an HDR toggle previously left them holding their first-creation 8-bit/wrong-size textures. Verified: SDR + HDR bloom both render with 0 validation errors (probe).
- **NEW-BLOOM-UNIFORM-PARITY** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 240). Bloom mis-mapped WebGL brightness/contrast onto a luminance threshold (brightness default -0.3 fed as threshold → negative threshold passed EVERYTHING; default bloom bloomed 100% of the frame, measured 1842x WebGL's fraction). Fixed: `BrightPass.wgsl` rewritten as a 1:1 ContrastBias.glsl port (HSB brightness shift via czm_RGBToHSB/czm_HSBToRGB WGSL ports + contrast curve, clamped for HDR intermediates); all six uniforms (contrast/brightness/glowOnly/delta/sigma/stepSize) mapped through the configure path with a full dirty check; `updateConfig` now also rewrites the blur UBOs (delta/sigma/stepSize were init-baked); user stepSize scaled 0.5x for the half-res blur chain (one blur texel = 2 full-res px) so the screen-space footprint matches WebGL; composite intensity default 0.5 → 1.0 (WebGL's composite is plain `bloom + color`); removed the earlier-running FR-sync cache refresh that could mask the configure-pass dirty check. Verified (`probe-bloom-parity.mjs`): default-uniform bloomed-pixel fraction webgl 0.160% vs webgpu 0.161% (ratio 1.01x), glowOnly + brightness changes respond, 0 errors. **Divergences observed while stabilizing the probe (separate items):** WebGPU ground-level daytime sky-atmosphere far brighter than WebGL; WebGPU sun primitive absent at a ground-level 45°-elevation view; no-imagery globe baseColor darker on WebGPU + water-wave material missing.
- **NEW-GROUND-VIEW-ENV-DIVERGENCES** — ✅ SHIPPED Batch 247. Three cross-backend environment divergences at a deterministic ground-level view, all root-caused and fixed; verified by `probe-ground-view-env.mjs` (webgl-vs-webgpu, same scene, numeric). **(3) no-imagery globe baseColor** — NOT an sRGB issue: `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` hardcoded `vec3(0.04,0.04,0.06)` (rgb 10,10,15) as the first-pass base instead of consuming `globe.baseColor`. Fix: wired WebGL's `u_initialColor` through a new `TileUniforms.initialColor` vec4 tail (`TILE_UNIFORM_FLOATS` 476→480, `INITIAL_COLOR_OFFSET` 476; packer reads `tileProvider.baseColor` first-pass / zero subsequent). Now exact rgb(31,38,51) = WebGL. **(2) sun disk missing** — the WebGPU sun command was pushed onto `frameState.commandList` (frustum-binned, executes BEFORE the env-injected skyAtmosphere DUPLICATE), so the alpha-over atmosphere shell (alpha≈1 at ground) erased the disk. Fix: Sun.js adopts the dual-path convention (push for frustum existence AND return for `environmentState.sunDrawCommand`) + SceneRenderer.js env-injection now dedupes against already-binned commands. Disk renders (atmoOn bright 0→1051 px) with the atmosphere-off control intact. **(1) over-bright ground sky** — three compounding non-parity bugs in the WebGPU sky path: (a) the inscatter-LUT fast path (`useLut`) bakes the world-space sun in a synthetic Y-up frame with no view-sun azimuth axis → frame-filling daytime blue; gated OFF (`ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT=false`; bake retained for the globe fog drape, see NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE); (b) the scattering shell used `innerRadius=maxRadius`, `outerRadius=×1.025` instead of WebGL's `(|cam|-eyeHeight)-radiusAdjust` + `+111e3` — re-ported exactly (the missing ~5 km radiusAdjust over-weighted the Rayleigh integrand ~1.7×); (c) the 64-step uniform march was MORE converged than WebGL's coarse 16/4 adaptive quadrature, so even with matching coefficients the sky read ~1.5× bright — `computeScattering` is now a 1:1 port of `czm_computeScattering` (adaptive `w_inside_atmosphere`/`w_stop_gt_lprl` steps + stride). Also switched the per-instance `atmosphere{Rayleigh,Mie}Coefficient/ScaleHeight/Anisotropy` reads (module constants had silently diverged from WebGL defaults). Result: ground-sky luminance ratio webgpu/webgl **1.73x → 0.99x**, value **1.46x → 0.99x**. No high-altitude regression (orbit limb halo unchanged vs HEAD; bloom-parity + orbital-catalog + globe-bindgroup-cache + ground-atmosphere + sandcastle-smoke all green). **Note:** the world-terrain water-mask wave material on WebGL-only is a separate item — that's `showWaterEffect`/ocean-wave material parity, tracked under the collections/material backlog, not closed here. Reproducer/evidence: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-ground-view-env.mjs` + `output/ground-view-env/*.png`.
- **NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE** (M, surfaced Batch 247 per Principle 9) — ✅ **KEYSTONE SHIPPED (Batch 428, A-LUT-REPARAM).** Rather than re-parameterize the EXISTING inscatter LUT in place (which the globe/voxel/splat/point-cloud + primitive fog-drape paths sample directly via `sampleAtmosphereFogLut` and are tuned against its `(cosViewZenith × altitude)` mapping — re-paramming it would break their output), a NEW sun-relative **sky-view LUT** (Hillaire 2020) was added alongside, baked by `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl::computeSkyView`. **Parameterization:** 2D `rgba16float` 256×128 texture; U = relative view↔sun azimuth `[0,π]→[0,1]` (sky mirror-symmetric about the sun meridian → half-plane covers all azimuths), V = view-zenith with the Hillaire non-linear horizon warp `V = 0.5 + 0.5·sign(l)·sqrt(|l|)` (resolves the horizon band). Sun zenith is passed observer-relative (`dot(sunDir, normalize(cameraWC))`) in the params `_pad2`→`sunCosZenith` slot — the world-sun `.y` is NOT the observer's sun elevation at arbitrary lat/lon, which was the dominant brightness bug during bring-up. The bake reuses the existing transmittance LUT + Rayleigh/Mie/ozone constants (only the table's domain mapping is new) and rides the existing group-1 extended bind group (added binding 6); dispatched chained after `computeInscatter` on every sun-direction change. **Opt-in:** `skyAtmosphere.useScatteringLut` (default `false`), threaded → `u.debug.z`; flag-off keeps the inline `czm_computeScattering` march. **Parity:** flag-off is **byte-identical** to pre-change (probe `probe-sky-view-lut.mjs off` stash-baseline diff = **0.0000% mismatch, maxDelta 0**) — the default path never samples the new LUT and the new bake writes a texture nothing reads. **Flag-on verified** across azimuths (toward/90°/anti-sun) at a fixed low sun: meridian horizon lum 205.8 vs inline 223.1 (close match), strong correct azimuthal variation (warm/bright near the sun → cool/dim anti-sun) the old table could NOT produce, no seams at the azimuth wrap, no f16 blowout, horizon resolved; 0 device errors (`probe-atmo-lut-no-device-error` GREEN). **Inscatter-LUT fast path** (`ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT`) for the SKY shell stays OFF — the sky-view LUT is the sun-relative replacement; the old inscatter LUT remains the fog-drape source unchanged. **Remaining follow-ups (NOT in 428):** (a) re-parameterize the MS LUT (`computeMultipleScattering`) onto the sky-view domain so SKY-MS gets directional all-azimuth lift (today it's azimuth-flat → only a tiny ~0.4-lum veil add at off-meridian); (b) optionally fold the env-map / aerial-perspective MS source onto the sky-view param (Phase 2); (c) bake at >1 observer altitude (currently ground-level only). **Files:** `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl`, `WebGPUAtmosphereLUT.ts`, `SkyAtmosphere.wgsl`, `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js`, `WebGPUPerformanceManager.ts`, `Scene/SkyAtmosphere.js`, `probe-sky-view-lut.mjs` (NEW).
- **NEW-GROUND-ATMOSPHERE-DRAPE-LIMB-WIDTH** — ✅ **CLOSED (Batch 513, NEW-GLOBE-DRAPE-LIMB-CLOSEOUT, 2026-07-03).** The drape band itself measured AT PARITY: `probe-limb-halo-width` drape diagnostic reports WebGL=1 px vs WebGPU=1 px (delta 0) at the full-disc framing. The residual the epic was chasing was re-re-attributed to the **SkyAtmosphere shell**: `skyColorForRay` (`SkyAtmosphere.wgsl`) clipped planet-striking rays at the earth surface (`rayEnd = earthIntersect.x`), which (a) rendered the see-through disk interior as a solid daylight-blue disc whenever the globe surface didn't cover it (globe.show=false — latent since the original port, unmasked by the 2026-06-25 skybox-over-atmosphere draw-order fix, which is why Batch 327's shell gate had measured thin-rim "parity": the opaque skybox was hiding the disc), and (b) truncated WebGL's ~10 px limb extinction tail (shallow sub-limb chords marching through the planet with finite optical depth — the row-scan proved rim peak pixels byte-matched while WebGPU cut the tail: WebGL `204:(67,108,154) 205:(219,246,245) 206-209 bright tail` vs WebGPU dark from 206). **Fix (Batch 513):** march planet-striking rays through the planet like WebGL, with a −150 km underground sample-height floor in `computeScattering` (view + light rays) so the extinction is deterministic (WGSL exp() overflow is spec-indeterminate; WebGL rides f32 overflow to the same visual black). Above −150 km the math is bit-identical, so non-striking rays (every ray in a globe-covered default view) are unchanged. **Verified:** shell gate PASS WebGL=14 px vs WebGPU=16 px median (±6 px tol); drape diag 0 px; underground/translucency/colorgrading/polar/atmosphere probes green. Historical investigation under `NEW-VR2-3b-LIMB-HALO-RESIDUAL` below.
- **NEW-POSTPROCESS-USER-WARN-PROD** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 290). User-supplied GLSL `PostProcessStage`s (no `wgslFragmentShader` uniform) are silently SKIPPED on WebGPU because the backend needs WGSL — the dropped stage produces no output and the user had no signal it didn't run. The `glslOnlyCount > 0` `oneTimeWarning("WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.userStagesGLSL", …)` in `configureWebGPUPostProcessPipeline` was wrapped in `//>>includeStart('debug', pragmas.debug)`, so shipping (minified) builds stripped it and users got silence. Un-stripped: the warning is now PERMANENT (a real, user-actionable error per the CLAUDE.md logging rules — "Real errors must always reach the console"). `oneTimeWarning` is production-safe (only its internal `defined(identifier)` assert is pragma-stripped; the `console.warn` body runs in every build) and dedupes by identifier so it fires once, not per frame. Warning text clarified to say the stages are SKIPPED / produce no output. Verified: `probe-taa-userwarn.mjs` (NEW) — adding a GLSL-only PostProcessStage on a WebGPU scene emits exactly one `console.warn` containing "GLSL custom shaders are not transpiled" and does NOT crash; a WGSL-equipped stage emits no warning.
- **NEW-MODEL-IBL-BRDF-LUT** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 287). The generated split-sum environment BRDF LUT (`WebGPUBrdfLutGenerator`, rg32float 256×256) is now bound into the model material bind group (new bindings 37/38 — `unfilterable-float` texture + `non-filtering` sampler, since rg32float isn't filterable without the optional `float32-filterable` feature) and consumed by `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`'s ambient/IBL term. The specular IBL now uses the WebGL-matching split-sum form `radiance * FssEss` where `FssEss = Fr*lut.x + lut.y` (`Fr` = roughness-dependent Fresnel `f0 + (f90-f0)*(1-NdotV)^5`, `f90 = max(1-roughness, f0)`), and the diffuse IBL uses the Fdez-Aguera multi-scatter form `irradiance * (FmsEms + dielectricScattering)` — a 1:1 port of `ImageBasedLightingStageFS.glsl::textureIBL`. Replaces the prior `radiance * fresnelSchlickRoughness(...)` approximation that ignored the LUT and the energy-compensation terms. The BRDF LUT view is plumbed from `frameState.brdfLutGenerator._colorTexture._webgpuTextureView` (with a 1×1 scale=1/bias=0 placeholder in `WebGPUModelPipelineCache` until the generator runs, collapsing the term to `radiance*F0`). Verified: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-model-ibl.mjs` — WebGPU specular IBL matches WebGL within 8.5% (edge-dominated) at two camera angles, 0 device errors; model-pbr-audit (5 models) + model-aniso-ibl + collections-regression + sandcastle-smoke all green.
- **NEW-MODEL-IBL-KTX2-CUBEMAP-WEBGPU** — ✅ **RESOLVED (Batch 371, C2-2, 9fae6c1c7e; premise re-verified STALE Q6, 2026-07-04).** Authored `imageBasedLighting.specularEnvironmentMaps` KTX2 cubemaps now load + drive WebGPU model IBL, matching WebGL. The Batch 369 producer + FR lifecycle (kept as scaffolding after that revert) was re-wired in Batch 371 once the `NEW-WEBGPU-KTX2-TRANSCODER-FORMATS` prereq (Q1) landed: `ensureWebGPUSpecularSource` in `WebGPUImageBasedLighting.ts` load-once-fetches the KTX2 (`loadKTX2` no longer throws on a `WebGPUContext`), `buildWebGPUSpecularCubeFromKTX2Buffers` uploads the base mip into an `rgba16float` cube, `generateIBLMaps` prefilters on-device, and the cube is published as `_specularEnvironmentCubeMap` for the IBL consumer. Q6 (Campaign 3) re-ran `probe-model-ktx2-ibl.mjs` → GATE PASS: (A) cube loaded (`ready` + `maxMip>0`), (B) parity webgpu-KTX2 vs webgl-KTX2 **9.43% < 12%**, (C) consume-proof vs procedural **5.26% > 3%**, (D) 0 device errors; output PNGs read (WebGPU reflective cube matches WebGL; the procedural fallback is visibly flatter). No code change needed at Q6 — probe is the standing regression guard. Original open-item notes retained below for history. (orig) The explicit `imageBasedLighting.specularEnvironmentMaps` KTX2 cubemap path never becomes `ready` on a WebGPU context, so an app that supplies an authored environment map silently falls back to the per-model procedural `DynamicEnvironmentMapManager` sky on WebGPU (WebGL uses the authored map). Root cause: `SpecularEnvironmentCubeMap.isSupported(context)` gates on WebGL-only capability getters (`colorBufferHalfFloat` && `halfFloatingPointTexture`) || (`floatingPointTexture` && `colorBufferFloat`)) && `supportsTextureLod` — these are false/undefined on the WebGPU `GraphicsContext`, so `update()` early-returns before creating the cube map, and `WebGPUImageBasedLighting` never sees `_texture._webgpuTexture.view`. Fix path: add WebGPU-equivalent capability getters to the WebGPU context (rgba16float is universally renderable/filterable on WebGPU; textureLod is always available) and verify the `CubeMap` + `loadMipmaps` path produces a sampleable `_webgpuTexture.view` from the KTX2 mip buffers. The globe-terrain CSM receiver now DARKENS the ground where a caster's shadow falls (the reported symptom is gone). **Root cause = suspect (b): the cascade light-eye was on the WRONG side.** `WebGPUCSMRenderer._computeCascadeVPMatrix` placed the light camera at `eye = center − lightDir·2r` with `forward = center − eye = +lightDir` (looking back TOWARD the sun, from the anti-sun side). The WebGPU cast shadow has a coarse "sawtooth" edge because the 1024² CSM cascade-0 fits a 6226 m sphere (~12 m/texel) — the camera frustum slice (near→splitFar 7502 m) at a top-down 1700 m camera balloons the fit, while the WebGL reference cell uses a 2048 single shadow map fitted TIGHTLY to the visible scene (sub-meter/texel). This is a cascade-RESOLUTION gap, not the projection miss (the shadow is in the right place with the right coverage). The other 5 sub-checks pass (shadow casts, PCF softens B>A, no peter-panning, no acne wipe, 0 errors).

A lit `PerInstanceColorAppearance` (`flat:false`) primitive rendered its diffuse-shaded body noticeably DARKER on WebGPU than WebGL under the same light, independent of shadows (probe reproduced WebGPU body lum **92.5 vs WebGL 120.2**, ratio 0.77 — the same gap as the originally-reported ~92 vs ~154). **Root cause:** the WGSL primitive-lit fragments `phong` / `phongTextured` (`PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl` / `PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl`, the shaders `selectWebGPUShader` routes the lit color/per-instance-color appearances to) used an **ad-hoc Blinn-Phong term** — `lighting = 0.15 (ambient) + (0.7·max(dot(N, L_sun),0) + 0.15·spec) · shadowFactor` — that diverged from the GLSL reference `czm_phong` (`Builtin/Functions/phong.glsl`) used by `PerInstanceColorAppearanceFS` (and `AllMaterialAppearanceFS`). No regression: `probe-phong-render` (RENDERS OK, 0 errors), `probe-clustered-phong` (PASS, clustered additive lighting still layers correctly on the new base term), `probe-csm-soft-shadow` (6/6 PASS, ratio 1.24×, 0 errors); WebGL `PerInstanceColorAppearance` + `MaterialAppearance` + all `*Appearance` specs green (47 SUCCESS); `tsc` clean. **Files:** `PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl`, `PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl`, `probe-perinstance-diffuse.mjs`. **NOTE / follow-up:** the separate MaterialAppearance lit shaders (`PrimitiveMatColorLit.wgsl` et al.) carry the *same* ad-hoc Blinn-Phong term and so are still darker than their `czm_phong` WebGL reference — distinct WGSL files (not shared with `phong`), so untouched here. Tracked as **NEW-MATAPPEARANCE-DIFFUSE-PARITY** below.

- **NEW-COLLECTIONS-DIRTY-GATE** — Billboard/Label rebuild + full-upload entire instance buffer every frame. Port the Point renderer needsRebuild gate; keep resident instance array; writeBuffer only dirty sub-ranges. **ATTEMPTED + REVERTED (Batch 226) — subtler than the Point reference implies.** A `needsRebuild` gate (skip `buildInstanceData` + `writeBuffer` unless `_billboardsToUpdateIndex > 0 || lastLength !== length || definesChanged`) DID work for static billboards (verified: 1 build over 30 static frames, renders correctly) — the perf win is real. BUT the dirty-tracking re-arm is entangled with the WebGL vertex-build's reset SEQUENCE: `_updateBillboard` only re-pushes when `!billboard._dirty`, and the WebGL build clears `_dirty` (BillboardCollection.js:806/890) AND `_createVertexArray` (line 786) AND `_billboardsToUpdateIndex`, in order. Replicating only the `_dirty` reset → a *moving* billboard never re-triggered a rebuild (stale render). Adding the `_dirty` re-arm → static billboards rebuilt ~2×/frame (something — the `runSharedSceneLogic` readiness loop calling `_updateBillboard` for `textureDirty`, and/or `_createVertexArray` never being reset on WebGPU so `updateMode` re-runs `recomputeActualPositions` every frame — re-dirties them). **A correct gate must replicate the full WebGL reset sequence** (`_dirty` + `_createVertexArray` + `_billboardsToUpdateIndex`, and stop the readiness loop / `updateMode` from re-pushing settled billboards on WebGPU) and re-verify BOTH static-skips AND moving-updates. Reproducer: a probe toggling a `cache._buildCount` debug counter over static then dynamic frames. NOTE: the Point renderer (the "reference") likely has the SAME latent moving-primitive staleness — verify it too. Reverted to avoid shipping a correctness risk.
  - **ROOT-CAUSE PREREQUISITE (confirmed Batch 226, 2nd attempt):** added a backend-agnostic monotonic `_instanceVersion` bumped in `_updateBillboard`; the FR rebuilds when it advances (recorded, never reset). The version-signal is CORRECT (a color change and a position change each bumped it + triggered a rebuild) but it STILL rebuilt ~2×/frame for "static" billboards → **`_updateBillboard` is being called every frame for settled billboards on the WebGPU path** (the `runSharedSceneLogic` readiness loop / unreset `_createVertexArray`). So **step 0 for ANY dirty-gate is stopping the WebGPU collection path from re-dirtying settled billboards each frame** (replicate WebGL's "dirties consumed" semantics, or compute a true source-changed signal that ignores the per-frame re-touch). Both gate attempts are blocked on this, not on the gate logic itself.
  - **DESIGN DECISION (owner Q, 2026-06-11 — supersedes "all-or-nothing gate"):** the right target is **per-INSTANCE partial sub-range writes**, not the all-or-nothing rebuild. WebGPU's whole-buffer rebuild is O(N) per change-frame; for "micro-updates to tens of thousands of objects" (sparse changes in a huge collection) the fix is a **resident CPU instance array + `device.queue.writeBuffer(buf, K*stride, …, stride)` per changed instance** (O(changed), e.g. ~640 B for 10-of-50k vs 3.2 MB). This NEEDS the per-instance dirty list (`_billboardsToUpdate[0.._billboardsToUpdateIndex]`) — but does NOT need WebGL's per-ATTRIBUTE separate buffers (keep interleaved for draw-time cache locality; re-writing a changed instance's full 64 B record is fine). Extreme per-frame churn (100k+ all moving) → GPU-resident scatter via compute / storage buffer (no CPU round-trip). **Best home: a shared resident-instance-buffer manager with dirty-range tracking (pairs with NEW-COLLECTION-RENDERER-BASE), used by billboard/label/point.** Do probe-driven in a dedicated session after the step-0 re-touch fix.

Remaining follow-up for this ID is only the structural fold into NEW-COLLECTION-RENDERER-BASE (P1-T6) — **DONE for Billboard + Point (Batch 302):** the manager lazy-create + the capture→sync→consume ordering are now single structural calls (`getOrCreateInstanceManager` + `syncInstancesAndConsume`) in the shared base. - **NEW-GLOBE-DYNAMIC-OFFSET-UBO** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 292). Group-0 (camera UB + tile UB) of the globe surface renderer converted to a DYNAMIC-OFFSET bind-group layout (`hasDynamicOffset: true` on both bindings). Before: the group-0 bind group was rebuilt over the ring-allocator slice `(buffer, byteOffset)` and the cache keyed on the byte offset, so it churned whenever the per-frame allocation sequence shifted (tile streaming in/out during camera motion → all later tiles' offsets move → group-0 miss for each). Now: the bind group is built ONCE over the ring page at offset 0 (size = struct width), keyed only on the `(camera page, tile page)` buffer identities; the actual slice offset is supplied per-draw via `setBindGroup(0, bg0, [cameraOffset, tileOffset])`. The page identities cycle through the ring's `pageCount` and recur every `pageCount` frames, so the cache converges to ~`pageCount` group-0 entries and stays at ~100% hit-rate even under sustained panning. Dynamic offsets are 256-aligned by the ring allocator (and 0 on the first-frame fallback), satisfying `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`. The `_pipelineLayout` is unchanged (dynamic-offset is a BGL-entry property, transparent to pipelines), so all globe pipeline variants pick it up automatically. The offsets thread through `TileDrawDescriptor.bindGroup0DynamicOffsets` → the scene-adapter command's `_bindGroup0DynamicOffsets` → the `execute` closure (covers opaque, translucent, depth-only pre-pass, wireframe). Verified (`probe-globe-bindgroup-cache.mjs`, new Phase E sustained-pan): group-0 creations during 120 panning frames dropped from ~15 (max 3/frame, churn in 9 frames) to **0** (group-0 lifetime entries capped at 3 = pageCount, vs 63 before); group-1 imagery churn = 23-27 over the same window proves the motion actually streamed tiles (non-vacuous); steady-state + teleport-pan + visual + zero-error phases all still PASS; 99.6% lifetime hit rate. Regression: collections-regression, collections-far-camera, collections-2dcv-morph, bloom-parity, orbital-catalog, pickposition-webgpu, sandcastle-smoke all PASS.
- **NEW-GLOBE-RENDERBUNDLE-CACHE** — ✅ RESOLVED (Batch 292, dropped-as-net-negative). The globe pass built and discarded a `GPURenderBundle` every frame (create encoder → record every tile command → `finish()` → `executeBundles`). Render bundles only amortize when CACHED and replayed across many frames; this one was rebuilt from scratch each frame, paying full construction cost with zero amortization. It also CANNOT be safely cached: each globe command records `setBindGroup(0, bg0, [cameraOffset, tileOffset])` with the per-tile ring-allocator dynamic offsets BAKED IN at record time, and those offsets rotate every frame (the per-frame ring allocator cycles pages by design — NEW-GLOBE-DYNAMIC-OFFSET-UBO made the bind-GROUP object stable but the dynamic-OFFSET *values* still change frame-to-frame), so a cached bundle would replay stale offsets and bind the wrong UB slices; a signature-keyed cache including the offsets would miss every frame. Measured (`probe-globe-bundle-cost.mjs`, 55-tile low view): the bundle path ran ~0.3-0.4 ms SLOWER at the median than direct `executeBatch`, with a markedly worse p90 (build-cost spikes ~7.0 ms vs ~4.6 ms). **Decision: dropped the inline bundle** — `executeGlobeDispatch` now falls straight through to `executeBatch`. p90 frame cost improved to the no-bundle regime; unused imports (`isSceneFBMrtMode`, `MRT_NORMAL_ROUGHNESS_FORMAT`, `WebGPUContext` type) removed. The `WebGPURenderBundleManager` infrastructure is untouched (still used by other paths); the file docstring records the constraint so a future session doesn't re-add an inline globe bundle without first making the per-tile UBs frame-stable.

- **NEW-CAMERA-JITTER-ACCUMULATION** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 322). TAA sub-pixel jitter accumulated unboundedly on a stable frustum: `Scene.js` did `proj[8] += jitter.x; proj[9] += jitter.y` against `cam.frustum.projectionMatrix`, which is a DIRTY-CACHED getter — on a settled camera (stable fov/aspect/near/far) it returns the SAME array every frame without recomputing, so each frame's `+=` stacked on top of the last and proj[8]/proj[9] drifted ~linearly (a random walk with non-zero-mean IGN drift; measured peak ~5× maxJitter over 120 frames, growing with frame count). On a CHANGING frustum the matrix recomputed to its un-jittered base each frame so the old `+=` happened to be correct there. **Fix:** new `WebGPUTAAEffect.applyProjectionJitter(proj, jitterX, jitterY)` writes `base + jitter` ABSOLUTELY each frame — it tracks the un-jittered base (`_jitterBase8/9`) + last-applied jitter (`_jitterLastX/Y`); if the live `proj[8]/[9]` no longer equals `(storedBase + lastJitter)` within 1e-9 the frustum recomputed to a fresh base → re-capture it, then set `proj[8] = base8 + jitterX; proj[9] = base9 + jitterY`. Robust to BOTH the settled-cached case (bounded at base±maxJitter, no accumulation) AND the recomputed case (self-heals). The frozen/snapshot branch now calls `resetProjectionJitter()` (NaN-sentinels the base) alongside zeroing `jitterX/jitterY` so re-enabling can't reason about a stale base; the non-frozen branch still routes through `computeJitter` which sets `jitterX/jitterY` for the TAA shader. WebGL untouched (whole block gated by `scene.taaEnabled` + WebGPU-only `_alternateSceneRenderer?._postProcess`). **Spec:** `WebGPUTAAJitterAccumulationSpec.js` (5 cases, pure CPU/no GPU) — 120-frame stable-frustum bounded-drift assertion (per-frame + peak ≤ maxJitter), a negative control proving the old `+=` drifts >3× maxJitter, exact-`base+jitter` write, self-heal-on-recompute, and reset-then-recapture. Files: `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts`, `Scene.js`, `WebGPUTAAJitterAccumulationSpec.js` (+ `SpecList.js` registration).
  - **RE-SCOPE (2026-06-20 audit) — this is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH, not a fix for a reproduced live drift.** The unbounded-accumulation precondition (a dirty-cached projection getter returning the SAME array every frame so `+=` stacks) is generally ABSENT in the live WebGPU render loop: `WebGPUSceneRenderer._updateFrustumUniforms` (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1437`) sets `frustum.near/far` + NaN-sentinels the frustum cache (`frustumCache._near/_far = NaN`) and calls `uniformState.updateFrustum(frustum)` **every frame per frustum**, recomputing the camera-frustum projection from scratch — which invalidates the very near/far cache the Batch-322 random-walk assumed was stale. So the Batch-322 absolute-write is correct and worth keeping (it self-heals on recompute AND bounds the hypothetical settled-cache case), but it should NOT be read as having fixed an observed, reproduced TAA drift in the live loop. The spec's 120-frame drift is a synthetic stable-frustum harness, not the production code path.
  - **CROSS-REF — the deeper REAL gap (tracked separately, see NEW-TAA-PROJECTION-JITTER-OVERWRITTEN below):** that same per-frame `_updateFrustumUniforms` recompute OVERWRITES the projection jitter `Scene.js` applies to the camera frustum projection — the recomputed un-jittered projection lands in the uniform buffer BEFORE any draw, so the **projection-jitter half of TAA never reaches the GPU** on WebGPU. The history-reprojection/velocity half still works, but sub-pixel sample-position dithering (the part that actually anti-aliases static edges) is silently dropped. This is the substantive TAA-quality gap; the Batch-322 accumulation guard does not address it.
- **NEW-TAA-PROJECTION-JITTER-OVERWRITTEN** (M) — ✅ **SHIPPED Batch 358** (`WebGPUSceneRenderer._updateFrustumUniforms` now re-applies `taaEffect.jitterX/Y` to the per-frustum projection before `uniformState.updateFrustum` captures it; `setProjection` clones it + marks every dependent matrix dirty so the jitter flows into the camera UB; gated on `taaEnabled` → zero-op when off. Verified baseline-isolated via new `probe-taa-jitter.mjs`: WebGPU TAA-on projection center-offset 0 → 0.000828, TAA-off = 0). **Was Open (surfaced by the 2026-06-20 TAA audit; see NEW-CAMERA-JITTER-ACCUMULATION cross-ref above).** On WebGPU the projection-jitter half of TAA never reaches the GPU. `Scene.js` applies the per-frame sub-pixel jitter to the **camera frustum projection** (via `WebGPUTAAEffect.applyProjectionJitter`, Batch 322), but `WebGPUSceneRenderer._updateFrustumUniforms` (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1437`) then recomputes the projection from the frustum's near/far each frame (`frustumCache._near/_far = NaN` → `uniformState.updateFrustum(frustum)`) and writes that **un-jittered** projection into the camera uniform buffer before any draw — clobbering the jitter. Net effect: history reprojection + motion-vector accumulation work, but the sub-pixel sample-position dithering that actually anti-aliases static edges is dropped, so WebGPU TAA under-resolves compared to WebGL. **Needs:** carry the TAA jitter THROUGH the per-frame frustum-uniform recompute — either jitter the projection AFTER `updateFrustum` inside `_updateFrustumUniforms` (so the recompute can't overwrite it), or fold the jitter into the projection the uniform pack reads, gated on `scene.taaEnabled` + non-frozen. Must preserve the Batch-322 absolute-write semantics (no re-introduced accumulation) and stay WebGL-untouched. **Files (investigation start):** `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts` (`_updateFrustumUniforms` ~L1437–1483), `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts` (`applyProjectionJitter`), `Scene.js` (jitter application site). **Trace:** NEW-CAMERA-JITTER-ACCUMULATION re-scope, 2026-06-20.
- **NEW-BINDGROUPCACHE-EVICTION** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 293). The generic post-process bind-group cache (`WebGPUBindGroupCache`, used by Bloom/SSAO/DoF/GodRays/AutoExposure) keyed each bind group on `(layout id + per-entry resource identity)` in an UNBOUNDED `Map<string, GPUBindGroup>` with eviction only via explicit `invalidateAll()`. In the failure mode its own docstring warns about — input texture views recreated every frame WITHOUT a matching `invalidateAll` (the "0% hit rate" symptom) — the key set grew by one per frame forever, leaking a `GPUBindGroup` (≈150-300 B of driver state) each frame for the whole session. Fix: bounded LRU + optional age eviction. Map iteration order is kept as a recency list (each hit re-inserts the entry at the tail via delete+set), so the first key is the LRU → O(1) `_evictLRU()` on any miss that would exceed `maxEntries` (default 1024 — far above any real effect's stable key set, which is single-digit). New `beginFrame()` advances a frame clock and, when `maxIdleFrames > 0` (default 0 = LRU-only), drops entries idle past the window. Constructor now takes an optional `BindGroupCacheOptions { maxEntries, maxIdleFrames }`; all six existing callers use the no-arg form and are unaffected (default cap applies). `getStats()` gains an `evictions` counter. Verified: `WebGPUBindGroupCacheSpec.js` +7 tests (30/30 green) — cap never exceeded, LRU touch protects recently-hit entries, **500 frames of per-frame identity churn stays bounded at ≤16 entries (was +1/frame unbounded pre-fix)**, age eviction drops/keeps by window, `maxIdleFrames=0` does no age eviction. Regression: bloom-parity (post-process cache live path), collections-regression, globe-bindgroup-cache, sandcastle-smoke all PASS. **Companion IDs left open (assessed this batch):** `NEW-RENDERBUNDLE-AGING-DECOUPLE` — `WebGPURenderBundleManager` ALREADY has full bounded LRU (`_maxCacheSize`/`_evictOldest`) + age eviction (`_maxIdleFrames`/`_evictStale`) driven by `beginFrame()`, so it is NOT an unbounded-growth gap; this ID is purely the "decouple aging from the frame tick" refinement, deferred. `NEW-RESOURCEMANAGER-KEY-EVICTION` — `WebGPUResourceManager`'s sampler + BGL caches key on `JSON.stringify(descriptor)`; both key spaces are naturally finite (a finite set of sampler descriptors and pipeline layouts per app), so realistic growth is bounded — lower value, deferred.

Therefore: **`NEW-FORK-MODERNIZATION-REVERT` and `NEW-CAMERA-UPDATEVIEWMATRIX-REVERT` are DECLINED as reverts** (modernization is product direction — stays). - **NEW-WEBGPU-INSTANCED-VA-DIVISORS** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 245; found by the Batch-238 probe baseline; pre-existing on main since the v1.140 upstream merge). ANY instanced model (vec3 OR matrix instancing path) crashed the WebGPU render loop: `VertexArray` bind runs `context._vertexAttribDivisors[index] = this.instanceDivisor` (VertexArray.js:123) but `WebGPUContext` never initialized `_vertexAttribDivisors` — the `glVertexAttribDivisor` no-op compat stub existed, the divisor state cache next to it was missed (`TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined` → model never `ready` → WebGPU CPU pick unreachable). (Per-edge / per-lineString `materialColor` + per-vertex COLOR_0 overrides SHIPPED Batch 330 — see **NEW-EDGE-MATERIALCOLOR-OVERRIDE-WEBGPU** below.) **Pre-fix gap analysis retained for context:** the WebGPU model-edge path (`WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer` + `WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter`) was only PARTIALLY realized vs upstream `EdgeDisplayMode`; the inventory previously marked it fully SHIPPED (now §C.3 / §B.6 corrected). **Two tri-mode gaps:** (1) `SURFACES_ONLY` (the DEFAULT) must HIDE all extension edges, but the emitter gated only on `defined(edgeGltfPrimitive?.edgeVisibility)` and never read `model.edgeDisplayMode` — so any edge-bearing glTF emitted edges in the default mode (visible divergence vs WebGL on the most common CAD/BIM config; a one-line guard, effort S). (2) `EDGES_ONLY` (CAD wireframe) rendered surfaces with NO edges — the inverse of intent — three coupled causes: no `CESIUM_3D_TILE_EDGES_DIRECT` pass (slot 12) in the WebGPU frustum loop (`WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts` — commands binned there silently never executed), the emitter hardcoded `Pass.CESIUM_3D_TILE_EDGES`, and the surface command was emitted unconditionally with no EDGES_ONLY suppression (`WebGPUSceneRenderer3DTilePasses.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUModelRenderer.js`; effort M). **Three data-path gaps:** the extractor consumed only the per-triangle 2-bit `edgeVis.visibility` encoding and early-returned otherwise (effort L) — (a) explicit `lineStrings` edges were dropped (BENTLEY/styled-gltf-lines assets yielded zero WebGPU edges); (b) the authored `silhouetteNormals` signed-byte accessor is ignored — WebGPU re-derives face normals from adjacency, so silhouette classification can diverge AND the upstream PR#13421 degenerate-triangle repro can't be confirmed clean on WebGPU (the synthesized zero-area-tri normal biases the silhouette dot-product differently than the authored-normal path; the existing NEW-UPSTREAM-EDGE-DEGENERATE-13421 fix is the WebGL/CPU half only); (c) per-edge / per-lineString `materialColor` overrides are unsupported (WebGPU applies one primitive-level color, no `a_edgeColor` equivalent) — **RESOLVED Batch 330, NEW-EDGE-MATERIALCOLOR-OVERRIDE-WEBGPU below.** **Files:** `WebGPUEdgeVisibilityEmitter.ts`, `WebGPUModelRenderer.js`, `WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer3DTilePasses.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`. Tracked in FEATURE_INVENTORY §C.3. **Trace:** WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md (P2 "EdgeDisplayMode.SURFACES_ONLY suppression" + "EdgeDisplayMode.EDGES_ONLY (CAD wireframe)" + "WebGPU edge data parity" + P3 "Degenerate-triangle edge fix (PR#13421) parity on WebGPU").

### MEDIUM / LOW (23)

**`NEW-DECOUPLEDSCAN-FORWARD-PROGRESS-GUARD` (A2.3) — ✅ SHIPPED (C4 queue, 2026-07-04).** The decoupled-lookback prefix-sum kernel (`DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl`, opt-in via `useDeterministicPointCloudLOD`/`useDecoupledScan`, default OFF) spun on peer-workgroup partitions with an UNBOUNDED `loop { atomicLoad; if !empty break; storageBarrier() }`. WebGPU guarantees no cross-workgroup forward progress, so that spin could livelock/hang the device when a predecessor partition is never scheduled (occupancy < dispatch size). **Latent bug surfaced en route:** the `storageBarrier()` sat inside the lane-0-only lookback (`if (localIdx == 0u)`) — non-uniform control flow — which is a WGSL COMPILE ERROR ("'storageBarrier' must only be called from uniform control flow"), so the entire scan module failed to compile and the scan path was silently dead (only ever "verified" by mock-device specs; the sole runtime consumer, PointCloudLOD, has no Scene wiring yet). **Fix:** (1) removed the illegal `storageBarrier()` — `atomicLoad` on the read_write storage atomic already re-reads device memory each iteration (atomics can't be hoisted/CSE'd), so peer stores stay visible without a fence; (2) added a WGSL iteration-cap watchdog (`MAX_LOOKBACK_SPINS = 1<<20`, shared budget across the whole lookback) that abandons the spin and terminates the kernel instead of hanging; (3) host-side occupancy gate in `WebGPUDecoupledScan` (`maxSafeWorkgroups`, default = `device.limits.maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension` — pure capability gate, no false trips) exposed as `canDispatch(n)`; `dispatch()` refuses (returns false, encodes nothing) when it trips and emits a PERMANENT throttled `console.error` sentinel (CLAUDE.md loop-sentinel mandate); (4) `WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.dispatch` now checks `canDispatch` and falls back to the atomic-compaction path when unsafe (byte-identical when `useDecoupledScan` is false — the gate lives inside the opt-in branch). **Verified:** `probe-decoupledscan-progress-guard.mjs` (real GPU, injects built WGSL) — shader now COMPILES, correct inclusive prefix sum across 16 wg (4000 ones), ragged 13-wg random tail, and 391 wg (100000 ones) terminating in ~22 ms; `WebGPUDecoupledScanSpec` 10/10 (4 new gate tests), `WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessorSpec` 7/7, `probe-pointcloud-lod` PASS, `tsc` clean. **Files:** `Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl`, `WebGPUDecoupledScan.ts`, `WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts`, `WebGPUDecoupledScanSpec.js`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-decoupledscan-progress-guard.mjs`.

**`NS-DECOUPLEDSCAN-NO-SCENE-WIRING` — ✅ SHIPPED (Campaign 5).** Follow-on to the forward-progress guard above: the GPU point-cloud LOD processor compiled and had the guard, but its opt-in path (`pointCloud.enableGPULOD`, read by `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer`) had NO public Scene control, so the deterministic decoupled-scan path was never reachable in-product — it could only ever be verified by direct-dispatch probes. `PointCloud.js` is instantiated ONLY by `TimeDynamicPointCloud`, so the wiring is a single owner. **Fix (Scene wiring, default OFF / byte-identical when off):** (1) added a public `gpuLOD` boolean (default `false`) to `PointCloudShading`; (2) `TimeDynamicPointCloud.renderFrame` now maps `pointCloud.enableGPULOD = shading.gpuLOD === true` alongside the other `shading.*` → `pointCloud.*` mappings. The deterministic-scan sub-option (`useDecoupledScan`) was already reachable via `contextOptions.useDeterministicPointCloudLOD` (passes straight through `ContextFactory` → `WebGPUContext`). Full in-product chain now: `new Viewer(el,{contextOptions:{renderer:'webgpu',useDeterministicPointCloudLOD:true}})` + `new TimeDynamicPointCloud({shading:{gpuLOD:true}})` → `enableGPULOD` → LOD processor (>50k pts) → `_dispatchScanPath` (tagVisible → decoupled scan → compactScanned). WebGL ignores `gpuLOD` (no-op). **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pointcloud-gpulod-scene-wiring.mjs` (NEW, real GPU) — CHECK A: `PointCloudShading().gpuLOD===false` default / settable true; CHECK B (option ON): the real `context.pointCloudLOD` processor records all THREE scan passes (`tagVisible`, `Scan ComputePass`, `compactScanned`); CHECK C (off-gate, option OFF): only the atomic `computeMainSubgroups` pass, ZERO scan passes. `probe-pointcloud-lod` + `probe-decoupledscan-progress-guard` still PASS; `tsc`/eslint clean. **Files:** `Scene/PointCloudShading.js`, `Scene/TimeDynamicPointCloud.js`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pointcloud-gpulod-scene-wiring.mjs`.

`fitShadowMapToScene` 5-step bounding-box construction + light-space sign notes; `resize` 1-pass/4-pass cascade layout ASCII diagrams + clear-pass + texture-space transform; `checkVisibility` in-view/horizon/fade/sphere-frustum comments; `updateCameras` per-camera-role inline comments + light-direction/position/near-far section headers. Comment-only, zero logic change; ShadowMap specs 50/50, CSM cast-dispatch probe PASS), `NEW-SYNC-MOVEMAP`, `NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY`, `NEW-TS-CONVERT-JS-RENDERERS`.

#### `NEW-CLUSTER-MULTIFRUSTUM-BOUNDS` — premise reconciled 2026-07-05 (PERF-only, NOT a correctness gap)

Verified against live code + a Playwright probe. `WebGPUSceneRendererClusteredLighting.ts:208-219` collapses the whole visible depth into a SINGLE cluster grid built from `scene.camera.frustum.near/far`, and B572 (`NEW-CLUSTERED-ASSIGN-BOUNDS-DIRTY`) already fixed the bounds→assign re-dispatch. The remaining "multi-frustum" item is **not** a binning-correctness or WebGL-parity gap:

- **Self-consistent → conservatively correct.** The FS `clusterIndexFor` (`ClusteredLighting.wgsl`) uses the *identical* collapsed near/far + *identical* exponential slice mapping as the `ClusterBounds` compute pass, so every fragment lands in the cluster whose AABB actually contains it — regardless of how many render frustums the scene splits into. Coarse Z-slices make a cluster over-*include* lights (a superset), never drop the ones that belong; the per-light `dist > range → 0` cutoff in `evalSingleClusteredLight` zeroes any over-included light. Result: pixel-identical output vs a per-frustum grid.
- **WebGPU-only feature — no WebGL reference.** Cesium has no Forward+ clustered lighting in WebGL, so there is nothing to match. Off by default (`scene.clusteredLightingEnabled=false`), byte-identical when off.
- **Per-cluster overflow is not solved by per-frustum grids anyway** — `CLUSTER_MAX_LIGHTS_PER_CLUSTER=256` per cluster vs `CLUSTER_MAX_LIGHTS=1024` total; per-frustum grids redistribute Z-resolution but keep the same per-cluster cap and 24 slices.
- **Acceptance evidence:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-clustered-multifrustum.mjs` — a genuine 19-frustum scene (log-depth split via lowered `logarithmicDepthFarToNearRatio`) shows the model correctly lit by a clustered point light (40,958 changed px, max Δ 430, 0 device errors); the model renders identically OFF/ON and only brightens where the light reaches. Standing `probe-clustered-visible.mjs` still PASS.

Per-frustum-slice cluster grids remain a **deferred performance / Z-resolution optimization** (tighter binning near the camera → fewer lights evaluated per fragment in deep scenes). It would add per-frustum grid selection threaded through every consumer draw inside the frustum loop — a new correctness surface — for zero visible change. Left deferred; the existing `:208-219` comment ("Per-frustum-slice cluster bounds are a future optimization") is accurate as-is.

- **NEW-CLOUD-SCALE-METERS** — ✅ FOUND + FIXED (Batch 253, caught by the final-sweep run of probe-polyline-cloud-consume — the first since the Batch-251 log-depth flip). `WebGPUCloudRenderer`'s VS sized the quad as `quadPos * scale / viewportSize * 2 * clip.w` — `CumulusCloud.scale` interpreted as SCREEN PIXELS, distance-invariant — while upstream `CloudCollectionVS.glsl` applies `positionEC.xy += scale * offset` (METERS in eye space). - ~~**NEW-WASMRTE-SUBRANGE-ENCODE** (S) — Sub-range variant of WasmRTEBridge.batchEncode (encode dirty [offset,count) at offset).~~ **SHIPPED Batch 271.** Added `batchEncodeRange(positions, srcOffset, count, outHigh, outLow, dstOffset?)` to `WasmRTEBridge.js` — encodes the contiguous `[srcOffset, srcOffset+count)` slice into the `[dstOffset, ..)` output window IN PLACE (untouched output bytes preserved), so an incremental repack can patch only its dirty slice. `dstOffset` defaults to `srcOffset`. Implemented as **JS-side pointer arithmetic over the EXISTING `batch_rte_encode` kernel** (copy the dirty slice to the front of the RTE arena, encode from index 0, read the result back into the dst window) — **NO new Rust export, NO WASM rebuild**. The scalar JS fallback (`_encodeRangeJS`) uses the same fround split (`high=fround(v); low=fround(v-high)`) as both `batchEncode` and the wasm32 kernel, so the two paths are byte-identical. Honors the bridge contract (threshold gate, feature-detect, arena-slot alloc, try/catch → JS fallback). **Also fixed a latent bug surfaced while verifying:** the wasm-bindgen glue does NOT re-export `memory`, so `_wasmModule.__wbindgen_export_0 ?? _wasmModule.memory` was `undefined` and the WASM path of EVERY RTE encode was silently catching + falling back to JS. `loadWasm` now captures the exports object returned by `__wbg_init()` (which carries `.memory`) into `_wasmExports`; a new `_wasmMemory()` helper resolves it for `_encodeWasm`/`_encodeRangeWasm`/`_toEyeWasm` (output unchanged — JS fallback was byte-exact — but the WASM kernel now actually runs). VERIFY: `Tools/wasm-subrange-encode-check.mjs` (standalone node, drives the REAL bridge via an ESM resolve-hook loader + a fetch shim that feeds the on-disk `.wasm`) — 18 assertions: WASM vs JS byte-identity over an interior sub-range, equality to an independent reference fround encode, dst-offset placement, untouched-byte preservation, src≠dst relocation, full-range == whole-array `batchEncode`, default-dstOffset, and a trip-wire that FAILS if any "using JS fallback" warning fires (so the WASM kernel is proven to genuinely run). When `_dirtyCount >= BUFFER_WASM_ENCODE_THRESHOLD` (5000) AND `_positionView instanceof Float64Array`, the POSITION high/low lanes for the whole contiguous dirty slice are encoded in ONE `batchEncodeRange(_positionView, dirtyOffset, dirtyCount, posHigh, posLow, dirtyOffset)` call (points have `vertexOffset == index`, so the slice is contiguous and maps 1:1 onto `posHigh[i*3..]`). Color/pick/outline interleave + pick-id creation + per-primitive `_dirty` clear stay in the JS loop. Below threshold (or FLOAT positions) the per-primitive scalar `EncodedCartesian3` loop runs as before. Bridge is lazily `new`'d on the cache/renderContext with a fire-and-forget `loadWasm()`; destroyed on teardown. A per-collection `_wasmEncodeThresholdOverride` lets the probe force scalar/batch on the SAME collection. **Encode equivalence (the key correctness point):** the batch path uses the fround split (`high=f32(v); low=f32(v-high)`) while the scalar `EncodedCartesian3` uses the AGI 65536-grid split — the high/low BYTES differ, but both satisfy `high+low == value` exactly in f64, so the shader's RTE reconstruction `(posHigh-camHigh)+(posLow-camLow)` rounds to the SAME eye-space position (verified numerically: 0.0m component diff even at GEO camera distance, and the camera stays AGI-encoded in `packCameraUniforms`). VERIFY: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffercoll-wasm-encode.mjs` — a 6084-point grid drawn via the batch path vs a forced-scalar twin diffs **0 px on WebGPU / 3 px on WebGL** (AA tol), sub-threshold (64) + override-Infinity collections stay scalar (instrumented `wasmEncodeRepacks`/`scalarEncodeRepacks` counters), and a full-grid position update (#13465) re-renders +126px through the batch path; 0 rendering console errors; PNGs visually identical. tsc + gulp build green; collections-regression, buffer-logdepth-zfight, collections-far-camera, buffer-point-update, logdepth-zfight, orbital-catalog, sandcastle-smoke all PASS. **Caveat (historical) — the WASM kernel did NOT execute in the bundled build at Batch 272** (the byte-identical JS fallback ran instead); **this was FIXED in Batch 274 (NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD below) — the real kernel now loads + runs in the bundle.** Rendering was correct either way. **Threshold lowered 5000→2000 in Batch 273** — see NEW-BUFFERCOLL-ENCODE-BENCHMARK below for the measured rationale (the win is the encode-hoist, not WASM SIMD).
- ~~**NEW-BUFFERCOLL-ENCODE-BENCHMARK** (M) — Benchmark 10k/50k/100k scalar-vs-WASM both backends + threshold tuning + visual-regression probe.~~ **SHIPPED Batch 273.** Built TWO complementary measurement vehicles + tuned the threshold from the data (NOT assumption — honest result reported). **(1) `Tools/wasm-encode-benchmark.mjs`** — a Node CPU-encode micro-benchmark that drives the REAL `batch_rte_encode` kernel under raw node (same loader+fetch-shim harness as `wasm-subrange-encode-check.mjs`, with a trip-wire that fails on any silent JS fallback), comparing the WASM kernel vs the scalar fround twin at 10k/50k/100k with warmup + median timing + byte-identity assertions. This is the ONLY place the real kernel runs (the bundle can't load WASM — NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD). Result: WASM ~**1.2-1.25x** at 10k-50k, **ties** (~1.0x) at 100k — the WASM path's per-call arena copy/readback overhead scales with count and erodes the SIMD win; absolute CPU encode is tiny (0.1-1.2 ms even for 100k/frame). **(2) `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffercoll-encode-benchmark.mjs`** — a Playwright end-to-end probe (BOTH backends) that nudges EVERY point each frame to force a full-range repack+upload, times repack+writeBuffer via a debug-pragma timer in both hot paths (`_repackMsTotal`/`_repackSamples` on the cache/renderContext), and prints a per-count per-backend ms/frame table for the batch-encode strategy vs the forced-scalar (`_wasmEncodeThresholdOverride=Infinity`) path, PLUS a WebGPU-vs-WebGL coverage no-regression assertion (Principle 8) + PNGs. **KEY FINDING:** the dominant repack cost is the per-primitive `EncodedCartesian3` 65536-grid split INSIDE the loop, NOT the GPU upload and NOT WASM. Hoisting the position encode into one contiguous `batchEncodeRange` fround call makes the repack **~25-40% faster end-to-end at ≥1500 points on BOTH backends** even with the WASM kernel dark (JS fround twin running). Crossover (forced-batch sweep at 500/1000/1500/2000/3000): batch LOSES below ~750 (fixed slice-setup overhead), marginal at ~1000, wins reliably from ~1500 up; absolute repack < 0.5 ms/frame below 1500 (negligible). **Threshold set to 2000** (both backends, kept in lock-step) — inside the winning region with margin against timer noise. **Honest negative on WASM specifically:** the SIMD win is below browser measurement noise and dormant anyway (bundle load), so NO WASM-specific gating was added — the threshold gates the encode-strategy hoist, which wins regardless of whether the kernel or its JS twin produced the bytes. With >= 2 points the dynamic-update path renders correctly (verified). WebGPU is unaffected (single point updates fine). Not a regression from the `_dirty` fix — the fix is correct (proven on both backends with >= 2 points + on WebGPU with 1). The documented dropout did NOT reproduce there — consistent with the "flaky/intermittent" description; it likely depends on a specific draw/depth/cull state the default viewer loop doesn't hit. Per Principle 8 (reproduce-in-a-probe-first), NO speculative source fix was shipped — a fix that can't be shown to move a failing probe isn't a fix. The probe is retained as a regression gate documenting the working path; tighten it to capture the flaky case (and only then fix) if a real scene reproduces it deterministically.

- **NEW-BUFFERPRIMITIVE-COLOR-ALPHA** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 315, `b6a23ae518`). color.alpha translucency now emitted via lockstep-widened packed lanes (point `showSizeAndColor` vec3→vec4, polygon `showAndColor` vec2→vec3, polyline new f32 alpha lane @location 8). **Pre-fix gap analysis retained for context:** (M) — surfaced by WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06, upstream PR#13384.
