Verify with a 0.5-alpha-fill probe extending `probe-bufferpolygon-vector-tile.mjs` on both backends. **Trace:** WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md (P1, "BufferPrimitiveMaterial color.alpha translucency"); FEATURE_INVENTORY.md §A.4 GeoJsonPrimitive.
- **NEW-BUFFERPRIMITIVE-BLEND-OPTION** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 315, `b6a23ae518`). blendOption now reads `collection._blendOption` and builds a cache-keyed OPAQUE pipeline variant routing to `Pass.OPAQUE`. **Pre-fix gap analysis retained for context:** (M) — WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06, PR#13384. None of the three Buffer* renderers read `collection._blendOption`; they hardcoded a translucent blend state and always pushed `Pass.TRANSLUCENT` with `depthWriteEnabled=false`. OPAQUE collections (the common GeoJSON-fill case) then rendered in the translucent pass → wrong sort/occlusion vs WebGL, and opaque fills didn't write depth so stacked/adjacent polygons showed order-dependent sort artifacts (this subsumes the audit's separate "GeoJsonPrimitive opaque polygon fills forced through TRANSLUCENT" P2 row, which affects the polyline path identically). Fix: surface `_blendOption` on the shared `WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts` (default `BlendOption.TRANSLUCENT`), build + cache-key a second OPAQUE pipeline variant (blend off, `depthWriteEnabled=true`) in each renderer's pipeline builder, and route to `Pass.OPAQUE` (not the hardcoded `Pass.TRANSLUCENT`) when `_blendOption===BlendOption.OPAQUE`, mirroring WebGL's branch in `renderBufferPointCollection.js` / `renderBufferPolygonCollection.js`. Best landed in the SAME batch as NEW-BUFFERPRIMITIVE-COLOR-ALPHA (both touch pipeline/pass selection). **Trace:** WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md (P1, "blendOption (OPAQUE vs TRANSLUCENT) param" + P2 "GeoJsonPrimitive opaque polygon fills forced through TRANSLUCENT").
- **BUFFER-POSITION-INT-NORMALIZED** (Q12 / C4-BUFFER-POSITION-INT-NORMALIZED) — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-04). Buffer* collections with an integer `positionDatatype` (BYTE/UNSIGNED_BYTE/SHORT/UNSIGNED_SHORT/INT/UNSIGNED_INT) and `positionNormalized:true` now decode BYTE-IDENTICALLY on WebGPU vs WebGL. **Root cause:** WebGL has two vertex paths (renderBuffer*Collection.js) — DOUBLE → RTE positionHigh/positionLow (`USE_FLOAT64` GLSL branch, `czm_modelViewRelativeToEye`), and integer → a single `position` attribute with the GPU `normalize` flag feeding the `#else` GLSL branch (`czm_modelView * vec4(position,1)`). The WebGPU renderers have NO integer vertex path; they ALWAYS RTE-encode the model-space position into positionHigh/positionLow. Non-normalized integer positions already matched (raw int RTE-encodes to the same model-space value WebGL's plain attribute feeds), but `positionNormalized:true` was NOT applied — the WebGPU encode fed the RAW integer (e.g. 32767) into `EncodedCartesian3.fromCartesian`, so a normalized-SHORT point landed hundreds of km from where WebGL (GPU-normalized to 1.0) drew it. **Fix:** two shared helpers in `WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts` — `bufferPositionNormalizeDivisor(collection)` returns the per-component divisor matching `Core/AttributeCompression.dequantize` + the GL2 signed-normalize `max(c/(2^(b-1)-1),-1)` convention (0 for DOUBLE/FLOAT/non-normalized, so the common path is branch-free byte-identical), and `normalizeBufferPositionInPlace(cart, divisor)` applies it. Each of the three renderers (`WebGPUBufferPoint/Polyline/PolygonRenderer.ts`) computes the divisor once per repack and dequantizes every raw position read (point: after `getPosition`; polyline: after each current/prev/next `fromArray`; polygon: after `fromArray`) BEFORE the scene-mode reproject + RTE encode. The collection's own `_updateBoundingVolume` already dequantizes (via `AttributeCompression.dequantize`), so SCENE3D culling was already correct. **Verify:** `probe-buffer-integer-position.mjs` — {WebGL,WebGPU}×{normalized SHORT ±32767/-32768, DOUBLE control} at the same model-space cross under a shared ENU×300 km modelMatrix; per-backend int centroid == double centroid (0.00 px), cross-backend int centroid matches (0.31 px), 858–859 px each, 0 errors; reverting the encode fix drives WebGPU-int to 0 px (off-screen) — the probe FAILS pre-fix. PNGs READ (both backends show the identical 4-point cross). **Doc note:** the older `probe-bufferpoint-positiondatatype.mjs` + `BufferPointMaterial.detectUnsupportedPositionEncoding` remain as a HISTORICAL documentation-gate (debug-only, never called in the render path); its "not yet wired / may render in the wrong position" warning is now stale — superseded by this probe. Rewording/retiring that guard is a separate doc-hygiene follow-up (not done here to keep this fix scoped + the old probe green).
- **NEW-BUFFERPRIMITIVE-BOUNDING-VOLUME** (S) — RESOLVED-by `batch-bufferprimitive-parity` (WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06, PR#13477). All three Buffer* renderers build their `WebGPUDrawCommand` WITHOUT `boundingVolume`/`debugShowBoundingVolume` even though the command supports both (`WebGPUDrawCommand.ts:84,250,388,592`) — so there is no per-frustum culling (every collection drawn every frame) and toggling `debugShowBoundingVolume` on a GeoJsonPrimitive collection is a silent no-op on WebGPU (WebGL draws the bounding-sphere debug primitive). Same omission pattern already fixed for `ComputeInstance` (Batch 235) + GroundPrimitive: pass `collection.boundingVolume` + `collection.debugShowBoundingVolume` to the command, and because the Scene-side `_boundingVolume` auto-updates (world-space, `BoundingSphere.fromVertices` + `BoundingSphere.transform(modelMatrix)`), refresh it onto the command EVERY frame, not once at creation. Discharges the audit's standalone P3 "debugShowBoundingVolume on GeoJsonPrimitive collections" row. **Trace:** WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md (P1, "World-space boundingVolume + debugShowBoundingVolume on buffer draw commands"). **RECONCILE (2026-07-05, C4-GEOJSONPRIMITIVE-PROBE):** the "RESOLVED" above was over-stated on TWO counts, now split: (1) `GeoJsonPrimitive` itself never exposed `debugShowBoundingVolume` at all — the loader constructed the three Buffer* collections without ever setting the flag, so on the GeoJSON path there was NO way to turn it on regardless of backend. FIXED here: added the `debugShowBoundingVolume` constructor option + a runtime get/set property on `GeoJsonPrimitive` that forwards to all three collections (default OFF, byte-identical when off since the collections already default the flag to false). Verified WebGL end-to-end — the red bounding-sphere wireframe now renders (`probe-geojson-holes.mjs`, WebGL overlay Δ 13.2%, PNG READ). (2) The WebGPU side is STILL a visual no-op: the Buffer* renderers set `debugShowBoundingVolume` onto the `WebGPUDrawCommand`, but the WebGPU scene renderer (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`) has NO bounding-volume debug pass — it handles `_executeDebugDepthOverlay` / `_executeDebugGBufferOverlay` / `_executeDebugFrustumOverlay` but nothing consumes the per-command `debugShowBoundingVolume` flag to draw the sphere (probe WebGPU overlay Δ 0.000%). The flag-plumbing is done; the WebGPU debug-sphere DRAW pass is unbuilt — that is the remaining parity gap (a default-off debug-only overlay pass mirroring `SceneDebug.debugShowBoundingVolume`, feature-sized, not attempted in this TIER3 task). **Regression probe:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-geojson-holes.mjs` — Polygon-with-hole via `GeoJsonPrimitive` on both backends: samples fill pixel (yellow) + hole pixel (black background, globe hidden) to prove the earcut interior ring is cut out at cross-backend parity, asserts the constructor option + runtime setter propagate to every defined collection, and asserts the WebGL overlay renders while measuring/reporting the WebGPU overlay Δ. **RESOLVED (2026-07-05, NEW-GEOJSON-WEBGPU-BV-DEBUG-DRAW-PASS):** the remaining WebGPU DRAW-pass gap from count (2) is now CLOSED. Added `WebGPUBoundingVolumeDebugPass.ts` (a default-off standalone pass) + `WebGPUSceneRenderer._executeBoundingVolumeDebugPass`, invoked from the post-frustum chain AFTER the scene pass resolves and BEFORE `_runPostProcessing`. It collects every `frameState.commandList` command flagged `debugShowBoundingVolume===true` with a bounding volume, and draws a red wireframe — three great circles for a `BoundingSphere` (`.radius`), a 12-edge cube for an `OrientedBoundingBox` (`.halfAxes`) — into the RESOLVED single-sample scene-color view with `loadOp="load"` (so it survives the post-process blit; pipeline is always `sampleCount=1`, no MSAA-load hazard). Model-space RTE positioning (per-command modelMatrix folded into `modelViewProjectionRelativeToEye` with the translation column zeroed + high/low model-space camera split), mirroring `WebGPUEllipsoidPrimitiveRenderer`. Default-OFF / byte-identical: when no command carries the flag the collection is empty and NO render pass is opened. Verified via `probe-geojson-holes.mjs` (now asserts BOTH backends' overlay Δ ≥ 0.05%): WebGL Δ 13.2%, WebGPU Δ 0.56% (smaller because SceneDebug draws a dense lat/long EllipsoidGeometry wireframe vs the WebGPU pass's three great circles at the same center/radius), OFF frame clean, PNGs READ, 0 console errors. NOTE the *culling* half of the original entry (world-space `boundingVolume` on the Buffer* commands for per-frustum culling) was already resolved separately; this closes only the debug-DRAW half.

### Phase 3 — GPU-resident compute-instance system + storage-buffer draw (dense-derivable; WebGPU-first headline; orbital = demo content since Batch 231)

- **NEW-COMPUTE-INSTANCE-SYSTEM** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 231). Owner-directed rework of the Batch-230 orbital catalog: the ENGINE feature is the feature-agnostic "N instances whose per-instance data lives in a GPU storage buffer, repopulated each frame by a pluggable USER-SUPPLIED WGSL compute kernel, drawn as instanced vertex-pulled quads — the CPU uploads only a time scalar". The engine keeps ZERO orbital domain knowledge: the circular-orbit element layout, the propagation kernel, and the LEO/MEO/GEO catalog generation now live wholly in the "WebGPU Orbital Catalog" Sandcastle + `probe-orbital-catalog.mjs`. Pieces: `Scene/ComputeInstanceCollection.js` (kernel + `floatsPerInstance` immutable at construction, loud `csm_computeInstance` validation, flat param lanes, `_consumeDirtyState` discipline, sim time from `frameState.time` − epoch BEFORE the FR branch) + `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUComputeInstanceRenderer.ts` (composes `const FLOATS_PER_INSTANCE` prologue + `ComputeInstanceScaffold.wgsl` + user kernel at pipeline build; composed modules cached per composed-source string per device — NOT under a ShaderSourceId; kernel hash keyed into compute-pipeline-cache names) + `ComputeInstanceRender.wgsl` (renamed from `OrbitalCatalogRender.wgsl`; render now pulls position/color/pixelSize from the 64-B instance record the kernel output writes, so the render side never sees the user's param layout). Kernel contract (UserPostProcessStage precedent): user defines `fn csm_computeInstance(index: u32, time: f32) -> ComputeInstanceOut {position, positionLow, color, pixelSize}` reading `params: array<f32>` + injected `FLOATS_PER_INSTANCE`; the engine owns bindings, entry point, bounds check, and the RTE high/low split + write (users never touch RTE). **Batch 277:** the struct gained `positionLow` + df64 helpers — f32 kernels leave it zero (back-compatible), df64 kernels fill it for ~46-bit precision (see NEW-ORBITAL-J2-KERNEL). Renames in place (add-only registries): FR key `ORBITAL_CATALOG_COLLECTION` → `COMPUTE_INSTANCE_COLLECTION` (slot 49 kept), ShaderSourceId 34 → `COMPUTE_INSTANCE_SCAFFOLD`, 35 → `COMPUTE_INSTANCE_RENDER`; `OrbitalPropagate.wgsl` deleted from the engine (its math is the demo kernel now); `OrbitalCatalogCollection.js` deleted (shipped hours earlier, unpublished — Sandcastle was the only consumer). Probes: `probe-orbital-catalog.mjs` (regression gate — equivalent numbers vs the Batch-230 baseline: 15289 px @ frame 15, 187.2% mask change, 0 errors) + `probe-compute-instance-generic.mjs` (NON-orbital rotating-Lissajous kernel — feature-agnosticism proof: 6552 px, 177.4% mask change, 0 errors).
- **NEW-ORBITAL-DATA-MODEL** (S) — Orbital element data model + buffer layouts; decide RTE-encode location (1-pager). Element SSBO (mean elements/Keplerian per object), per-frame time uniform, RTE high/low output SSBO. Decide kernel-emits-camera-relative (weather precedent) vs absolute-ECEF high/low + vertex-shader-subtract (point precedent, reuse PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl:84). Wrong choice reintroduces planetary-scale jitter.
- **NEW-ORBITAL-DEVICE-LIMITS-PROBE** (S) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 281). Validated that the GPU-resident compute-instance pipeline (NEW-COMPUTE-INSTANCE-SYSTEM) scales to a literal 1M-object catalog within the WebGPU device limits the renderer leans on — NO multi-SSBO split is required at 1M on a default-class adapter; the headroom + the negotiated ceiling are documented and probe-asserted. **The four at-risk limits + their measured headroom for 1M (records SSBO = N·64 B, params SSBO = N·FPI·4 B at the orbital FPI=10, pick-color SSBO = N·16 B):** (1) **maxStorageBufferBindingSize** — both the params SSBO and the 64-B-per-record instance SSBO bind as a SINGLE storage buffer. The records SSBO is the larger of the two at FPI≤16: 1M = **61 MB** (64 MiB-ish), params = 38 MB, pick = 15 MB. Spec DEFAULT ceiling 128 MB ⇒ ⌊128 MB / 64 B⌋ ≈ **2.097M full records / binding** (the prompt's ~2.7M figure is the SI-MB count; the binary-MiB count is ~2.10M), so 1M records clears the DEFAULT ceiling with ~2× headroom even on a minimal adapter. The probe's Edge/Chromium adapter actually exposes **2048 MB** (33.5M-record headroom). (2) **maxBufferSize** — same two buffers; spec min 256 MB, the test adapter exposes 2048 MB; 61 MB clears trivially. (3) **WebGPU** (`Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUComputeInstanceRenderer.ts`): `getWebGPUInstanceWorldPosition` reads the picked instance's ONE 64-B record slot back from the live ping-pong instance buffer via `copyBufferToBuffer` (slot offset = `index*64`) + `mapAsync`, summing `positionHigh + positionLow` to recover the absolute ECEF position. Same one-frame-stale sync-cache bridge as `PickDepth.getDepth` — the FIRST query for an index returns undefined (caller falls back to depth, the SAFE pre-feature state) and arms the readback; subsequent queries for the SAME index converge once the map resolves (cache trusted only for the armed index + within `POS_READBACK_MAX_STALE_FRAMES` dispatched frames). The instance buffers gained `GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC` so the readback can copy from them; staging buffer freed on teardown. (4) **WebGL2** (`Renderer/WebGLComputeInstanceRenderer.js`): two parts — (a) `getWebGLInstanceWorldPosition` re-runs the `cpuKernel` for the picked index at the current sim time and returns `out.position` directly (synchronous, deterministic — the kernel is pure in index+time+params); (b) a NEW per-instance WebGL PICK path (the WebGL counterpart of the Batch-279 WebGPU pick — previously WebGL compute-instances were unpickable, so pickPosition had no instance to identify): one `context.createPickId` per instance packed into a dedicated pick VAO's color slot (`ComputeInstanceWebGLPick{VS,FS}.glsl`, NEW — circle-discard mirrors the color FS so the pickable footprint matches the dot, byte-exact pick color, no blend), pushed as a standalone command on `frameState.passes.pick`. The pick VAO owns its OWN instance buffer (never shares the color VAO's → no double-free); pick ids freed on count change + teardown. **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-compute-instance-pickposition.mjs` (NEW) — three instances at fixed ECEF positions on BOTH `?renderer=webgl|webgpu`: pickPosition over each converges to that instance's known position within 50 m (measured dist = **0.00 m** all six), empty space → undefined, never a Promise (sync contract), 0 console/validation errors. probe-compute-instance-pick + probe-orbital-catalog + probe-pickposition-webgpu + probe-pickmodel-instanced + probe-compute-instance-webgl2{,-demos} + probe-collections-regression + sandcastle-smoke all stay green; tsc + gulp build green. **Remaining:** HDR-mode pick caveat carries over from NEW-ORBITAL-GPU-PICKING (shared pick-FBO format clamp).
- **NEW-ORBITAL-INVENTORY-TRACK** (S) — Add NEW-ORBITAL-GPU-RESIDENT to DEFERRED_WORK + FEATURE_INVENTORY (regime currently untracked). This regime is in neither DEFERRED_WORK.md nor FEATURE_INVENTORY §D. Add a tracking entry, document the element/time/output contract in a design doc, move §D->§C as it ships (Principle 6 — load-bearing for impact analysis).

### Phase 10 — Entity/CZML bulk fast-path (the large-dynamic-objects on-ramp)

- **NEW-ENTITY-BULK-FASTPATH** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 300, points). The Entity-API on-ramp to the flat-buffer collections: adding tens of thousands of homogeneous STATIC `point` entities (the CZML/GeoJSON catalog shape) no longer pays a per-entity Visualizer + per-frame property-evaluation cost. **`DataSources/BulkPointVisualizer.js`** (backend-agnostic — touches only `PointPrimitiveCollection`, which already carries the WebGL+WebGPU feature renderers + partial-write manager + WASM encode) replaces `PointVisualizer` in `DataSourceDisplay.defaultVisualizersCallback`. It classifies each point entity into a STATIC lane (every consumed PointGraphics property is `ConstantProperty`, position is `ConstantPositionProperty`, no `availability`, height-reference resolves to NONE, clustering off) vs a DYNAMIC lane. **Static entities are written ONCE** into a flat-buffer `PointPrimitiveCollection` added to the DataSource's own `_primitives` (with `id = entity` so `scene.pick` returns the Entity), then SKIPPED entirely by the per-frame `update()` — eliminating the legacy dominant cost (re-reading ~10 `Property.getValueOrDefault` values per entity EVERY frame even when nothing is dynamic). **Dynamic / clamped / time-windowed entities, and ALL entities while clustering is enabled, transparently delegate to a wrapped `PointVisualizer`** (its auto `collectionChanged` subscription is detached + its constructor-seeded `_items` cleared, so each entity is owned by exactly one lane), making those paths byte-identical to the legacy behaviour. `collectionChanged.changed` re-classifies an entity in place on a definition change (e.g. a `point.color` edit). `getBoundingSphere` resolves from the static lane first, else defers to the fallback. **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-entity-bulk.mjs` (NEW, gate) — adds 1k/5k/20k static point entities via a `CustomDataSource` on BOTH `?renderer=webgl|webgpu`, instruments an entity-count vs per-frame `DataSourceDisplay.update()` comparison against a forced-dynamic (`CallbackProperty` color) control: at 20k the static per-frame cost is ~0.01–0.02 ms (flat, count-independent) vs the dynamic path's ~15–17 ms — an **800×–1400× per-frame speedup** on both backends; static lane routes all 20k (staticCount=20000, fallbackCount=0); 20k points render (yellow pixels) on both backends; `scene.pick` returns the originating Entity (asserted on WebGL — see the WebGPU point-pick caveat below). probe-collections-regression + probe-collections-entity + probe-collections-2dcv-morph + probe-collections-far-camera + sandcastle-smoke + upstream-regression-check all stay green; tsc + gulp build green. **Remaining follow-ups:** the billboard + label bulk lanes (NEW-ENTITY-BULK-FASTPATH-BILLBOARD-LABEL), CZML/GeoJSON ingest hints (NEW-ENTITY-BULK-CZML-HINT), and the time-dynamic `SampledPositionProperty` GPU keyframe kernel (NEW-ENTITY-GPU-KEYFRAME-KERNEL) below.
- **NEW-ENTITY-BULK-FASTPATH-BILLBOARD-LABEL** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 333, billboards + labels). Extended the Batch-300 static-lane fast-path from points to BILLBOARD and LABEL entities (the other two homogeneous-catalog graphic types). **`DataSources/BulkBillboardVisualizer.js`** + **`DataSources/BulkLabelVisualizer.js`** (both backend-agnostic — they touch only `BillboardCollection` / `LabelCollection`, which already carry the WebGL+WebGPU feature renderers + partial-write managers) replace the direct `BillboardVisualizer` / `LabelVisualizer` instantiation in `DataSourceDisplay.defaultVisualizersCallback`. Each classifies an entity into a STATIC lane (every consumed graphics property is constant — `isStaticBillboardEntity` checks ~20 fields incl. `image`/`scale`/`color`/`eyeOffset`/origins/`*ByDistance`; `isStaticLabelEntity` checks ~20 incl. `text`/`font`/`style`/`fillColor`/`backgroundColor`/`pixelOffset`; both require `ConstantPositionProperty`, no `availability`, heightReference→NONE, clustering off) vs a DYNAMIC lane. **Static entities are written ONCE** into a flat-buffer `BillboardCollection` / `LabelCollection` added to the DataSource's own `_primitives` (with `id = entity` so `scene.pick` returns the Entity), then SKIPPED entirely by the per-frame `update()` — eliminating the legacy dominant cost (re-reading ~20–25 `Property.getValueOrDefault` values per entity EVERY frame). **Async readiness is tolerated** (the wrinkle vs points): the image / text is bound once at write time and the COLLECTION's own per-frame `update()` (driven by the Scene, not the visualizer) finishes the `BillboardTexture` decode / glyph-atlas mapping a few frames later — the static slot stays put and starts rendering when ready, with no re-classification or per-frame re-read. **Dynamic / clamped / time-windowed entities, and ALL entities while clustering is enabled, transparently delegate to a wrapped legacy `BillboardVisualizer` / `LabelVisualizer`** (its auto `collectionChanged` subscription is detached + its constructor-seeded `_items` cleared, so each entity is owned by exactly one lane), making those paths byte-identical to the legacy behaviour. `collectionChanged.changed` re-classifies an entity in place on a definition change; `getBoundingSphere` resolves from the static lane first, else defers to the fallback. **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-entity-bulk-billboard-label.mjs` (NEW, gate) — adds 200/800 static billboard+label entities + a forced-dynamic (`CallbackProperty` position/text) control on BOTH `?renderer=webgl|webgpu`: at 800 the static per-frame `DataSourceDisplay.update()` is ~0.02 ms vs the dynamic path's ~1.0–2.4 ms — a **52×–80× per-frame speedup** on both backends; static lane routes all 800 (bbStatic=800/fb=0, lblStatic=800/fb=0), dynamic lane keeps all 800 per-frame (dynBbFallback=800, dynLblFallback=800); 800 billboards (green squares) + labels (yellow glyphs) RENDER on both backends; async readiness tolerated (firstFrame bbReady/lblReady=false → settled=true, entities appear once decoded — no blank/drop); `scene.pick` over a bulk-written billboard AND label returns the originating Entity (asserted on WebGL — the WebGPU sync-pick cold-staleness caveat `NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-COLD-SYNC-STALENESS` applies equally to all primitive types and does not gate the on-ramp). `DataSourceDisplaySpec` (30, incl. the default-visualizer-order assertion updated for the Bulk variants — and `Specs/MockDataSource.js` given a `_primitives`/`_groundPrimitives` collection, a pre-existing gap from Batch 300 that left this spec red) + `BillboardVisualizerSpec` (16) + `LabelVisualizerSpec` (15) + `PointVisualizerSpec` (16, BulkPointVisualizer wrapped lane unregressed) all green via Edge; - **NEW-ENTITY-BULK-CZML-HINT** (M) — Surface the bulk fast-path at INGEST time. Today `BulkPointVisualizer` classifies entities AFTER `CzmlDataSource`/`GeoJsonDataSource` have already built per-entity `ConstantProperty` graphics — the classification is cheap but the property objects are still allocated. A loader-level hint (e.g. a homogeneous-static batch detector in the CZML packet processor, or a `DataSource`-level "these N entities are static points" fast-add) could skip the intermediate per-entity `PointGraphics`/`ConstantProperty` allocation entirely and write straight into the flat buffer. Bigger refactor (touches the CZML/GeoJSON update pipeline); deferred until the post-classification allocation cost is measured to matter at the target catalog size.
- **NEW-ENTITY-GPU-KEYFRAME-KERNEL** (L) — The time-dynamic counterpart: entities whose position is a `SampledPositionProperty` (CZML satellite tracks, flight paths) are inherently DYNAMIC and today fall to the per-frame fallback lane (per-entity interpolation on the CPU every frame). The high-scale answer is a GPU keyframe kernel on the `ComputeInstanceCollection` substrate (Phase 3) — upload the sample keyframes + times once to a storage buffer, interpolate position on the GPU per frame in the kernel, vertex-pull into the instanced draw. **The KERNEL half SHIPPED Batch 309 as NEW-SAMPLED-POSITION-KERNEL** (`Scene/SampledPositionKernel.js` — the reusable keyframe-interpolation kernel family: WGSL kernel + JS cpuKernel + `packInstance(keyframes,epoch)` packer + `floatsPerInstance` + `sample()` reference; linear interp + HOLD extrapolation, the GPU analogue of `SampledPositionProperty`, verified to 0.1 m against a CPU `SampledPositionProperty` on both backends — see that entry). **What REMAINS under THIS id** is the AUTO Entity→keyframe-buffer BRIDGE: a `BulkPathVisualizer`-style fast-path that detects `SampledPositionProperty`-positioned entities, harvests their sample keyframes into a `SampledPositionKernel` collection automatically, and preserves the Entity API + `scene.pick` returning the Entity (the analogue of `BulkPointVisualizer` for the static lane). That bridge — plus the Hermite/Lagrange interp option (NEW-SAMPLED-POSITION-KERNEL-HERMITE) needed to match a non-linear `SampledPositionProperty` — is the deferred remainder; the kernel + a hand-fed demo/probe are done.
- **NEW-ENTITYCLUSTER-GPU** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 301, GPU bin/count). `EntityCluster`'s screen-space proximity declutter (billboard/label/point markers) was a pure-CPU per-frame `new KDBush(...)` build (O(N log N)) plus a greedy range-query merge — doesn't scale to the 50k+ markers Phase 10 targets. The DATA-PARALLEL half (assign every visible screen-space point to a grid cell + count occupancy) is now offloaded to a single O(N) GPU compute pass on WebGPU: **`Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/EntityClusterGridGPU.wgsl`** hashes each point into a uniform screen-space grid whose cell edge equals the merge radius (`pixelRange`) and accumulates per-cell occupancy (`atomicAdd`) + a per-cell representative index (`atomicMin`) + a per-point cell-id. **`Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEntityClusterDispatcher.ts`** owns the buffers/pipeline + a one-frame-latency `mapAsync` readback and registers as the `ENTITY_CLUSTER_GPU` (slot 50) FeatureRenderer (`computeGrid`/`destroy`/`getStatistics`). **`DataSources/EntityClusterGPU.js`** (backend-agnostic — consulted ONLY via `context.getFeatureRenderer(ENTITY_CLUSTER_GPU)`, no `isWebGPU` branch) runs the SEQUENTIAL representative-selection + 3×3-neighbourhood merge on the CPU but over the reduced NON-EMPTY-cell set rather than every point, then `EntityCluster.js`'s declutter consumes it (one frame stale — declutter already lags the camera off `camera.changed`, so visually identical). WebGL2 never reaches the GPU branch and keeps the unchanged KDBush path. **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-entitycluster-gpu.mjs` (NEW, gate) — 2000 dense clusterable point entities cluster on BOTH backends (WebGL 48 reps, WebGPU 20 reps from 2000), zoom-out merges more aggressively (near→far 48→3 WebGL, 20→4 WebGPU), the GPU dispatcher actually ran (10 dispatches), parity within tolerance (ratio 0.42 — the grid merge is more aggressive at near zoom than the CPU bbox merge but is a valid declutter of the same set), 0 console errors on both. probe-collections-regression + probe-entity-bulk + probe-point-label-partial-write + probe-collections-2dcv-morph + sandcastle-smoke + upstream-regression-check all green; tsc + gulp build green. **Composes with Batch 300:** when clustering is enabled the bulk fast-path routes all points to the legacy lane (clustering re-positions primitives per frame), so the GPU cluster path operates on that lane's flat-buffer `PointPrimitiveCollection`. Follow-up: **NEW-ENTITYCLUSTER-GPU-MERGE** below.
- **NEW-ENTITYCLUSTER-GPU-MERGE** (L) — ⚠️ PARITY-TIGHTENING SHIPPED (Batch 308); full GPU connected-components STILL DEFERRED. The Batch-301 GPU path offloads the BINNING half (the O(N log N) → O(N) win) but the representative-selection + neighbour MERGE still reads back the per-cell aggregates and runs on the CPU over the non-empty cells. **What Batch 308 shipped (the parity half):** the CPU merge in `DataSources/EntityClusterGPU.js::clusterWithGrid` was over-aggressive — it absorbed the ENTIRE unclaimed 3×3 cell neighbourhood unconditionally, and a 3×3 block spans 3·pixelRange, so it merged points up to ~3× the merge radius apart → systematically FEWER representatives than the CPU KDBush path (probe parity ratio was 0.42; WebGPU 20 reps vs WebGL 48 from 2000 dense points). The absorb is now GATED on screen-space pixel distance to the seed — (a) a NEIGHBOUR cell only merges when its per-cell representative (`cellRep`, the GPU atomicMin index) is within `pixelRange` of the seed's representative (the requested rep-to-rep gate), and (b) within an absorbed cell only the individual members within `pixelRange` of the seed are pulled in (member-to-seed gate, mirroring the CPU bbox range query). The merge also switched from a per-CELL `claimed` array to per-POINT greedy claim-on-accept (claim only when a cluster meets `minimumClusterSize`, so a sub-threshold seed's members stay available to a denser later seed — exact CPU greedy semantics, and prevents the double-count a partial-cell-claim would cause). **Result:** parity ratio 0.42 → **1.02** (WebGPU 49 reps vs WebGL 48), far-count parity 4→3 (now both 3), no new readback (the merge still consumes the existing one-frame-stale grid — no per-frame stall added), 0 errors. `probe-entitycluster-gpu.mjs` parity band tightened 0.4–2.5 → **0.75–1.25**. **What is STILL DEFERRED (the GPU half):** moving the merge itself ONTO the GPU — a parallel union-find / connected-components pass over the grid (each non-empty cell links to its densest in-range neighbour, then a pointer-jump compaction emits cluster ids), producing the representative set GPU-resident with no per-cell readback. The output (representative world centroids + member counts) would then drive the cluster label/billboard/point collections directly — the centroid accumulation can stay GPU-side too via an RTE high/low atomic-sum into a per-cluster buffer. This remains a perf refinement (removes the per-cell readback for the very largest sets), not a correctness gap, and the cross-backend cluster-count parity it would need is now ALREADY achieved on the CPU consumer. The dispatcher's grid buffers (`cellCounts`/`cellRep`/`pointCellId`) are the scaffolding it builds on — they stay GPU-resident and are already the right inputs for the union-find.
- **NEW-WEBGPU-POINT-COLLECTION-PICK** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED / VERIFIED-WORKING (Batch 323). **Root cause: the consumer was NOT broken in the committed code — the entry's "producer pushed, consumer doesn't resolve" hypothesis (carried from the Batch-300/304 triage) was STALE.** A dedicated WebGPU pick-pass investigation (Batch 323) traced the full point-pick path against the working billboard path and found FULL PARITY: (1) the producer pushes a `pickOnly: true` point command with `pass: 8` (Pass.OPAQUE) — `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js::_pushPickCommand`; (2) `View.insertIntoBin` bins it into `frustumCommands.commands[Pass.OPAQUE]` by `command.pass`, identical to billboard; (3) the consumer — `WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts::executePickBatch` — dispatches it via the FORK-34 `cmdMarkers.pickOnly === true` branch (Batch 207) into the single-target pick FBO render pass, the same branch billboard takes; (4) the point pick pipeline targets `context.scenePipelineFormat` (single target, matching the pick FBO color) with `depth24plus-stencil8` depth (matching the pick FBO depth) — format-compatible, so no "attachment state not compatible" drop; (5) the WGSL pick shader (`PointPrimitivePick.wgsl`) reads `@location(2) pickColorIn` / `@location(3) showVec` at byte offsets 32/48, byte-consistent with the CPU `buildPickInstanceData` pack (pick color at floats 8-11, show at 12) and the shared `INSTANCE_BUFFER_LAYOUT`; (6) `point._pickId = context.createPickId(point, "point")` registers the id the same way billboard's `createPickId(bb, "billboard")` does, so `pickObjectsFromPixels` round-trips it. **The "returns undefined" symptom in the original triage was the COLD synchronous-pick staleness, NOT a point-specific defect:** WebGPU readback is async, so `scene.pick()` (the SYNC API) returns the PREVIOUS frame's pick-FBO pixels via `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.end()` (one-frame-stale by design). The very first sync pick on a fresh pick FBO returns `undefined` for ANY primitive — a side-by-side BILLBOARD control exhibits the IDENTICAL cold-null then warms to its id, proving point is at parity, not special. **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-point-pick-webgpu.mjs` (NEW, gate) — a raw `PointPrimitiveCollection` (one 50px point, `id`) + a billboard control on `?renderer=webgpu`: warmed `scene.pick` (sync) AND `pickAsync` both return the PointPrimitive with `id` round-tripped (asserted `id === "probe-point-1"`), the billboard control resolves identically, an empty-space pick returns `undefined`, 0 console/WebGPU-validation errors. A standalone WebGL-vs-WebGPU literal repro confirmed WebGL cold-picks immediately (sync readback) while WebGPU cold-picks `null` then warm-picks the id — the documented async-readback delta, shared with billboard. A 3-distinct-points-at-3-distinct-pixels check resolved to 3 distinct ids (`p0`/`p1`/`p2`), proving the per-instance pick color + readback sample the correct pixel. `PointPrimitiveCollectionSpec` (67 specs incl. `is picked` / `can change pick id` / `is not picked` / scaleByDistance + translucencyByDistance pick) all green via Edge; tsc --noEmit clean; gulp build exit 0. **No source change required** — the feature was already correct; this batch closes the entry with a regression gate + verified root cause. WebGL pick path untouched.
- **NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-COLD-SYNC-STALENESS** (M, surfaced Batch 323) — ✅ **RESOLVED via documentation + guidance (Batch 361, 2026-06-23).** The FIRST synchronous `scene.pick()` against a freshly-rendered pick FBO returns `undefined` on WebGPU for ANY primitive type (point/billboard/model): WebGPU readback is async, so `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.end()` submits the copy for the current pick's location but returns the PREVIOUS pick's pixels (`_lastReadPixels`); the first pick has no previous result → empty. **The "forced sync readback" parity option is INFEASIBLE:** WebGPU has no synchronous GPU→CPU readback (`mapAsync` resolves only on a future event-loop tick, and a browser can't synchronously block on a promise), so `scene.pick` cannot read the current frame's pick result in-call on WebGPU. Prewarming doesn't help either — `_lastReadPixels` is LOCATION-specific (the last scissor region), so priming it at init would make the first user pick return the *primed* location's object rather than the clicked location's (a wrong answer, worse than undefined). **Resolution (the only correct one):** (1) `scene.pick` JSDoc now documents the WebGPU one-frame-stale / cold-first-pick semantics and steers one-off/click-driven callers to `scene.pickAsync` (which `await`s the readback and always returns the correct current-frame result); (2) a one-time latched `console.warn` in `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.end()` fires on the cold path (`!_lastReadPixels`) with the same guidance. The common hover-then-click pattern is already warm by click time (the prior frame's hover primed the cursor location), so the practical impact is limited to standalone programmatic picks. Files: `Scene/Scene.js` (JSDoc + `@see pickAsync`), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts` (`_coldPickWarned` latch). Gate: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-point-pick-webgpu.mjs` (the existing WebGL-vs-WebGPU cold/warm repro confirms warm picks resolve + the cold-null is expected).

### Phase 12 — med/low bug-bash (Batch 304, 2026-06-15)

- **NEW-USEWEBMERCATORT-SINGLE-SOURCE** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 304). The Mercator-vs-geographic imagery projection decision was computed in TWO places that could disagree: `getOrCreateImageryTexture` (in `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts`) bound a variant via a rich decision tree (merc cache hit → merc texture → geo cache → reprojected texture → race-window merc → direct upload) and returned `isMercator`, while the tile-UB packer (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts`) INDEPENDENTLY recomputed the shader's `useWebMercatorTLayer` flag as `tileImagery.useWebMercatorT && !!imagery._webgpuMercatorTexture`. That local recompute missed the cache-hit and Mercator→geographic-fall-through and race-window cases, so in the streaming/race windows the shader's V-coordinate space could disagree with the actually-bound texture's projection → a misprojected imagery strip until steady-state. **Fix:** added a pure peek `resolveImageryProjection(host, tileImagery)` that returns `{ variant: "merc" | "geo" | "upload", isMercator }` — the SINGLE authority for the decision. `getOrCreateImageryTexture` now honors its `variant` for which branch to bind; the tile-UB packer derives `effectiveUseWebMercatorT` from `resolveImageryProjection(...)?.isMercator`. Pure (no uploads / no cache writes), idempotent, and both consumers see the same per-imagery texture fields (`_webgpuMercatorTexture`/`_webgpuReprojectedTexture` are stable across a frame), so binding + flag + cached translation/scale coordinate-space can no longer diverge. `TileUBHost extends TextureCacheHost` so the packer can call it (the renderer `this` already satisfies both). **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-phase12-bugbash.mjs` item (1) — globe + Mercator(default-Bing-tiling) imagery renders top-down with healthy color diversity (nonBlack 99.9%, 446 distinct colors) on WebGPU; probe-globe-bindgroup-cache (imagery texture binding) + probe-logdepth-zfight (globe render) green.
- **NEW-UPLOADIMAGESOURCE-OBSERVABILITY** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 304). `uploadImageSource` (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTextures.ts`) ended in `catch (e) { return null; }`, swallowing ALL errors — a `createTexture`/`copyExternalImageToTexture` throw silently blanked the tile with no signal. The transient undecoded-`<img>` case is ALREADY handled by an early `!source.complete` return BEFORE the try, and unsupported source types are rejected before it, so reaching the catch signals a genuine fault (OOM, out-of-bounds size, lost device). **Fix:** the catch now emits a PERMANENT (non-pragma) `console.error("[CesiumJS:webgpu] uploadImageSource failed for \"<key>\": <message>")` then returns null (the caller's cache-miss retry still covers recoverable cases). Deliberately does NOT re-throw — device loss is already routed through the `device.lost` promise in `WebGPUContextDeviceLoss`/`WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery`; a synchronous throw from this globe-render hot path would crash the frame loop instead of letting that async recovery engage. **VERIFY:** probe item (2) asserts ZERO `uploadImageSource failed` errors across a full WebGPU tile-streaming pan on a healthy device (the error is for faults, not the normal retry).
- **NEW-RAYSPHERE-PRECISION-BACKPORT** (L) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 304). The WGSL `GlobeTerrain.wgsl::raySphereIntersectionInterval` already scaled the ray origin by 1/radius to keep all intermediates in the [-10, 10] f32-stable range (the naive `c = dot(oc, oc) - radius*radius` loses ~10 m of precision at Cesium scale because `dot(oc, oc)` ≈ `radius*radius` ≈ 4e13, beyond f32's 2^24 mantissa integer range). The GLSL builtin `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval` (`Builtin/Functions/raySphereIntersectionInterval.glsl`) still used the naive form. **Fix:** ported the 1/radius scaling into the GLSL builtin, preserving the GENERAL (non-normalized-direction) form: dividing the whole quadratic by radius² gives `A = a/radius²`, `B = b/radius²`, and the precision-stable `C = dot(ocScaled, ocScaled) - 1` (the radius² factor cancels in the root ratio so t stays in world units). Benefits ALL GLSL ray-sphere consumers (sky atmosphere `AtmosphereCommon.glsl` / `computeScattering.glsl`, ground atmosphere, `SkyAtmosphereCommon.glsl`, `ComputeRadianceMapFS.glsl`). Numerically verified f64-equivalent to the original across normalized / non-normalized / oblique Cesium-scale inputs (the win is f32-hardware-only). **VERIFY:** probe item (3) runs on the WebGL renderer (the path that COMPILES the modified GLSL — WebGPU uses the already-fixed WGSL): full-disc view from 22,000 km, the sky-atmosphere ring (produced via `czm_raySphereIntersectionInterval`) renders a smooth blue ring (limbBlue 16.5%, no NaN/black wedge).
- **NEW-BILLBOARD-UPDATEMODE-ORDERING** (M) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 304). `BillboardCollection.update()` called `updateMode(this, frameState)` TWICE per frame: once inside `runSharedSceneLogic` (top of `update()`, where it MUST run so the WebGPU label/billboard feature-renderer path gets `_baseVolume`/`_baseVolume2D` seeded) and AGAIN at the old line ~770 in the WebGL path. After the first call `_mode === mode` but `_createVertexArray` was set true, so the second call re-entered and re-ran `recomputeActualPositions` to no visible effect — a redundant per-frame billboard walk. Upstream calls `updateMode` exactly once (last, after the capability + texture-undefined guards). **Fix:** dropped the redundant second call (left a comment explaining the shared call already ran it). The WebGL2 capability guard + texture-undefined guard stay AFTER the feature-renderer branch (they are WebGL-only — WebGPU must not throw on `!context.instancedArrays`), so they could not move above the FR branch as the raw finding text suggested; the genuine defect was the double-call. **VERIFY:** probe item (4) — a billboard cluster renders on WebGPU after the dedup (magenta 4282); probe-billboard-partial-write (vertex pipeline) + probe-point-label-partial-write + probe-collections-2dcv-morph (mode-switch `updateMode` path: billboard GL/GPU ratio ~0.99 across 3D/2D/CV) all green.
- **DP-H47** — CONFIRMED REAL + SCOPED (Batch 304), see the full entry in the DATA_PIPELINE section below. Not a bug-bash-sized fix; tracked as the next atmosphere-uniform-consistency work item.
- **NEW-WEBGPU-POINT-COLLECTION-PICK** — re-triaged Batch 304 as a pick-readback investigation (NOT a small map-back); RESOLVED Batch 323 — the investigation found the consumer already at parity with billboard (the "doesn't resolve" hypothesis was stale; the symptom was cold-sync-pick async-readback staleness shared by ALL primitives). See the ✅ SHIPPED / VERIFIED-WORKING entry above.

### Phase 4 / Phase 13 — ECS-in-WASM-on-worker — ❌ CLOSED AS NOT-NEEDED (Batch 305, NO-GO gate)

- **NEW-ECS-WORKER-GATING-SPIKE** (M) — ✅ DONE (Batch 305) → **NO-GO**. The gating measurement is complete: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-mainthread-encode-ceiling.mjs` drives the flat-buffer substrate (`BufferPointCollection`'s RTE position-encode + GPU-upload path — the same substrate the compute-instance WebGL2 cpuKernel and the Batch-300 entity bulk fast-path share) with a FULL-collection arbitrary position update EVERY frame (regime-2 worst case), at 10k/50k/100k/250k on BOTH backends, and fits the per-object cost to derive the 60fps/30fps objects-per-frame ceiling. **Result (conservative JS-fround encode path; the SIMD kernel does not load in the bundled build, NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD, and would only RAISE these numbers):**
  - **OFFLOADABLE encode+upload ceiling** (the ONLY cost a worker removes from the main thread): **WebGPU ~89k @60fps / ~187k @30fps**; **WebGL ~77k @60fps / ~154k @30fps** objects/frame. This COMFORTABLY COVERS the "tens of thousands of arbitrary per-frame updates" target (≥20k @60fps) on both backends with the encode alone, before any worker.
  - **End-to-end ceiling** (nudge/sim loop + render) is lower (~19-22k @60fps) but that is **56-65% dominated by the synthetic per-object position MUTATION (the nudge loop)** — the harness's stand-in for SIMULATION/INTEGRATION work. A worker does NOT eliminate that cost; it RELOCATES it to the worker thread (the worker still integrates every object every frame). Gating on the end-to-end number would wrongly credit the worker with removing work it merely moves. The honest gate is the offloadable encode+upload ceiling, which COVERS.
  - **Conclusion:** regime 2 (flat-buffer + main-thread encode) covers ARBITRARY per-frame updates to tens of thousands of objects at 60fps without a worker; regime 3 (GPU-compute, SHIPPED — orbital catalog propagates 1M GPU-resident instances/frame) covers the GPU-resident millions AND the case where SIMULATION itself is the bottleneck (it moves both sim and encode to the GPU). **There is no uncovered "regime 4" workload band that a worker-owned ECS would serve.** Therefore the entire ECS-on-worker phase is CLOSED as not-needed.
- **NEW-ECS-HEADLESS-WORKER-SPIKE** (M) — ❌ CLOSED NOT-NEEDED (Batch 305). The transfer-cost-vs-main-thread spike is moot: the gating measurement shows the main thread already sustains the target arbitrary-per-frame encode without a worker, so there is no main-thread cost the worker needs to beat. (If a future workload genuinely exceeds regime-2 on the encode axis AND cannot use regime-3 GPU-compute, re-open and run this transfer spike first.)
- **NEW-ECS-SUBSTRATE** (L) — ❌ CLOSED NOT-NEEDED (Batch 305). Greenfield ECS framework was conditional on the gating spike justifying a worker; the spike returned NO-GO. High over-build risk avoided.
- **NEW-COOP-COEP-SAB-ENABLE** (M) — ❌ CLOSED NOT-NEEDED for the ECS phase (Batch 305). The SharedArrayBuffer flip was needed only to make the worker's zero-copy promise real; with no worker, no SAB requirement from this track. (NOTE: COOP/COEP/SAB may still be wanted independently by other subsystems — `SharedResourcePool`/`SOABoundingSphereLayout`/`WasmCullBridge` fall back to `ArrayBuffer` without it — so this ID can be re-opened under a DIFFERENT driver, but it is no longer an ECS-phase blocker.)
- **NEW-ECS-WASM-KERNEL** (L) — ❌ CLOSED NOT-NEEDED (Batch 305). The hot-systems-in-WASM-on-worker kernel (the most fragile SAB-in-WASM-in-worker combination) is unbuilt and unneeded per the NO-GO. The encode itself already has a WASM kernel path on the main thread (`WasmRTEBridge.batchEncodeRange`); when its bundle-load gap (NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD) is fixed it raises the main-thread ceiling further, reinforcing NO-GO.
- **NEW-ECS-RENDER-UPLOAD-BRIDGE** (L) — ❌ CLOSED NOT-NEEDED (Batch 305). No worker output to wire back; the existing `BufferPointCollection._positionView` / `_renderContext` (WebGL2) + WebGPU storage/instance upload already serve the main-thread path measured here.
- **NEW-ECS-PRODUCTIONIZE** (L) — ❌ CLOSED NOT-NEEDED (Batch 305). The long tail (worker lifecycle/crash-recovery, worker-entity picking, compaction, WebGL2 fallback) only existed to productionize a worker the gate says not to build.

**Re-open criteria (all must hold):** a real workload requires ARBITRARY per-frame CPU updates to MORE than the measured ~77-89k-objects-@60fps offloadable ceiling (after the SIMD kernel lands, which raises it), AND that workload's simulation cannot be expressed as a GPU-compute kernel (regime 3 — which would be the cheaper answer anyway), AND the per-frame postMessage/transfer cost (run NEW-ECS-HEADLESS-WORKER-SPIKE first) is provably smaller than the main-thread saving. Until then: regimes 2 + 3 cover the realistic target.

## ADR-2026-04-28: Classification architecture — depth-sampling over stencil

**Decision:** Migrate `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer` from its current 2-pass stencil approach to WebGL's depth-texture sampling architecture. Pause the original C-R8 multi-frustum sweep (Sessions 2–4 of the stencil plan) until the depth-sampling architecture lands. After the migration, the multi-frustum work folds in for free as "swap the depth-source view per frustum" rather than "redirect a render pass into a scratch FBO and accumulate stencil bits."

**Why:**

- **Feature coverage.** Stencil approach can only classify against opaque surfaces that wrote depth. The depth-sampling approach can swap which depth source it reads from, unlocking translucent-on-translucent classification, PointCloud translucent classification (Batch 79 only fixed Models via selective depth-write), and `GroundPolylinePrimitive` (currently absent on WebGPU) on the same plumbing.
- **Architectural coherence with WebGL.** WebGL's classifier (`ShadowVolumeAppearanceFS.glsl`, `PolylineShadowVolumeFS.glsl`) samples `czm_globeDepthTexture`. Maintaining two architectures in parallel (stencil for WebGPU, depth-sample for WebGL) costs more long-term than one unified architecture.
- **Calendar.** Either path is ~5–6 sessions: finish stencil-based multi-frustum (Sessions 2–4) + later migrate, vs. migrate first + multi-frustum falls out for free. Same calendar, different end state.

**Trade-offs accepted:**

- Per-fragment cost goes up modestly (one depth-texture sample + reconstruction multiply) versus stencil's fixed-function early rejection. On desktop GPUs the delta benchmarks within ~2-3%; on mobile/integrated GPUs it can reach 5-15% in classification-heavy scenes. Acceptable for Cesium's typical workloads (terrain visualization, not mobile games).
- LOC churn: ~+800 LOC of WGSL classification shaders, ~-200 LOC of stencil pipeline plumbing. Net code growth, but a single conceptual surface.
- Sandcastle baseline regenerates after the cutover (visual regression suite is the safety net).

**Stays unchanged:**

- `depth24plus-stencil8` attachment format. The format's stencil bits are still used by `WebGPUInvertClassification` (separate concern, no migration plan today). Switching to `depth24plus` saves zero bytes per pixel on most drivers.
- Edge / shadow / OIT / picking pipelines — none of these use stencil today.
- The Batch 47 `WebGPUTranslucentTileClassification` scaffolding is the canonical example of the depth-pack approach in this codebase. The migration finally turns that scaffolding into the production classifier.

**Re-sequenced plan (replaces the earlier 6-session C-R8 sweep):**

1. **Migration Session 1** — WGSL port of `ShadowVolumeAppearanceVS/FS` + companion uniforms + first-cut single-pipeline `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer` swap that samples `globeDepthTexture` instead of doing the stencil 2-pass. Keep stencil pipelines compiled but unused as a one-batch fallback.
2. **Migration Session 2** — Runtime depth-source swap (globe-depth ↔ packed-translucent-depth). Wire the Batch 47 `_packedTranslucentDepthView` as the secondary source. Closes C-R8-CLASSIFICATION-DEPTH-SAMPLING and absorbs C-R8-TRANSLUCENT-CLASSIFICATION-DISPATCH.
3. **Migration Session 3** — Per-frustum FBO redirect now becomes "per-frustum depth-source bind group." Closes C-R8-TRANSLUCENT-MULTI-FRUSTUM. Composite + accumulation are no-ops (the depth-sample approach doesn't need them).
4. **Migration Session 4** — `WebGPUGroundPolylineRenderer` (port `PolylineShadowVolumeVS/FS` to WGSL). Reuses the Session 2 depth-source plumbing. Closes C-R8-GROUND-POLYLINE-NATIVE.
5. **Migration Session 5** — Delete unused stencil pipelines from `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer`. Drop the Batch 47 composite scaffolding (`composite()`, `_compositePipeline`, `COMPOSITE_WGSL`, `_runTranslucentTileClassificationComposite`) — the depth-sample architecture doesn't need it.

**Origin:** Audit + senior-dev review on 2026-04-28 after Batch 79 fixed the user-visible Model translucent-tile classification bug via selective depth-write. The audit revealed the stencil approach was a local minimum and the multi-frustum sweep would re-architect the wrong surface. See conversation transcript at `eb6dfaec-c294-4f46-966a-d8d9138c8bf0` for the full reasoning.

## C-R1 - command.renderState adoption tail

**Parent finding (PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_RENDERER_DEEP_2026_04_16.md:30):** `RenderStateToPipelineVariant.ts` foundation + 7 consumer renderers landed in Batches 30/35-37/39. Four named gaps remain.

### ~~C-R1-CLASSIFICATION~~ — RESOLVED via architectural retirement (Migration Session 5, Batch 85; doc sync Batch 176)

**Original framing:** Classification primitives (ClassificationPrimitive, GroundPolylinePrimitive) need their multi-pass renderState (stencil-depth pass, color pass, pick pass) routed through pipeline variants. Each pass uses distinct stencil/colorMask/depthFunc so WebGPU has to materialize three pipelines and dispatch in order. The audit anticipated needing a new `WebGPUClassificationPrimitiveRenderer` alongside the existing `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer`.

**Resolution:** The 3-pass stencil-depth technique was **intentionally retired** during Migration Session 5 (Batch 85, ~2026-04-22). The technique is now compiled-but-dormant scaffolding in `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js` lines 7-26 (documents the migration) and lines 97-102 (confirms: "the legacy stencil VS/FS, color VS/FS... were removed alongside their pipeline descriptors. The depth-sample dsColor/dsPick path is now the only classification path"). The replacement `dsColor`/`dsPick` pipelines sample the globe-depth texture (via the effects bind group at `@group(3) @binding(15)`) and discard fragments that don't have a classifiable surface — single-pass, no stencil dance, simpler architecturally.

`WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer.js` covers BOTH `ClassificationPrimitive` and `GroundPrimitive` via the depth-sample classifier; no separate `WebGPUClassificationPrimitiveRenderer` was needed (the audit's anticipated split didn't materialize). `Vector3DTilePrimitive` / `Vector3DTilePolylines` / `Vector3DTileClampedPolylines` follow the same depth-sample pattern in their own renderers.

**Doc-sync note:** This entry stayed flagged as "open" through Batches 85-175 because the doc reconciliation lagged the architectural pivot. Batch 176 audit confirmed the retirement and updated the entry. No code change required.

**Trace:** PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_RENDERER_DEEP_2026_04_16.md:30 (original framing); Migration Session 5 / Batch 85 (architectural pivot); Batch 176 (doc reconciliation).

### ~~C-R1-COLLECTIONS-PER-ENCODER~~ — RESOLVED (audit 2026-05-02)

**Audit finding (AUDIT_2026_05_02.md D.2):** All five collection renderers forward `renderState` onto their commands today: `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js:884`, `WebGPULabelRenderer.js:724`, `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js:852/991`, `WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js:1112/1273`, `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts:596`. `WebGPUDrawCommand.execute()` at `WebGPUDrawCommand.ts:500-504` automatically calls `applyPerEncoderState(passEncoder, this.renderState)` when defined. Custom stencilRef / blendConstant / scissor flow correctly.

**Status:** No code change needed; entry preserved as a marker so future audits don't re-investigate.

### ~~C-R1-GLOBE-RENDERSTATE~~ — RESOLVED (Batches 99 + 177 + 182 + 183, doc-sync Batch 219)

All three sub-issues now closed:

- **cullFace** — shipped Batch 99 (`WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:316` derives `disableCulling` and selects `cullMode`).
- **depthMask** — re-audit (Batch 175) confirmed this was never a real gap: the upstream provider always pairs `depthMask = false` with `blending = ALPHA_BLEND`, and the WebGPU heuristic `!isBlend` produces the byte-correct depth-write state for every globe translucency variant.
- **colorMask** — folded into `NEW-GLOBE-TRANSLUCENCY-MULTI-PASS`, which shipped end-to-end in Batches 177 + 182 + 183. The depth-only back-face pre-pass + cull-separated translucent passes use the WebGPU equivalent of `colorMask = false` via `writeMask: 0` on the pipeline's color target.

Batch 219 doc-sync only — code already in place.

**What:** `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts` builds pipeline variants from locally-derived state rather than consuming a literal upstream `command.renderState` blob. The original audit framed this as "the provider sets per-tile depthMask / cullFace, the WebGPU path overrides."

**Resolution (cullFace, Batch 99):** `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:316` reads `disableCulling` from the renderer's per-frame derivation (cameraUnderground OR globeTranslucent OR `tileProvider.backFaceCulling === false`) and selects between `cullMode: "none"` and `cullMode: "back"`. Mirrors WebGL's `_renderState` vs `_disableCullingRenderState` selection in `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1226-1231`. The renderer path doesn't dispatch from `command.renderState` because the WebGPU globe surface renderer builds its own `WebGPUDrawCommand`s directly — the variant flags are the intentional pattern, not the WebGL command-dispatcher RS pattern.

**Re-audit finding (Batch 175):** Pre-Batch-175 the entry framed `depthWriteEnabled: !isBlend` at `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:321` as "ignoring upstream depthMask." Code inspection of `GlobeTranslucencyState.js:720-741` and `GlobeSurfaceTileProvider.js:364-382` shows the upstream provider ALWAYS pairs `depthMask = false` with `blending = ALPHA_BLEND` — the WebGPU heuristic `!isBlend` thus produces the byte-correct depth-write state for every globe translucency variant. **No depthMask gap to close** until the provider's pattern changes; if it does, the same derivation pattern Batch 99 used for cullFace can be added.

**Genuine remaining gap (rescoped):** `GlobeTranslucencyState.js:720-727` sets `colorMask = { red: false, green: false, blue: false, alpha: false }` for the depth-only back-face-only pass (depth pre-pass for translucent globe rendering). The WebGPU globe renderer doesn't currently emit this auxiliary depth-only pass — the entire globe-translucency multi-pass technique (depth-only back-face → translucent back-face → translucent front-face) isn't yet implemented. Filed as `NEW-GLOBE-TRANSLUCENCY-MULTI-PASS` for the dedicated work.

**Trace:** PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_RENDERER_DEEP_2026_04_16.md:30; Batch 99 cullFace; Batch 175 re-audit + rescope; Batch 176 deeper inspection of existing scaffolding.

### ~~NEW-GLOBE-TRANSLUCENCY-MULTI-PASS~~ — depth-only pre-pass + cull-separated translucent back/front passes for translucent globe rendering — RESOLVED (Batches 177 + 182 + 183)

**Resolution:** Shipped as direct command emission from `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer` rather than fixing the broken `WebGPUGlobeTranslucencyState` scaffolding. The 3-pass technique now fires per tile when `globeTranslucent && !cameraUnderground` and the regular color command flips to `cullMode: "back"`.

- **Batch 177** — Depth-only back-face pre-pass. New `selectDepthOnlyBackFacePipelineHelper` in `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts` builds a variant with `cullMode: "front"`, `depthWriteEnabled: true`, `colorWriteMask: 0`, no blend. Cache-key suffix `_DOB`. Emitted before the regular imagery-layer command when `globeTranslucent && !isSubsequentPass && !debugWireframe && debugFragmentMode === NONE`.
- **Batch 182** — Translucent back-face command + culling-decision split. `selectTranslucentBackFacePipeline` builds a variant with `cullMode: "front"`, `depthWriteEnabled: false`, `blend: ALPHA_BLEND`. Cache-key suffix `_TBF`. Emitted between the depth-only pre-pass and the regular color command. The `disableCulling` decision split out `globeTranslucent` so the regular color command flips from `cullMode: "none"` to `cullMode: "back"` (front-face only) — completing the 3-pass technique.
- **Batch 183 fix** — 3-pass emission gate at `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:871-876` extended with `!cameraUnderground` so the underground-and-translucent case correctly takes the legacy single-pass both-faces path (the user's primary intent when underground is "see through the globe", which the 3-pass technique would double-blend).

**Why we pivoted away from the existing `WebGPUGlobeTranslucencyState` scaffolding:** The pre-existing scaffolding mutates `cmd._blendEnabled` / `_depthWriteEnabled` / `_cullMode` between executions, which is non-functional for WebGPU because pipelines bake those fields at creation. Direct command emission with pre-built pipeline variants per cull-mode is the correct WebGPU shape; the broken scaffolding is left in place as forward-looking infrastructure for the eventual `MANUAL_DEPTH_TEST` multi-frustum overlap case (deferred — see C-R8-TRANSLUCENT-MULTI-FRUSTUM).

**Trace:** Batches 177, 182, 183. `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:511, 871-948`; `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:buildPipelineDescriptor` (`depthOnlyBackFace`, `translucentBackFace` flags + `_DOB`/`_TBF` cache-key suffixes).

### ~~GLOBE-TRANSLUCENCY-ALPHA~~ — front/back alpha + translucencyByDistance threaded into the globe FS + sky translucent path — RESOLVED (2026-07-02)

**Resolution:** The 9 derived blend/cull/depth variants existed (Batches 177/182/183) but the ALPHA VALUES never reached the FS, and the front-face color command selected the OPAQUE pipeline on pass 0 — an enabled translucent globe still composited opaque. Five coordinated changes:

1. **Camera UB tail (+12 floats, 180 → 192)** — `translucencyFrontAlphaByDistance` / `translucencyBackAlphaByDistance` (NearFarScalar packed `(near, nearValue, far, farValue)`, camera-underground swap pre-applied per `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1487-1492`) + `translucencyControl` (x = the WebGL TRANSLUCENT define analogue). All-zero when off. `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTypes.ts`.
2. **Tile UB tail (+4 floats, 480 → 484)** — `localizedTranslucencyRectangle` (antimeridian-clipped `globe.translucency.rectangle` localized to tile UV via the shared `clipRectangleAntimeridian`). `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts`.
3. **GlobeTerrain.wgsl FS** — port of GlobeFS.glsl lines 746-751: inside the rectangle, `alpha *= interpolateByDistance(frontFacing ? front : back, v_distance)`, gated on `translucencyControl.x`.
4. **Front-face pipeline selection** — `isBlend = isSubsequentPass || globeTranslucent` in `createTileCommands` (was `isSubsequentPass` only) so the translucent front face uses the ALPHA-blend/depth-write-off variant, matching WebGL's `getTranslucentFrontFaceRenderState`. **Pass-structure split to match WebGL's `getDerivedCommandTypes`:** the DOB + TBF 3-pass now fires only when `backTranslucent` (`_backFaceTranslucent`); the default opaque-back case (backFaceAlpha = 1) instead emits a NEW depth-only FRONT-face pre-pass (`selectDepthOnlyFrontFacePipeline`, `_DOF` cache suffix — mirrors WebGL's DEPTH_ONLY_FRONT_FACE keeping scene depth populated). WebGL's OPAQUE_BACK_FACE sibling is deliberately NOT mirrored: WebGL z-rejects it everywhere (base depth func LESS at equal depth); WebGPU's less-equal would wrongly draw the globe underside.
5. **SkyAtmosphere.wgsl** — port of the GLSL `GLOBE_TRANSLUCENT` path (SkyAtmosphereCommon.glsl:63-90) as a runtime gate on `u.atmosControl.w` (previously reserved lane; packed from `globeTranslucencyState.translucent`): planet-intersecting sky rays get the dark distance-faded navy horizon gradient instead of the full scattering integral. Without this the WGSL sky flooded the see-through planet disk with bright daylight blue (terrain scenario diff 99.8% → 22.9%).

**Verify:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-globe-translucency.mjs` (NEW, gate) — off-default (off-gate, 24.5% ≈ standing residual), translucent-space (21.2%), translucent-terrain (22.9%, below the 24.5% standing baseline). Luminance-response check: WebGPU mean lum tracks alpha like WebGL (alpha 1/0.5/0.05 → 104/53/7.7 vs WebGL 92/45/4.1; ratios 1/0.51/0.07 vs 1/0.50/0.045). `probe-globe-underground.mjs` + `probe-atmosphere-toggle.mjs` regressions green.

**Residuals (minor, tracked):**

- A faint tile-aligned brighter veil on parts of the WebGPU translucent terrain view — consistent with blend commands executing in BOTH frustums of the multi-frustum split (depth-write-off blend double-applies in the overlap bins; WebGL bins/splits differently). Within the standing residual; revisit if a probe isolates it above tolerance. Related: C-R8-TRANSLUCENT-MULTI-FRUSTUM.
- The `backTranslucent` (backFaceAlpha < 1) 3-pass path now carries the alpha values but has no dedicated parity probe; WebGL uses DEPTH_ONLY_FRONT_AND_BACK_FACE there where WebGPU keeps its Batch-177 depth-only BACK pre-pass.
- TRANSLUCENT_`*`_MANUAL_DEPTH_TEST variants (types 7/8) remain unwired (pre-existing; see C-R8-TRANSLUCENT-MULTI-FRUSTUM).

### ~~C-R1-PRIMITIVE-DERIVED~~ EFFECTIVELY RESOLVED (audit 2026-05-02)

**Audit finding:**

- The `pickCommand` paths (both shader-path and material-path) in `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` already forward `appearance.renderState` — Batch 98 landed this. See `pickCommand` construction at `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js:1502-1535` (shader path) and `:2326-2354` (material path), both with `renderState: appearance?.renderState` and explanatory comments. So per-encoder dynamic state (stencilRef, scissor, viewport, blendConstant) flows through pick passes.
- `depthOnlyCommand` and `pickDepthCommand` are NOT emitted by the WebGPU primitive flow — and **have no consumer in the WebGPU dispatch path.** WebGPU primitives use a parallel-array shape (`colorCommands[]` + `pickCommands[]`) rather than the WebGL per-command derived-dictionary shape. The dispatcher in `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:188` checks `derivedCommands.depth.depthOnlyCommand` as a fallback, but no Pass dispatch in the WebGPU `executeFrustumLoop` invokes primitives in depth-only mode (shadow casting goes through `executeShadowMapCastCommands` + the dedicated CSM cast pass; globeDepth uses `executeUpdateDepth` which copies post-render). Adding `depthOnlyCommand` emission would be scaffolding without a consumer.

**Status:** Pick variant renderState forwarding is complete. Depth-only variant emission has no consumer to plumb to. Per the dead-code audit rule (CLAUDE.md), not adding scaffolding without a consumer.

**If/when needed:** A future depth-only primitive dispatch (e.g., a real early-z prepass landing for performance) would need both the consumer-side dispatcher hook AND the producer-side `depthOnlyCommand` emission. They should land together.

**Trace:** PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_RENDERER_DEEP_2026_04_16.md:30; Batch 98 (pick variant renderState); audit 2026-05-02.

- **NEW-PANORAMA-CULL-OVERRIDE-WEBGPU** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 317, `2ee9421571`). `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` now derives the pipeline `cullMode` from the appearance's `renderState.cull.{enabled,face}` (→ `'none'` when `enabled===false`) before the `closed`-based fallback, cache-key in sync; an inside-viewed `EquirectangularPanorama` is now VISIBLE on WebGPU (WebGL parity). **Pre-fix gap analysis retained for context:** (M, found by WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06; upstream #13369) — **NOTE: distinct from C-R1-PRIMITIVE-DERIVED above, which is scoped to depth-only/pick renderState forwarding and explicitly EXCLUDES pipeline-cull derivation.** The #13369 `flat:true` lighting fix IS honored on WebGPU (`matImageFlat` selected — tracked SHIPPED as NEW-UPSTREAM-PANORAMA-LIGHTING-13369), but the WebGPU material pipeline in `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` baked `cullMode` SOLELY from `appearance.closed` and ignored the appearance's `renderState.cull.enabled:false`. So an `EquirectangularPanorama` viewed from INSIDE the sphere showed back faces, and `closed:true` forced `cullMode:'back'` → the panorama was INVISIBLE on WebGPU while WebGL (which honors `cull.enabled:false`) showed it. Fix: derive the pipeline `cullMode` from the appearance's `renderState.cull.{enabled,face}` (→ `'none'` when `enabled===false`) BEFORE falling back to the `closed`-based default, keeping the cache-key in sync. **Files:** `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js`. **Trace:** WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md (P2 "EquirectangularPanorama cull-override (renderState.cull.enabled:false)"); upstream #13369; sibling NEW-UPSTREAM-PANORAMA-LIGHTING-13369 (lighting half, SHIPPED Batch 299).
- **NEW-BUFFERPOLYGON-2DCV-REPROJECT** (L, found by WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06) — ✅ **MOSTLY SHIPPED (PARITY-BUFFER-2DCV, 2026-07-01).** **NOTE: distinct from NEW-CLASSIFIER-2D-CV-MORPH (FEATURE_INVENTORY §B.3 :517–518), which covers the `.vctr` `Vector3DTile*` classifiers, NOT the `BufferPolygon` family.** The three Buffer* WebGPU renderers now reproject ECEF→scene-mode positions in 2D / Columbus View / Morph via a shared `projectBufferPositionForMode` helper (`WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts`) that wraps `SceneTransforms.computeActualEllipsoidPosition` (`.zxy` swizzle for CV, `(0,x,y)` for 2D, CPU morph lerp for MORPHING) — mirroring the shipped `WebGPUPolylineRenderer` / `PolylineCollection` convention. Each renderer (a) enters the reproject path ONLY when `frameState.mode !== SCENE3D` (SCENE3D byte-identical — the batch WASM encode stays active, the position is a no-op clone), (b) forces a full re-pack when the scene-mode/morph projection frame changes (`bufferModeNeedsRepack`, keyed on cache `_lastPackMode`/`_lastPackMorphTime`), and (c) builds a settled-2D/CV coplanar-depth pipeline variant (`depthCompare:"always"`, no depth write, via `computeNoDepthTest` from `WebGPUCollectionRendererBase`) so the flat-map fill draws on top without z-fighting. **Also fixed a pre-existing blocker found during this work:** the `BufferPolyline` pipeline declared **9 vertex buffers** (over WebGPU's guaranteed `maxVertexBuffers`=8) → `createRenderPipeline` returned an INVALID pipeline, so ANY frame containing a BufferPolyline was dropped with a validation error (blocked all BufferPolyline rendering on WebGPU, ALL modes incl. 3D). Fixed by interleaving loc7 (`showColorWidthAndTexCoord` vec4) + loc8 (`alpha` f32) into ONE stride-20 buffer (8 buffers total; WGSL unchanged). **Verified** (`Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffer-2dcv-parity.mjs`, PNGs READ): points+polyline+polygon all render in SCENE3D + Columbus View; points+polygon render in SCENE2D. **Residual → NEW-BUFFERPOLYLINE-2D-EXTRUSION** (below). **Files:** `WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBufferPointRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBufferPolylineRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBufferPolygonRenderer.ts`. **Trace:** WEBGPU_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md (P2 "Vector-tile buffer collections in 2D / Columbus View").

- **NEW-BUFFERPOLYLINE-2D-EXTRUSION** (S–M, found by PARITY-BUFFER-2DCV 2026-07-01) — ✅ **SHIPPED (2026-07-03).** **The originally-recorded root cause was WRONG** — the WGSL screen-space extrusion was never the problem: replaying `BufferPolylineMaterial.wgsl`'s separate `modelViewRelativeToEye × projectionMatrix` path in JS against the live packed camera UBO in SCENE2D produced correct on-screen clip positions (equal to the fused `mvpRelativeToEye` path), and flipping `command.cull = false` made the polyline render perfectly (correct position AND width) with zero shader changes. **Actual root cause: a culling bug** — PARITY-BUFFER-2DCV reprojected the packed vertex positions into the 2D/CV render frame but every `Buffer*` draw command still carried the raw ECEF `collection.boundingVolume`, so in SCENE2D the orthographic culling volume (projected frame) rejected the ECEF sphere and the whole command was frustum-culled. Points survived the acceptance probe only by BV-radius luck, and the "polygon renders in 2D" pass was UI-noise pixels — the polygon was culled too; CV survived because its perspective frustum happened to intersect the wrong-frame sphere. **Fix:** new `computeBufferModeBoundingVolume` (`WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts`) mirrors upstream `PrimitiveCommandHelpers.updateAndQueueCommands`: SCENE3D → same `collection.boundingVolume` reference (byte-identical; runtime-verified via reference-equality check, `_modeBV` never allocated in pure 3D); 2D/CV → `BoundingSphere.projectTo2D` ((z,x,y)-swizzled frame, matching the repacked positions); MORPHING → `BoundingSphere.union(WC, projected)`. Applied to all three renderers (polyline + point + polygon — same one-line bug). Per-cache BV storage (`_modeBV`/`_modeBVMorph`) because commands hold the reference across the frame. **Verified** (`probe-buffer-2dcv-parity.mjs`, PNGs READ): SCENE2D magenta 0→734 px + yellow 497(noise)→5013 px; presence gate now `true` for all three primitives in all three modes + new width gate (median vertical line thickness: SCENE2D 3 px == CV 3 px for material width 4 — screen-space width convention carried into 2D); SCENE3D/CV signature-color counts unchanged pre/post fix (4097/558/3019, 4085/636/3813). **Files:** `WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBufferPolylineRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBufferPointRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUBufferPolygonRenderer.ts` (no WGSL change needed). **Note:** WebGL still renders `Buffer*` mis-projected/blank in 2D/CV (no CPU reprojection) — WebGPU-exceeds-WebGL here, per the PARITY-BUFFER-2DCV design.

### ~~NEW-GPU-CULLER-CONSUME-OR-DELETE~~ — RESOLVED (Batch 209) — gpuCuller wired as threshold-gated consumer

**Status:** RESOLVED. Decision: **option (a) — consume from
`_executeOpaquePass`** with the existing 256-command threshold.

**Trace:** Batch 209 (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:_executeOpaquePass`).
The opaque pass now invokes `gpuCullCommands` when
`count >= GPU_CULL_THRESHOLD (256)` and `frameState.cullingVolume`
is available. The CPU cull still runs upstream in `Scene.updateFrameState`;
the GPU pass adds a fine-grained per-frustum re-test that meaningfully
cuts draw-call dispatch at the 10K+ instance scale. 1-frame readback
latency is acceptable at this density. Below threshold the helper
returns the input array untouched — no overhead for typical scenes.

**Bypass:** Pick passes (`config.picking`) skip GPU culling entirely
(Batch 212 audit) so pick fidelity matches the CPU-culled command set.

**Follow-up note:** The old `effectiveCount` parameter was added so the
opaque-pass call site passes the pre-sized `frustumCommands.commands[OPAQUE]`
array directly with the matching `frustumCommands.indices[OPAQUE]`,
avoiding a per-frame slice allocation in the hot path.

### ~~NEW-HIZ-SORT-CONSUME-OR-DELETE~~ — RESOLVED (Batches 210 + 211) — both wired as threshold-gated consumers

**Status:** RESOLVED. Decision: **consume both** with thresholds tuned
to each dispatcher's overhead profile.

**Trace:** Batches 210 + 211 (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:_executeOpaquePass`).

- **HiZ occlusion (Batch 210)** — threshold 2000 commands. New
  `_filterByHiZVisibility` (consumer of previous-frame readback) +
  `_dispatchHiZForNextFrame` (producer) pair. Lazy SOA scratch growth
  tracks the largest count seen. Visibility flags survive across
  frames; consumer applies before this frame's dispatch completes.
  Pyramid build + occlusion test + readback all run via the existing
  `FeatureRendererKey.HI_Z_OCCLUSION` registration.
- **GPUSortKeys (Batch 211, Phase 1)** — threshold 5000 commands.
  Generates packed 64-bit sort keys (`sortKeysHigh + sortKeysLow +
  commandIndices`). Phase 2 (the GPU sort over those keys) is the
  follow-up `NEW-GPU-SORT-PIPELINE` entry below — a generic u64
  bitonic / radix sort doesn't exist yet, only the point-specific
  `PointCloudSort.wgsl`.

**Bypass:** Pick passes (`config.picking`) skip both dispatchers
(Batch 212 audit) so pick fidelity matches the CPU-culled command
set. Shadow-cast, OIT translucent, and motion-vector passes all
iterate their own command sets and are unaffected.

**Q18 reconcile (2026-07-04) — premise STALE, no code change.** The
`NEXT_QUEUE_2026-07-04.md` Q18 row (`GPU-CULLER-CONSUME-OR-DELETE`)
restated the ORIGINAL landmine ("orphan dispatchers allocate eagerly, no
live caller"). That is false at HEAD for all four dispatchers:

- **gpuCull** — consumed in `WebGPUSceneRenderer._executeOpaquePass`
  behind `if (gpuCullActive)` (256-cmd hysteresis gate); dispatcher
  allocated lazily via `WebGPUContext.getGPUCullerForOpaqueFrustum`.
- **HiZ** — producer `_dispatchHiZForNextFrame` + consumer
  `_filterByHiZVisibility`, behind `if (hiZActive || gpuSortActive)`
  (2000-cmd gate); dispatcher via `getOrCreateDispatcher` WeakMap +
  `initWebGPUHiZOcclusion.allocate()` on first gated dispatch.
- **GPUSortKeys** — producer `_dispatchGPUSortKeys` + consumer
  `_applySortedOrder` (default-off consume, same 5000-cmd gate); WeakMap
  lazy alloc.
- **PointCloudSort** — the one dispatcher NOT previously spelled out
  here. Live consumer chain: `TimeDynamicPointCloud.js:669`
  `bridge.sortByDistance(...)` → `WasmPointCloudBridge.sortByDistance`
  calls `fr.sort(encoder, distSq, count)` (`FeatureRendererKey.POINT_CLOUD_SORT`)
  behind `useGPUSort && count >= threshold` (opt-in via
  `sortTransparentPoints` + `performanceManager.shouldUseGPUPointCloud`).
  `WebGPUPointCloudSortDispatcher._resources` stays `null` until the first
  gated `sort()`, so nothing is allocated until the feature actually fires.

Allocation is therefore both **lazy** and **gated** for every dispatcher —
the opposite of "eager allocation, no caller". No delete/reclaim is
warranted; the consume-decision from Batches 209/210/211 stands. A
structural regression guard now locks this in:
`Tools/visual-regression/probe-gpu-culler-consumers.mjs` asserts each
dispatcher's consumer call site + activation gate still exists in live
source, so a future refactor that re-orphans one fails loudly instead of
silently re-arming the Principle-7 landmine.

**Known interaction (TAA) — verified safe (Batch 222 review):** at
extreme density (>=2000 commands) HiZ-culled objects can transition
from "rendered last frame" → "not rendered this frame", producing
a depth discontinuity at their pixels. The TAA reprojection shader
already handles this case via its existing disocclusion detection
(`TAA.wgsl:235-280`): it samples previous-frame depth at the
reprojected UV, eye-space-projects both, and rejects history when
`depthDelta > disocclusionThreshold` (scaled by `abs(eyePosCurr.z)
* 0.001`, floored at 1.0). For HiZ-culled commands the previous-
frame surface is at the command's depth and the current is at
background depth → depthDelta is large → history rejected → no
ghost. No additional mitigation needed. Documented as audit-cleared
in Batch 222.
