## WIRE-PP-LIBRARY-BUILTINS-RESIDUALS — per-stage gaps left by the library built-in interception (2026-07-02)

**Surfaced by WIRE-PP-LIBRARY-BUILTINS (the 7 orphaned `PostProcessStageLibrary` built-ins).** The interception mechanism shipped: `WebGPULibraryPostProcessStage.ts` maps the well-known `czm_*` names (`czm_black_and_white`, `czm_brightness`, `czm_night_vision`, `czm_silhouette`, `czm_edge_detection_<guid>` prefix, `czm_lens_flare`, `czm_depth_view`) to their WGSL twins during the configure pass's user-stage scan (`WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts`), with per-frame enabled/uniform sync + a CPU twin of the czm_* sun/earth frame state for LensFlare. Parity rewrites landed for EdgeDetection (depth-Sobel), NightVision (frame-seeded noise), DepthView (raw depth), Silhouette (vec4 mix), Brightness (`target` reserved-word fix), LensFlare (full gate/mask/ghost/halo port). Also fixed while here: upstream's `removeStages()` compaction only runs AFTER the feature-renderer early-return in `PostProcessStageCollection.update()`, so on WebGPU `postProcessStages.remove(stage)` left an `undefined` hole, `_stages.length` never shrank, and the length-based rebuild gate (Batch 290) leaked BOTH user WGSL stages and library stages until the next add — the FR update now mirrors the compaction. Probe: `probe-pp-library-builtins.mjs` (7/7 stages, cross-backend, off-gate byte-identical).

**Residual per-stage gaps (this entry):**

1. **LensFlare `dirtTexture` / `starTexture` overlays not ported.** The WGSL twin implements the space gate, sun-on-screen gate, isInEarth ghost mask, 4-ghost chromatic chain, halo, and sun-distance weighting (ghost/halo geometry matches WebGL pixel-position-for-pixel-position), but WebGL additionally adds a tiled dirt-texture overlay and modulates the in-space result by the rotating starburst texture (WGSL approximates the star factor as 1.0 → smoother, somewhat brighter ghosts). Fix shape: load `Assets/Textures/LensFlare/{DirtMask,StarBurst}.jpg` into GPU textures at stage init (the stage uniforms carry the URLs), extend the stage's bind group + `LensFlareUniforms`, port the dirt-tile/star-rotate math. M effort.
2. **`selected` feature masking (CZM_SELECTED_FEATURE) unsupported** for EdgeDetection/Silhouette (and BlackAndWhite's selected bypass). WebGL rebuilds the stage shader with `czm_selected()` when `stage.selected = [features]` is set; the WebGPU twins always process the whole frame (identical to WebGL with no selection). Needs the pick-id/selected-texture plumbing — same infrastructure gap as the model-selection post-process path. L effort.
3. **DepthView encoding divergence (within-tolerance, documented).** WebGL shows `czm_readDepth` (reversed-log → conventional depth); WebGPU shows the raw conventional device depth from `depthSampleableView`. Same near-dark/far-white shape, absolute gray levels differ (probe xMean 43/255 at tol 45). Also the WebGPU sampleable depth copy does not include point-primitive depth (the WebGL depth vis shows the probe's 200px point disc, WebGPU's doesn't). Only worth chasing if a consumer needs numeric depth-vis parity.
4. **Ordering vs user WGSL stages:** intercepted library stages execute AFTER all user `wgslFragmentShader` stages (two separate pipeline arrays), not interleaved in `collection._stages` order. Matters only when a scene mixes both kinds and depends on order. S effort (merge into one ordered list) if it ever bites.

**Files:** `WebGPULibraryPostProcessStage.ts` (registry + stage class), `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts` (interception + sync + compaction), `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts` (chain slot), `Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/{BlackAndWhite,Brightness,NightVision,DepthView,EdgeDetection,Silhouette,LensFlare}.wgsl`. **Trace:** 2026-07-02.

## BUG-GLOBE-PIPELINE-NAME-AXES — globe descriptor name doesn't encode all structural pipeline axes (latent central-cache aliasing) (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.generateCacheKey` keys on `descriptor.name` (the optional `variant` arg is unused by the globe path — `resolveGlobePipelineEntry` passes only the descriptor). The convention (documented at `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:371-374`) is therefore "distinct pipeline structure MUST produce a distinct name". Bug 487 (GLOBE-UNDERGROUND-COLOR) fixed the worst instance — the no-cull variant differed only in `primitive.cullMode` with an identical name, so underground tiles aliased to the cull-back pipeline and the underside never rendered (nondeterministic by creation race).

**Remaining latent instances (same class).** The globe descriptor name (`Globe terrain (quant, norm, blend, …labels)`) still does NOT encode:

- `strideBytes` / `hasWebMercatorT` (changes the vertex `arrayStride` + texcoord attribute format — an alias here binds the wrong vertex layout),
- `hasGeodeticSurfaceNormals` (extra attribute + different shader module via `GEODETIC_NORMAL` define),
- `ShaderDefine.LOG_DEPTH` / `GLOBE_IMAGERY_REDUCED` (different shader modules),
- `_sampleCount` (multisample state — canvas-format/MSAA flips are partially covered by the `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` LOCAL cache wipe, but the CENTRAL cache retains the old-name entry).

Most combinations are coincidentally disambiguated by the existing labels (quant/norm/blend correlate with stride) or by session homogeneity (webMercatorT is uniform per imagery provider), which is why no visible artifact is currently attributed to them — but the failure mode is the Bug 487 shape: silent, race-decided, wrong-pipeline binds.

**Suggested fix (S).** Fold the missing axes into the name (e.g. `, s${strideBytes}, wm${0|1}, d${defines.toString(16)}, ms${sampleCount}`) OR pass a `variant` object to the central cache. Audit the OTHER renderers that use name-keyed central caching for the same convention violation.

## PARITY-POINT-SPRITE-SHAPE-RESIDUALS — residuals surfaced by the point-sprite shape/size parity fix (2026-07-02)

**Surfaced by PARITY-POINT-SPRITE-SHAPE.** The shape/size fix shipped: WebGPU point-cloud quads now rasterize as SOLID SQUARES like WebGL `gl_Points` (the old soft-circle carve in `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts`'s inline WGSL + `PointCloudEDLDepth.wgsl` was WebGPU-only invention — `ModelFS.glsl` only carves a circle under `HAS_POINT_DIAMETER`, the Bentley point-style extension); the phantom 1920×1080 viewport read (`uniformState._context?._canvas` — always undefined) was replaced with the real `drawingBufferWidth/Height`; WebGL point-size attenuation reached parity (per-point `min(geometricError·geometricErrorScale·drawingBufferHeight/sseDenominator / eyeDepth, bakedMax)` in the color/LOD/velocity/EDL-depth VSes via the formerly-`_pad2` UB lane, with `PointCloud.js` giving a constant style `pointSize` priority over attenuation exactly like WebGL's `hasPointSizeStyle` branch, and `boundingSphere` falling back to `_boundingSphere` on the FR path so `TimeDynamicPointCloud.getGeometricError` stops zeroing attenuation); and `PointPrimitiveColor/Pick.wgsl` now mirror `PointPrimitiveCollectionVS` sizing exactly (outlinePercent from unpadded size, scaleByDistance on the TOTAL size, +3px AA padding, `v_pixelDistance = 2/totalSize`). Probe: `probe-point-sprite-shape.mjs` (styled point cloud + attenuation-only cloud gated on gain-NORMALIZED ds4 < 16% — per-channel means equalized before the per-cell compare so the drifting tint residual below cancels while spatial shape/size/coverage breaks still score 20%+; point primitives raw ds4 < 5%; 0 device errors; tighten the normalized gates to ~8% once the tint fix lands).

**Residuals (this entry):**

1. **WebGPU point-cloud blue/brightness COLOR tint — candidate new parity row.** With shape + size now matching, the remaining point-cloud probe residual is a color-path gap: the WebGPU cloud reads bluer/brighter than WebGL on the same PNTS data. It drives essentially ALL of the remaining point-cloud raw-ds4 on both probe scenes and DRIFTS monotonically across consecutive same-session runs (seven 2026-07-02 runs — styled: 9.34/12.14/12.9/13.76/14.52/15.6/16.67%; attenuation-only: 12.29/13.96/14.6/15.52/16.31/17.14/18.85%) — which is why the probe gates the point-cloud scenes on the gain-NORMALIZED ds4 instead of the raw one. Quantified at fix time: WebGL/WebGPU per-channel mean ratios over lit cells ≈ R 0.78 / G 0.72 / B 0.69 (WebGPU ~27-45% brighter, blue lifted most — the probe prints these `gains` every run), and a per-channel gain-equalized compare still leaves ~9.7-12.4% ds4 (itself creeping ~1pp/run), so the tint is NOT a pure global gain — it has a drifting per-point/nonlinear component. The monotone session-correlated creep is itself a lead: it smells like a time/adaptation-dependent stage (auto-exposure/tonemap adaptation or similar) contributing to the WebGPU point-cloud brightness, not a fixed constant offset. Suspect the color pipeline around the point-cloud draw (gamma/linear handling, tonemap interaction, or the RGB path through `buildInstanceBuffer`) rather than geometry — sizes matched in the auditor's footprint check. Worth its own parity ID (shape: `PARITY-POINTCLOUD-COLOR-TINT`) before any probe-gate tightening. M-investigate/S-fix effort.
2. **`czm_pixelRatio` and `u_maxTotalPointSize` unplumbed into the PointPrimitive WGSL UB (pre-existing, acknowledged in the shader comment).** `PointPrimitiveCollectionVS` multiplies the total sprite size by `czm_pixelRatio` and clamps to `u_maxTotalPointSize` (the GL aliased-point-size range cap); the WGSL twin (`PointPrimitiveColor/Pick.wgsl`) does neither — probes run at DPR 1 so this is invisible in CI, but **hiDPI (devicePixelRatio > 1) point primitives will undersize vs WebGL** by the pixel-ratio factor. Fix shape: add pixelRatio (and a large-constant max size — WebGPU has no aliased-point clamp to mirror) to the collection UB pack in the point-primitive renderer. S effort.

**Files:** `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts` (color path, UB pack), `Shaders/WebGPU/Collections/PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl` / `PointPrimitivePick.wgsl` (pixelRatio lanes). **Trace:** 2026-07-02.

## GLTF-PRIMITIVE-MODE-RESIDUALS — residuals surfaced by the glTF POINTS-mode topology fix (2026-07-02; expanded audit 2026-07-31)

**Surfaced by GLTF-POINTS-MODE.** The topology gap shipped: `extractPrimitiveGeometry` now carries `primitiveType` (glTF `primitive.mode`), `WebGPUModelRenderer` maps mode-0 POINTS to a `"point-list"` GPUPrimitiveTopology on `primCache.topology`, and `WebGPUModelPipelineCache` threads a sticky per-primitive topology (same set-before-`getPipeline*` contract as the metadata/customShader chunks; `topologyVariantKey` leaves triangle-list keys byte-identical) through ALL per-primitive pipeline builders (color / depth-write / silhouette model+color / pick / pick-hover / precise-pick 1+2 / pick-metadata / velocity / classification / capture / error-fallback). Non-indexed POINTS primitives synthesize sequential indices at `ensurePrimitiveCache` time so they ride the drawIndexed path (WebGPU CPU-validates non-indexed `draw()` vertex ranges against every vertex-step slot; the 1-element default-attribute buffers pass drawIndexed via robust-access clamping but hard-fail `draw()`). Probe: `probe-gltf-points-mode.mjs` (PointCloudWithRGBColors.glb, 2500 non-indexed mode-0 points: WebGL 6186 vs WebGPU 6179 lit px, centroid Δ 0.2px, mean-channel Δ ≤ 6.2; off-gate `probe-model-pbr-audit` green).

**Residuals (this entry):**

1. **Non-indexed TRIANGLES models with missing attributes hit the same `draw()` validation error (pre-existing, latent).** Any non-indexed glTF primitive that lacks normals/tangents/uv/joints binds the pipeline cache's 1-element default vertex buffers, and the non-indexed `draw(vertexCount)` fails "Vertex range requires a larger buffer" — silently no model (invalid command buffer). The POINTS fix scoped the sequential-index synthesis to `topology === "point-list"` to keep the triangle off-gate byte-identical. `C11-90` widened the synthesis to every mode EXCEPT TRIANGLES (`synthesizesIndices` in the topology table), so LINES / LINE_LOOP / LINE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_FAN are covered. **Non-indexed TRIANGLES remains OPEN and deliberately untouched** — it is the one case where synthesizing would change the historical `draw(vertexCount)` path, and the off-gate byte-identity of the overwhelmingly common primitive is worth more than closing a latent gap no shipped asset has surfaced. Sizing the default buffers is the alternative fix.
2. **LINES / LINE_LOOP / LINE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_FAN still render as triangle-list. — ✅ SHIPPED (`C11-90`).** `topologyForPrimitiveType` is gone. `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelTopology.ts` is now the single enforceable home for the topology axis: an EXHAUSTIVE seven-mode table, `realizeModelPrimitiveTopology` (called exactly once per primitive from `ensurePrimitiveCache` — preparation, never draw), `modelPrimitiveState` (the only builder of a model/shadow `GPUPrimitiveState`, so `topology` and `stripIndexFormat` can never be written apart), and `buildModelTopologyVariantKey` / `modelTopologyAxisToken` / `parseModelTopologyVariantKey` (build+parse exact inverses). LINES→line-list, LINE_STRIP→line-strip, TRIANGLE_STRIP→triangle-strip (both with the exact `stripIndexFormat`), LINE_LOOP→line-list with each restart-delimited run's closing segment appended, TRIANGLE_FAN→triangle-list expanded around each run's hub. Triangle-list keys stay byte-identical (value AND numeric type), so no cached pipeline is orphaned. Contract: `Tools/visual-regression/model-primitive-topology.spec.mjs` (37/37), whose conversion fixtures are read out of the shipped `Apps/SampleData/models/PrimitiveRestart/*.glb` rather than hand-typed.
3. **`ModelPointCloudStylingStage.wgsl` remains orphaned — it does NOT map cleanly onto point-list.** WebGPU point-list rasterizes fixed 1px points (no `gl_PointSize` analog), which matches WebGL's unstyled `gl_PointSize = 1.0` default (ModelVS.glsl) — that's the parity the fix targets. Point-size STYLING (Cesium3DTileStyle `pointSize`, attenuation) on a Model-path POINTS primitive would need quad expansion like `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer`'s PNTS path; the WGSL styling helper stays as scaffolding for that follow-up (Principle 7 — do not remove).
4. **Shadow topology is only partially corrected in the dirty `C11-184` lane. — ✅ SHIPPED (`C11-90`).** Commands now carry `_shadowCastStripIndexFormat` beside `_shadowCastTopology`; `getShadowCastPipelineCacheKey` derives its topology segment from `modelTopologyAxisToken` (the SAME home the color key uses, so the two cannot drift), `_getOrCreateCastPipeline` builds its `primitive` block with `modelPrimitiveState`, and `WebGPUCSMCastPass` — which shares that factory — forwards the format too. A uint16 and a uint32 strip caster are now distinct cast pipelines; every pre-C11-90 caster key is byte-identical.
5. **Uint8 primitive-restart upcast is incorrect. — ✅ SHIPPED (`C11-90`).** `ModelPrimitiveGeometry` records `indexSourceComponentBytes` (the ORIGINAL accessor width, which `indexType` cannot express) and stays backend-agnostic; the realization promotes `0x00FF` → `0xFFFF` ONLY for the four modes `getMeshPrimitives.js` declares restart-capable, and the spec reads that permitted set out of `getMeshPrimitives.js` itself so ours cannot drift from upstream's. A uint8 LINES/TRIANGLES/POINTS asset keeps `255` as an ordinary vertex index and passes through by reference with zero allocation. Translation copies rather than rewriting in place, because the source array belongs to the cached immutable base descriptor.
6. **Generic Primitive duplicates the topology residual — STILL OPEN after `C11-90`.** `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.ts`'s own `mapCesiumPrimitiveTypeToWebGPU` maps strips without `stripIndexFormat`, leaves LINE_LOOP unclosed, and treats TRIANGLE_FAN as triangle-list. `C11-90` deliberately scoped itself to the MODEL path; the realization home (`WebGPUModelTopology.ts`) is written as a pure, backend-neutral module precisely so the generic-Primitive path can adopt it without a rewrite, but adopting it means reworking that path's own index ownership and cache keys and must not be conflated with the Model visibility-preparation performance row.

**Required architecture — ✅ IMPLEMENTED for the Model path (`C11-90`):** one immutable-input, cached WebGPU primitive realization
`{topology, indexData, indexCount, indexFormat, stripIndexFormat, vertexCount}`;
no settled-frame rescans or allocations; preserve restart batches in one draw;
key every model pipeline and shadow variant by topology plus strip format; and
carry the same pair in capture records. Route fan/loop conversion through the
preparation/resource lane so it never lands on the render hot path.
Conversion cost model: passthrough returns the caller's array BY REFERENCE
(`allocatedIndexBytes === 0`) — a conversion allocates exactly once, in
preparation, only for LINE_LOOP closure, TRIANGLE_FAN expansion, a uint8
restart translation that actually finds a sentinel, or non-indexed synthesis.

**Files:** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelTopology.ts` (NEW — the one home), `Scene/Model/ModelPrimitiveGeometry.js` (primitiveType extract + `indexSourceComponentBytes`), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts` (realization at `ensurePrimitiveCache` + realized index upload + capture-record and shadow-command axis), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts` (sticky realization + `modelPrimitiveState` at all 12 builders), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js` + `WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts` (cast key + descriptor). **Contract:** `Tools/visual-regression/model-primitive-topology.spec.mjs`. **Trace:** 2026-07-02; `C11-90` 2026-08-01.

## RTE-ELLIPSOID-AWARE-RESIDUALS — residuals surfaced by the ellipsoid-aware CSM ground-clamp fix (2026-07-02)

**Surfaced by RTE-ELLIPSOID-AWARE (FEAT-3DT2-03, CSM slice — SHIPPED).** The concrete positional-correctness gap named in the parity report (`WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:74-79` hardcoded WGS84 radii) is closed: the WGS84 constants are now DEFAULTS, `WebGPUCSMRenderer.setEllipsoid(radii)` (change-detected, degenerate-radii-guarded) recomputes the inverse-square radii, and `WebGPUContext.executeShadowMapCastCommands` threads `scene.ellipsoid?.radii ?? scene.globe?.ellipsoid?.radii` in once per cast frame. `computeVisibleGroundFar` + the ground-clamped `computeFrustumCornersWorldSpace` (new optional trailing `invRadiiSq*` params, WGS84 defaults keep the exported spec API + `defines=0`-style migration behavior identical) now solve against the scene's actual globe. Probe: `probe-ellipsoid-rte.mjs` — synthesized 0.5×-scaled ellipsoid (per the FEAT-3DT2-03 probe note; no Mars/Moon asset needed): pre-fix `computeVisibleGroundFar` diverged from the `IntersectionTests.rayEllipsoid` reference by ~862,000% (7,328 km vs 850 m) and cascade splits ballooned to `maxShadowDistance` (100 km); post-fix both agree to 0.000% and splits tighten to the visible ground (935 m). WGS84 off-gate: pixel mismatch 0.0000% vs the pre-change build + FP-exact groundFar/splits.

**Residuals (this entry) — the REST of the "ellipsoid-aware RTE" umbrella.** Verified during this fix: the RTE encoding itself (`positionHigh/Low`, `encodedCameraHigh/Low`, `mvpRelativeToEye`) is ellipsoid-INDEPENDENT (camera-relative ECEF — no radii appear in the math), so "tileset._ellipsoid is never threaded" does not affect tile POSITIONS through the RTE path. The remaining hardcoded-Earth-radius sites are feature-specific:

1. **Terrain shadow-cast vertical exaggeration (`WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js` WGSL `EARTH_RADIUS: f32 = 6378137.0`, quantized12 + terrainUncompressed variants).** Only active when `verticalExaggeration !== 1.0`; on a non-Earth globe the exaggeration offset in the CAST pass would mismatch the color pass. Fix shape: add the max radius to the existing `TerrainShadowGlobals` UB (`_pad` lane is free). S effort.
2. **Atmosphere / lens flare / procedural clouds / volumetric fog Earth-radius constants** (`WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js`, `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts`, `WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUVolumetricFogRenderer.ts`). These mirror WebGL upstream, which also treats atmosphere-adjacent effects as Earth-keyed (e.g. `PostProcessStageLibrary.createLensFlareStage` defaults to `Ellipsoid.WGS84.maximumRadius`); NOT a WebGL↔WebGPU parity gap, tracked here only for a future non-Earth-scenes epic.
3. **No real Mars/Moon asset test** (`PARITY-RTE-ELLIPSOID-BLOCKER` stands). The scaled-ellipsoid mock verifies the CSM math + cast-shadow placement cross-backend; an end-to-end non-Earth 3D Tileset pixel pass is still deferred until an asset is sourced.

**Files:** `WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts` (setEllipsoid + threaded solves), `WebGPUContext.ts` (per-frame threading), `cesium-js-types.d.ts` (`CesiumScene.ellipsoid`), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-ellipsoid-rte.mjs` (new gate). **Trace:** 2026-07-02.

- **NEW-GLOBE-DAYTIME-OCEAN-BRIGHTNESS** — ✅ SHIPPED (Q10, 2026-07-04). Root cause was NEITHER glint NOR atmosphere daylight brightness (both red herrings from the original triage) — it was the ocean **`diffuseHighlight`** term in `GlobeTerrain.wgsl::computeEnhancedOcean` being **zeroed on every daytime fragment**. WebGL `computeWaterColor` (GlobeFS.glsl L830) applies `diffuseHighlight = waveHighlightColor(0.3,0.45,0.6) * NdotL * mask * (1.0 - fade)` where `fade` is the **atmosphere camera-distance fade** (L428 = `clamp((cameraDist - lightingFadeOut)/(lightingFadeIn - lightingFadeOut),0,1)`) — 0 at close/mid range → full bluish highlight. The WGSL called `computeEnhancedOcean(..., dayFade, ...)` passing the **day/night TERMINATOR fade**, which `fragmentMain` forces to `1.0` whenever `enableLighting` is off (the DEFAULT) → `highlightFade = 1 - 1 = 0` → the highlight vanished, leaving the ocean ~4x darker (deep navy vs WebGL bright blue) at mid-range while night stayed at parity (NdotL≈0 kills the highlight for both). **Fix (2 hunks, WGSL-only, GLSL already correct):** (1) call site passes `tile.groundAtmosphereControl.y` (the identical lightingFade clamp, packed per-tile) instead of `dayFade`; param renamed `dayFade`→`lightingFade`. (2) `tsPerturbationRatio` now derives from the **distance-faded** tangent normal `normalize(vec3(waveN.xy * waveIntensityFade, waveN.z)).z` (matching WebGL L818-819 `normalTangentSpace.xy *= waveIntensity`) — WITHOUT this, correcting hunk (1) unmasked a latent bug where `nonDiffuseHighlight` (peaks as NdotL→0) blew the NIGHT ocean out to saturated cyan (lum 28→208), because the raw `waveN.z` never faded to 1 at orbit. **Verified** (`diag-daytime-ocean-tmp.mjs`, pinned clocks, caribbean-mid `-70.1037,18.485,2000000`): DAY gpu-vs-gl **91.0% → 2.05%** (WebGPU lum 46.4→116.5 vs WebGL 117.3); NIGHT **1.04%** preserved (28.3 vs 29.5); PNGs read — day ocean now bright blue with visible sun-glint bloom, night correctly dark. Off-gate: change is confined to reflective-ocean water fragments (`tile.flags.x>0.5 && waterMask>0.01`); land/non-globe byte-identical; tsPerturbationRatio hunk is byte-identical at close zoom where `waveIntensityFade≈1`.

- **NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-CLASSIFY-CONTAINMENT** — ✅ SHIPPED (Q15R, 2026-07-04) via WebGL-parity **stencil Z-fail**. `WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer` now emits, per batch per ground pass, a stencil-MARK draw (colorWrite off, `depthCompare` less-equal against the BOUND scene depth, `stencilFront.depthFailOp` decrement-wrap / `stencilBack.depthFailOp` increment-wrap, terrain compare-always / tileset compare-equal-0x80, readMask `CESIUM_3D_TILE_MASK` 0x80 / writeMask `CLASSIFICATION_MASK` 0x0f) then a stencil-TESTED color draw (`compare not-equal 0`, depth test off, passOp zero to reset), both in the same TERRAIN/CESIUM_3D_TILE_CLASSIFICATION pass bucket (execute in push order in one render pass → the mark's stencil is visible to the immediately-following color draw). This mirrors `Vector3DTilePrimitive.getStencilDepthRenderState` + `colorRenderState` and compares per-FRAGMENT volume depth vs per-FRAGMENT globe depth in hardware at full precision, sidestepping BOTH FS-reconstruction walls below. The mark + color pipelines use a group(0)-only layout (no globe-depth-texture sample) so they're independent of `_globeDepthView`; pick + velocity keep the depth-sample bind group and are skipped when it's absent. **Verified** (`probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs`, restructured): FAR (20 km) IoU **1.000**, NEAR (3 km) IoU **0.932** (area ratio 1.07 — vs the old ~2.25x-area h/(h-1000) over-inflation), at BOTH `msaaSamples=4` (viewer default) AND `msaaSamples=1`; polylines + globe at parity; 0 device errors; PNGs read. **KEY probe lesson:** the WebGPU globe surface + the async stencil pipelines take ~100 frames after `tilesLoaded` to warm up — the probe's old `settle` broke at ~31 frames, yielding a FALSE-NEGATIVE black globe + empty footprint that an earlier revision mis-attributed to an "msaa=1 globe-black gap"; the fix was 200 trailing warmup frames, NOT any renderer change (the globe renders fine at msaa=1 once warm). **Follow-up:** `NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-STENCIL-2DCV-COVERAGE` (below). Files: `WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer.js`, `probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs`. **Trace:** 2026-07-04.

  Historical investigation (Q15, superseded by the Q15R stencil fix above) — the depth-sample FS approaches, proven insufficient:
  - **Approach A (eye-distance):** render both volume faces (cullMode "none", depthCompare "always" so back faces reach the FS), decode the sampled surface's log depth to an eye distance via `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance(surfaceDepth, encodeNear, encodeFar)` (encode = `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` = `[0.1, 1e10]`), compare to the volume fragment's clip-w eye distance (`1.0/i.pos.w`). **Result:** NEAR (3 km) IoU 1.000 ✅; FAR (20 km) over-discards to 0 ❌ — the `exp2` decode amplifies the depth quantum + any encode-near/far inconsistency into km-scale eye-distance error at 20 km, which exceeds the thin ±1 km volume.
  - **Approach B (log-window-z):** compare in the shared log-window-z space directly (`surfaceDepth <= i.pos.z + eps`); both the globe's sampled depth and the volume's `o.pos.z` are log-encoded with the same encode frustum, so no `exp2` amplification. **Result:** NEAR IoU 0.932 ✅ (slightly loose); FAR still 0 ❌ — the volume's per-VERTEX log z (interpolated) cannot bracket a thin volume at far range against the globe's per-FRAGMENT depth.
  - **Infrastructure blocker (independent):** at `scene.msaaSamples = 1` — the config the standing probe `probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs` forces for its NEAR/FAR parity frames (a legacy of the now-fixed `NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-MSAA-PIPELINE` gap, Q2) — the WebGPU globe depth texture (`_globeDepthView`, and `_packedTranslucentDepthView` is null with no translucent content) reads far/empty (`surfaceDepth ≈ 1.0`) for the footprint, so ANY depth-sample containment discards everything. The pre-change classifier only "passed" at msaa=1 because empty depth ≠ 0 dodged its sky-discard and it painted the full (inflated) silhouette. Verify whether the globe depth copy is populated at msaa=1 before relying on any depth-sample classifier there.
  - **Correct fix — stencil Z-fail (WebGL parity):** mirror `Vector3DTilePrimitive.getStencilDepthRenderState` (shipped above — this is what Q15R implemented). The Q15 note's "msaa=1 depth-population blocker" turned out to be a **probe warmup artifact**, not a real infra gap: the bound scene depth-stencil DOES hold the globe surface during the classifier pass at both msaa levels once the globe is warm (~100 frames); the earlier msaa=1 forcing measured too early. **Trace:** 2026-07-04.

Fix shape (when a 2D/CV classifier consumer needs it): give the 2D/CV path its own stencil-mark against the 2D map's depth, or a mode-branched containment that matches the 2D orthographic frame. - **NS-MOON-MATTE-NOT-SUNLIT** (premise verified STALE, 2026-07-05) — User report (split-screen WebGL vs WebGPU): "the moon renders matte/flat, does not show sun-relative shading (lit hemisphere, terminator, phase, limb darkening)." **Re-verified against live HEAD code + probe — the shading is already present, strong, and cross-backend-identical; NOT a bug.** WebGL path: `Scene/EllipsoidPrimitive.js` sets the `ONLY_SUN_LIGHTING` define when `moon.onlySunLighting` (default true), so `EllipsoidFS.glsl` lights via `czm_private_phong` — pure Lambert (`diffuse = clamp(dot(sunDirEC, N),0,1)`, zero ambient, zero specular for `Material.ImageType`). WebGPU twin (`Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/Moon.wgsl` `phongCsmMaterial` + `_packMoonUniforms`) matches it exactly (world→model-rotated `sunDirMC`, specularStrength 0). New probe `probe-moon-sunlit.mjs` quantifies the two things a flat/emissive disc would fail: (1) near-full-phase **limb darkening** rim/center luminance ratio = 0.27 both backends (a matte disc → ~1.0); (2) half-phase **graded terminator** — lit-area fraction 0.35, lit centroid displaced 0.24·R toward the sunlit limb, ≥3 graded luminance buckets across the terminator. The "matte" perception traces to the DEFAULT viewer's tiny far moon disc (limb falloff unresolvable at ~30 px + maria albedo texture dominating the read) and to the physically-correct near-full Lambert appearance — both of which MATCH the WebGL reference, so any "de-matte" tweak would break WebGL↔WebGPU parity and change upstream `czm_private_phong` behavior. **No code change made.** Regression guard: `probe-moon-sunlit.mjs` (added to DEBUGGING_GUIDE probe inventory). **Trace:** 2026-07-05.

- **NS-MOON-ATMOSPHERE-EXTINCTION** — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-05, BOTH backends). The moon is now attenuated + reddened by atmospheric extinction along the camera→moon view ray, so a low-altitude near-horizon moon dims to a deep red ("blood moon") and fades into the horizon haze instead of rendering at full brightness. New backend-agnostic helper `Scene/computeAtmosphereExtinction.js` integrates the shipped Rayleigh/Mie optical depth (`Atmosphere` coefficients + scale heights, same 111 km outer shell as `AtmosphereCommon.glsl`) from the camera to the atmosphere boundary in the moon's direction and returns the per-channel transmittance. `Scene/Moon.js` computes it each frame (gated on `frameState.skyAtmosphereVisible`), publishes `frameState.moonAtmosphereExtinction`, and sets `EllipsoidPrimitive.atmosphereExtinction`. WebGL: `EllipsoidPrimitive` pushes an `ATMOSPHERE_EXTINCTION` define + `u_atmosphereExtinction` uniform (byte-identical for every non-moon ellipsoid — define absent) and `EllipsoidFS.glsl` multiplies the final color. WebGPU: `Moon.wgsl` gains an `extinction: vec3` uniform (offset 304, packed in `_packMoonUniforms`) and multiplies. **Physically gated / off-gate byte-identical:** from orbit (or when the sky atmosphere is hidden) the view ray never crosses the shell → optical depth 0 → transmittance EXACTLY `vec3(1.0)` → color × 1.0 is bit-identical. **Verified** `probe-moon-atmosphere.mjs` (PASS both backends): horizon ext (0.165,0.058,0.007) litLum 13 deep-red vs high ext (0.897,0.833,0.717) litLum 111 vs orbit ext (1,1,1) litLum 133 neutral; PNGs read; standing `probe-env-moon.mjs` still PASS (moon-from-space unchanged, litRatio 1.000). Files: `Scene/computeAtmosphereExtinction.js` (new), `Scene/Moon.js`, `Scene/EllipsoidPrimitive.js`, `Scene/Scene.js`, `Scene/FrameState.js`, `Shaders/EllipsoidFS.glsl`, `Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/Moon.wgsl`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js`. **Follow-up:** `NS-SUN-STARS-ATMOSPHERE-EXTINCTION` (below). **Trace:** 2026-07-05.

- **NS-SUN-STARS-ATMOSPHERE-EXTINCTION** — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-10, C7-SUN-STARS-EXTINCTION, BOTH backends; Principle 9 follow-up to NS-MOON-ATMOSPHERE-EXTINCTION). The atmospheric-extinction the moon got (B629) now also applies to the SUN billboard and the bright-star CATALOG starfield, on both backends, reusing the same `Scene/computeAtmosphereExtinction.js` integrator.
  - **SUN** (exact per-body integral, like the moon). `Sun.update` computes the camera→sun transmittance each frame (gated on `frameState.skyAtmosphereVisible`), publishes `frameState.sunAtmosphereExtinction`, and stores it on `sun._atmosphereExtinction`. WebGL `SunFS.glsl` multiplies the (gamma-corrected) sun color by `u_atmosphereExtinction`; WebGPU `SUN_SHADER_WGSL` multiplies by a new `extinction: vec3` (floats 28..30 in `packSunUniforms`). A low sun (~3° elev) dims to a deep-red disc (ext ≈ (0.16,0.056,0.006)); a high sun (~80°) is near-white ((0.90,0.83,0.72)); from orbit ext == exactly (1,1,1). No define needed — these shaders are sun-exclusive and `color × 1.0` is bit-identical.
  - **STARS** (per-direction analytic Bouguer model — the *cheapest correct grain*, documented). `StarField.update` integrates ONE zenith ray with the shared helper → `frameState.starZenithTransmittance` (mirrored on `starField._zenithTransmittance` for the probe). Each star's slant transmittance = `zenithTransmittance ^ airmass(elevation)`, `airmass = 1/max(sin elev, 1/38)` (plane-parallel Bouguer, capped at the ~38 Kasten-Young horizon limit). Applied per-star in the VS on both backends: WebGL `StarFieldVS.glsl` (uniforms `u_zenithTransmittance` + `u_cameraUpFixed`, dot with the fixed-frame star dir); WebGPU `StarField.wgsl` (uniforms `zenithTransmittance` + `cameraUpTeme` — camera up rotated into the TEME instance frame so `dot(directionFixed, cameraUpTeme)` === the same elevation sine; rotation-invariant, so both backends match). `zenithTransmittance == (1,1,1)` from orbit → `pow(1, airmass) === 1` → byte-identical.
  - **Off-gate byte-identical:** atmosphere hidden / from orbit → transmittance exactly `(1,1,1)` → every multiply is `× 1.0`. Verified (`probe-sun-stars-extinction.mjs`, PASS both backends): sun horizon dimmer+warmer than high, sun orbit ext (1,1,1), star surface zenithT (0.898,0.835,0.719) → derived extLowLum 0.30 ≪ extHighLum 0.83 (per-direction), star orbit zenithT (1,1,1), WebGL↔WebGPU parity on both sun ext and star zenithT. Sun PNGs read (dim deep-red horizon disc vs bright-white high disc). B629 `probe-moon-atmosphere.mjs` regression **green** (h=13.3 unchanged).
  - **Follow-up surfaced by this batch:** `NS-SUN-BLEND-MODE-DIVERGENCE` (below) — the extinguished horizon sun now composites *visibly differently* across backends because of a PRE-EXISTING sun-flare blend-mode divergence (extinction values are at exact parity; the composite is not).

The extinction is proven from the runtime B629 transmittance + the airmass model instead. **Two follow-ups remain:** (1) `NS-SURFACE-SKYATMOSPHERE-NIGHT-BRIGHT` — the surface night sky should be dark; (2) `NS-SKYBOX-CUBEMAP-EXTINCTION` — the static SkyBox star **cubemap** (`SkyBoxFS`) is NOT extinguished (only the catalog starfield is); extinguishing it per-fragment (same airmass model, `dot(normalize(v_texCoord), cameraUpTeme)`) needs the WebGPU skybox path too and is independently schedulable. - **NS-SUN-BLEND-MODE-DIVERGENCE** (surfaced 2026-07-10 by C7-SUN-STARS-EXTINCTION; Principle 9 follow-up; PRE-EXISTING, doc-only, independently schedulable). The sun/moon flare layer is composited with **different blend modes on the two backends**, so the now-extinguished low-horizon sun disc reads differently even though the extinction transmittance is at exact parity. **WebGL** (`Scene/Sun.js` ~line 310) draws the sun billboard with `BlendingState.ALPHA_BLEND` (`src.a × src + (1−src.a) × dst`): the dim red disc + its dark surrounding halo **replace** the sky, so the extinguished sun reads as a dim red disc sitting in a darkened patch of sky (see `probe-sun-stars-extinction-sun-webgl-horizon-low.png`). **WebGPU** (`Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js` lines 517-532, Batch 106 Slice 5c-B) draws the same flare with an **additive** blend (`src.a × src + 1 × dst`): the layer can only *brighten* the destination, so the dimmed sun fades to a faint pale glow over the sky and never darkens the surrounding halo (see `probe-sun-stars-extinction-sun-webgpu-horizon-low.png`). Both looked acceptable before extinction because a full-brightness white disc dominates either composite; extinction exposes the divergence at the dim end. **Fix (deferred):** bring the two backends to the same blend model — either (a) switch the WebGPU sun/moon flare pipeline to alpha blending to match the WebGL `ALPHA_BLEND` reference (requires the WGSL flare shader to output the halo in the alpha channel the way the GLSL path expects, and re-checking the moon flare which shares the same pipeline), or (b) confirm additive is the intended fork look and re-tune the WebGL path to match it. Either direction must stay **off-gate byte-identical** (the change only affects the flare composite, which is always drawn — verify the bright-sun case is unchanged) and be probe-verified against both PNGs. M effort. **Trace:** 2026-07-10.

- **C6-TPDF-DITHER-FINAL** — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-09, Campaign 6, WebGPU-only exceed-feature). Triangular-PDF (TPDF) dither added to the WebGPU tonemap stage to break visible banding across large smooth sky/atmosphere/fog gradients before 8-bit quantization. `Tonemapping.wgsl` + `Tonemapping_f16.wgsl` gain a `ditherStrength` field on `TonemapUniforms` (UBO grown 16→32 bytes, add-only, three trailing pads for 16-byte alignment) and a `tpdfDither(fragCoord, strength)` helper: two independent fract-hash samples subtracted → triangular PDF on (−1,1), scaled by `strength/255` and added after gamma. Opt-in via `scene.ditherEnabled` (optional `scene.ditherStrength`, default ±1 LSB), wired through `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection` → `pipeline.setTonemapDither()` (writes the 5th uniform float). **Off-gate byte-identical:** default OFF writes strength 0.0 → the added term is exactly `tri * 0 = 0` → frame bit-identical to pre-feature; no new pass/allocation (rides the existing tonemap stage). WebGL unaffected (WebGPU-only). **Verified** `probe-tpdf-dither.mjs` (HDR path, smooth sky strip): OFF distinctColors 99 / maxRun 10 → ON distinctColors 200 / maxRun 4 (banding broken), off-after-toggle frame hash IDENTICAL to OFF, 0 console errors, PNGs read. Files: `Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/Tonemapping.wgsl`, `Tonemapping_f16.wgsl`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts` (`setTonemapDither` + uniform layout), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts` (scene-flag wiring), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-tpdf-dither.mjs` (new gate). **Follow-up:** `C6-TPDF-DITHER-SDR-PATH` (below). **Trace:** 2026-07-09.

- **C6-TPDF-DITHER-SDR-PATH** (surfaced 2026-07-09 by C6-TPDF-DITHER-FINAL; Principle 9 follow-up). The shipped TPDF dither lives in the tonemap stage, which is **only enabled when `scene.highDynamicRange = true`** (the HDR post-process pipeline uses rgba16float ping-pong intermediates, so the sub-LSB dither survives in floating point until the final downcast to the 8-bit canvas). In the DEFAULT SDR pipeline the scene framebuffer is `bgra8unorm` (8-bit) — the sky/atmosphere gradients are quantized (and their banding baked) in the SCENE render **before** any post-process stage runs, so a post-tonemap dither cannot recover them. Closing the SDR path needs one of: (a) apply the dither at the point of 8-bit write inside the gradient-producing shaders (`SkyAtmosphere.wgsl` / `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` fog / `AerialPerspective.wgsl`) — scattered but exact; or (b) render the SDR scene to a higher-precision (rg11b10ufloat/rgba16float) target and dither at the final blit — one place but changes default memory/format and must stay byte-identical when off. Both are M effort and independently schedulable. Until then, banding reduction is HDR-only (documented in the shader comment + the tonemap-stage no-op in SDR). **Trace:** 2026-07-09.

- **C6-AERIAL-ELLIPSOID-SNAP** — ⛔ PREMISE DOES NOT REPRODUCE (investigated 2026-07-10, Campaign 6/7; reverted to a clean tree, no code shipped). Brief: port Takram three-geospatial (MIT) `correctGeometricError` into `AerialPerspective.wgsl` — snap the depth-reconstructed world position onto the analytic ellipsoid before the inscatter march to fix the far-zoom coarse-L0/L1-tile **horizon inscatter color error**. **Finding: the technique is effectively inert on Cesium's WebGPU globe.** Cesium tessellates every globe surface tile (incl. coarse LODs) to a 65×65 grid that tracks the analytic ellipsoid tightly, so the depth-reconstructed world positions are already on/above the analytic ellipsoid essentially everywhere. Two faithful ports were built + probed (`probe-aerial-ellipsoid-snap.mjs`, far view = 1200 km alt over 38.8°N, near view = 6 km): (1) **radial snap** onto the WGS84 analytic ellipsoid (latitude-aware; snapping to the scalar equatorial `innerRadius` sphere is wrong — it lifts ALL non-equatorial terrain outward by km) fired on a thin limb sliver only and changed the along-ray march distance negligibly (maxD 0.001, 0 pixels above 6/255) because a radial move at the grazing horizon is nearly perpendicular to the view ray; (2) **ray↔ellipsoid intersection snap** (the geometrically correct "put the fragment on the analytic surface along the ray") changed only ~13 limb pixels by maxD 0.010 (~2.5/255). Both are visually a no-op. A shader tint confirmed the undershoot gate fires only on a ~few-hundred-pixel limb sliver. **The visible far-zoom horizon banding is a DIFFERENT root cause:** the bright bands follow the **tile grid** (rectangular per-tile blocks near the limb), i.e. per-tile depth-discontinuity / low-step (`INSCATTER_STEPS = 10`) march quantization at LOD-tile boundaries — NOT a radial geometric-error undershoot. **Real fixes to schedule instead:** (a) raise/jitter `INSCATTER_STEPS` or add a per-pixel march-start dither in `AerialPerspective.wgsl` (ties into C6-TPDF-DITHER-SDR-PATH's "dither the gradient producer" option-a); (b) investigate the per-tile depth discontinuity feeding `eyeDistance` at coarse-LOD tile seams. The scaffolding for the snap (an opt-in `scene.aerialPerspectiveEllipsoidSnap` flag on a spare `froxelParams.z` bit + an appended `ellipsoidRadii` UBO vec4) is trivial to re-add if a future renderer path (e.g. Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles or a genuinely coarse mesh) produces real geometric error — but it buys nothing on the tessellated globe today. **Trace:** 2026-07-10.

- **C6-FFT-OCEAN** — ✅ SHIPPED v1 (2026-07-11, Campaign 6/7, WebGPU-only exceed-feature; closes the deferred WATER "GPU FFT spectral ocean" gap — zero ocean-surface geometry existed before). A GPU FFT spectral ocean: a per-frame compute chain synthesizes an animated wave displacement + foam map from a Tessendorf/Phillips spectrum, and a camera-anchored RTE ENU grid patch samples it to render a displaced, Fresnel-shaded ocean surface with Jacobian foam. Compute chain (single 256×256 cascade): `OceanInitialSpectrum.wgsl` h0(k)/conj(h0(-k)) (once/on-param-change) → `OceanTwiddle.wgsl` butterfly index+factor LUT (once) → `OceanTimeSpectrum.wgsl` time-evolve h(k,t)=h0·e^{iwt}+conj(h0(-k))·e^{-iwt} into packed Dy+iDx and Dz complex fields (per frame) → `OceanIFFT.wgsl` log2(N) horizontal + log2(N) vertical radix-2 butterfly stages ×2 fields (ping-pong rg32float, per-stage compute passes so writes sync) → `OceanMerge.wgsl` (-1)^(x+y) fftshift correct + 1/N normalize → filterable rgba16float (λ·Dx, Dy, λ·Dz, foam). `OceanSurface.wgsl` VS displaces a 200×200-quad grid patch (grid∈[-0.5,0.5]×patchExtent, world-anchored UV=ENU/L, curvature drop −d²/2R, RTE anchor via EncodedCartesian3 high/low + mvpRelativeToEye — never absolute f32 position) and FS shades finite-diff normal + Schlick Fresnel (F0=0.02) + Blinn sun specular + Jacobian foam, wave-detail faded over the B630 70 km→1e6 m handover band. **License:** FFT butterfly + spectrum packing derived from gasgiant/FFT-Ocean, Popov72/OceanDemo, WebTide (all MIT, attributed in file headers); Phillips spectrum derived from Tessendorf's published SIGGRAPH notes. FFT sign/index conventions CPU-validated against a brute-force IDFT before porting (butterfly output == unnormalized IDFT, no fftshift permutation; the (-1)^(x+y) is only for the centered-spectrum indexing used here). **Opt-in default-off / byte-identical:** `scene.globe.water.ocean.enabled` (default false) lazily creates one `OceanSurfacePrimitive` and adds it to `scene.primitives`; nothing is allocated/dispatched/drawn until enabled; disabling removes+destroys it (frees all GPU textures). `FeatureRendererKey.FFT_OCEAN=53` (COUNT 53→54, add-only) registered via LAZY loader in `WebGPUFeatureRenderers.ts`; `ShaderSourceId.OCEAN_SURFACE=41` (add-only, LOG_DEPTH ifdef). WebGL contexts never register the FR → `OceanSurfacePrimitive.update` early-returns on `!context.isWebGPU` (documented no-op, Principle 2/10). **Verified** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-fft-ocean.mjs` (WebGPU, fresh-load deterministic sessions): OFF-gate off1-vs-off2(toggle) delta **0.0** == base noise-floor off1-vs-off1b **0.0** (byte-identical, no residue); - **C6-PLANAR-REFLECT-REFRACT** — ⏸️ **UNBLOCKED-BUT-DEFERRED (premise re-verified REAL + gate now GREEN; investigated 2026-07-11, Campaign 6/7, no code shipped — clean tree).** Queue #20 (`QUEUE_2026-07-06_CAMPAIGN7.md`) rated M/epic and gated behind #19 (FFT ocean) with an explicit "SKIP if FFT ocean not landed" rule. **Premise verification:** (a) NOT stale — no planar reflection exists. `OceanSurface.wgsl` FS (lines 153–158) reflects the sky with a crude *analytic* approximation only (`skyColor = mix(shallowColor, hardcoded (0.55,0.72,0.92), clamp(dot(reflectDir, up)))` blended by Schlick Fresnel); there is no reflection render pass, no oblique near-plane clip matrix, no projective reflection texture, and no per-surface `reflection` opt-in. The only "Reflection"-named file, `WebGPUBindGroupReflection.ts`, is Naga bind-group-layout *introspection*, unrelated. (b) **Gate is now GREEN** — the #19 dependency `C6-FFT-OCEAN` shipped Batch 654 (`08af2cd678`), so the SKIP condition no longer applies; this item is genuinely unblocked and ready to build as the next planned step. **Why deferred (not force-landed):** a faithful three.js-`Reflector` planar reflection is a multi-day *scene-renderer-orchestration* epic in the most intricate subsystem, NOT a self-contained feature-renderer change, and could not be landed verified-green within a single task's budget. The specific structural blocker: the ocean FR emits a **deferred** `WebGPUDrawCommand` via `frameState.commandList.push` (`WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts` ~L977–986, `Pass.OPAQUE`) that the scene renderer executes *later* — so the reflection texture must be produced by a reflected-camera globe/sky re-render **before** that deferred draw runs, which means hooking the 4505-line `WebGPUSceneRenderer` frame orchestration (a camera-snapshot/repoint/restore + offscreen render), not the primitive's `update()`. **Concrete design for the next campaign (reuses proven machinery):** (1) Add opt-in `reflection` option to `OceanSurfacePrimitive` (default off → byte-identical; no target allocated, no extra pass when off). (2) Build the reflected virtual camera by mirroring the main camera across the ocean's local tangent plane at the anchor (`_anchor` + `_up` normal, both already computed each frame), and apply a **Lengyel oblique near-plane clip** (the water plane in eye space) so sub-surface geometry is clipped out of the reflection — the classic Reflector/Water technique. (3) Produce the reflection color target by REUSING the exact reflected-camera re-render pattern already proven in `WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapCapture.runSceneCapture` (snapshot `uniformState.camera` proxy fields → repoint to the reflected+oblique camera → ask the globe renderer to build its OWN draw commands → render into the reflection target with `loadOp:'clear'` to the sky fill → restore the main camera in a `finally`, honoring the same `_logDepthEncodeNearFar` stash caveat the capture documents). Single target (one reflected view), not 6 cube faces — cheaper than the env capture. (4) Bind the reflection texture + the reflection view-proj matrix into `OceanSurface.wgsl`; replace the analytic `skyColor` seam (already Fresnel-mixed at L156–158 — the "reflection seam is pre-built" note in C6-FFT-OCEAN follow-up #6) with a **projective** sample of the reflection target (clip→uv), keeping the analytic gradient as the `//>>else`/fallback so `defines=0` stays byte-identical. RTE-correct the projective coords (never an absolute f32 world position). (5) `Refractor`/`Water2` (BSD/MIT) flow-map river advection + screen-space refraction (`C6-SCREEN-SPACE-REFRACT`, queue #24, D, reuses the Hi-Z/scene-depth/scene-color SSR targets) are a *second* increment on top — schedule after the reflection pass lands. **Off-gate contract:** opt-in default-off, byte-identical when off (no target, no pass, no bind-group change on the existing ocean pipeline — gate the new bindings behind a `ShaderDefine` add-only bit + a `//>>else` analytic fallback); WebGPU-only (WebGL never registers the ocean FR → documented no-op, Principle 2/10). **Acceptance probe (to author):** flat ocean patch at low altitude over a coastline; ON = the reflection target shows terrain/sky mirrored with the oblique clip removing below-water geometry (distinguishable from the analytic gradient by reflecting actual terrain silhouettes); OFF = byte-identical to pre-feature (0.0 vs noise floor). **License:** PORT three.js `Reflector`/`Refractor`/`Water`/`Water2` (MIT) with attribution; Lengyel oblique-clip is a published technique (derive). **Files (projected):** `Scene/OceanSurfacePrimitive.js` (+`reflection` option), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts` (reflection target + reflected-camera pass wiring), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts` (pre-ocean reflection re-render hook, mirrors `runSceneCapture`), `Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/OceanSurface.wgsl` (projective reflection sample behind a new add-only `ShaderDefine`), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUShaderDefines.ts` (add-only bit), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-planar-reflect.mjs` (new). **Effort:** multi-day (large). **Trace:** 2026-07-05 (mine, THREEJS_TECH_MINE #22) → 2026-07-11 (premise re-verified real, gate green, decomposition recorded; deferred per the queue's gated-tail honest-partial rule).

C9-09 (`FAR-401-C0`, landed 2026-07-16) already built the authoritative per-frame demand record: `computeAttachmentDemand()` → `context._attachmentDemand` with `gbufferDemanded`, and `context.forceSceneMRT` defaults `true` (conservative always-MRT). The executor is ALREADY topology-parametric on `isSceneFBMrtMode()`: the G-buffer alloc site (`WebGPUContext.updateAndClearFramebuffers` ~L3964), the pass-open slot-1 builder (`WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.buildMrtSlot1Attachment` — returns null when mode off, all three scene-pass-open sites funnel through it), and every pipeline's target array (`makeSceneFBTargets` returns length-1 vs length-2 by mode). Concrete break: `_mrtMode` is a module-global consumed at pipeline-BUILD time by 31 renderers that call `makeSceneFBTargets`, but each renderer caches its built pipeline under its OWN key that does NOT include an MRT-topology dimension — e.g. the whole `WebGPUCollectionRendererBase` family (billboard/label/point/polyline) keys via `pipelineKeyWithDepthFlag(defines, noDepthTest)` (`WebGPUCollectionRendererBase.ts:208`), a Uint32 whose bits 0-30 are ShaderDefine and bit 31 is `NO_DEPTH_TEST_PIPELINE_KEY_BIT` — **no free bit for topology**. Session starts default (`_mrtMode` false) → collection renderers cache 1-target pipelines; user enables SSR → mode flips true, pass becomes 2-attachment, but the per-renderer cache returns the stale 1-target pipeline → "attachment state not compatible" validation error → black/broken frame. (Only the GENERIC `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.generateCacheKey` is already topology-safe — its `tg:` signature at L721-732 folds the target-array shape — but the 31 per-renderer/model/globe/ocean/voxel/gsplat/etc. caches are not.) The queue row's own phrasing "**Cache exact one-target/MRT variants**" is precisely this: every scene-FB pipeline cache must key BOTH variants by topology (or a global flush-on-flip broadcast must reach all 31 renderers — none exists today). **Additional gating:** queue §3 states "Attachment topology … wait for Gate B unless an explicit gate amendment records why the slice is correctness-independent"; this slice is NOT correctness-independent (it changes frame topology with a feature-break-on-toggle risk), and Gate B is not cleanly passed (the Gate-B item `C9-02A` is PARTIAL/PAUSED and spawned `NEW-WEBGPU-HDR-PICK-FORMAT-CLOSURE` + `NEW-WEBGPU-ASYNC-PICK-PIPELINE-READINESS-CONTRACT`). **Recommended phasing for a dedicated multi-batch run (each lands green, byte-identical when no consumer):** (P0) add a topology dimension to the pipeline-cache key of EVERY scene-FB renderer — widen the collection-family key past 32 bits (`` `${defines}:${mrt}` `` or a safe-int fold, since bits 0-31 are full) and audit each of the 31 `makeSceneFBTargets` callers (billboard, label, point, polyline, buffer-point/polygon/polyline, cloud, compute-instance, cubemap-panorama, depth-plane, derived-command, edge-visibility, ellipsoid, environment, flow-field, gaussian-splat, ground-polyline, ground-primitive, model-pipeline-cache, ocean, point-cloud + EDL, primitive-commands, sky-atmosphere, starfield, vector3d-{clamped-polylines,polylines,primitive}, voxel, weather) so BOTH the 1-target and 2-target pipeline are cacheable and selected by the current mode — verify via a probe that toggles a consumer mid-session with zero validation errors; lands byte-identical because default is still forced-MRT. (P1) gate the G-buffer alloc + MSAA companion + resolve on `context._attachmentDemand.gbufferDemanded` and call `setSceneFBMrtMode(gbufferDemanded)` in `updateAndClearFramebuffers` before any pipeline builds — still with `forceSceneMRT` default true, so still byte-identical but now the machinery is demand-wired. A correct retention needs a per-(renderer-instance = per-device)-keyed per-tile-per-pass packet cache with an explicit revision-tuple invalidation, per-frame in-place dynamic-offset + non-3D-BV update, and derived-command (translucency/pick) staleness handling — a dedicated multi-batch slice with its own 9-waypoint + water/clipping/shadow/exaggeration/2D-CV-morph + multi-view + device-loss acceptance matrix. **Off-gate:** the landed closure hoist is byte-identical by construction (no toggle; it always renders identically). **Files (landed):** `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js` (hoisted `executeWebGPUGlobeTileCommand` + two call-site refs). **Files (projected for the remainder):** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts` (retained descriptor packets + revision keys), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTypes.ts`, `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js` (retained wrapper cache + in-place per-frame field update), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-retained-terrain-descriptors.mjs` (new). **Effort:** remainder = L/epic, multi-batch. **Trace:** 2026-07-16 (C9-11 — premise verified real vs live code; byte-identical closure core landed + verified; wrapper/descriptor/array retention deferred per honest-partial / clean-tree rule).

- **C9-12-TERRAIN-STATIC-DYNAMIC-UPLOAD-SPLIT** (`FAR-303`, queue #30, R2) — ⏸️ **DEFERRED / BLOCKED (premise verified REAL; investigated 2026-07-16, Campaign 9; no code shipped — clean tree).** Goal: separate stable per-tile/material UB bytes from per-view/per-frustum ring data so changed tiles only rewrite their own ranges and per-frame upload calls AND bytes fall with no stale multi-view or mode data. Acceptance: API-lane writeBuffer bytes/frame drop materially from the ~112.9 KB / 10.03 writes-per-frame Gate-A baseline on settled frames, multi-view + mode-switch + mutation correctness green. **Premise verification (NOT stale — CONFIRMED gap):** the packers still stage the FULL uniform width per tile per imagery pass through the ring every frame — `createCameraUniformBufferHelper` (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1348`) packs `CAMERA_UNIFORM_FLOATS = 232` (928 B → 1024 aligned) and `createTileUniformBufferHelper` (`:1358`) packs `TILE_UNIFORM_FLOATS = 484` (1936 B → 2048 aligned) = **3072 B staged/tile/pass**, both routed through `writeUniformSlice → context.uniformAllocator.allocateAndWrite` (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:1028`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts`). C9-01 measured 39,300 descriptors × 3072 B ≈ **115.1 MiB** aligned staging over the route; the ring coalesces this into ~112.9 KB of `queue.writeBuffer`/frame. No static/dynamic split, no persistent per-tile static slab, and no revision-keyed skip exist in live code. The counters `cameraUniformAlignedBytes`/`tileUniformAlignedBytes` (`:1373`/`:1380`) confirm both packs run unconditionally every pass. **Why blocked as a single session (fundamental coupling, not a shortcut gap):** every byte-reducing approach reduces to one of two, and both are epic-scale or forbidden. (A) **The intended lever — WGSL static/dynamic struct split + shared static slab:** split the single group-0 `CameraUniforms`+`TileUniforms` into `ViewUniforms` (per-view, packed once/frame), `TileDynamicUniforms` (`modifiedModelView`/`modifiedModelViewProjection` — the irreducible f64 `view × mesh.center` RTE product, ~128 B → 256 aligned/tile/frame via the ring), and `TileStaticUniforms` (center3D hi/lo, scaleAndBias, minMaxHeight, projected tileRectangle/mercatorY, per-imagery-revision layer blocks, water-mask TS, flags — written to a persistent slab via `queue.writeBuffer` ONLY on a per-tile revision miss). This is the ~12× per-tile upload cut. It requires editing `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` (~3300 lines) group-0 struct declarations + EVERY field access, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceLayouts.ts` BGL 0, every pipeline layout, `_getOrCreateBindGroup0`, and the shared wireframe (`createWireframeTileCommands`) + env-capture (`getOrCreateCaptureTileCommands`, which also calls `_getOrCreateBindGroup0`) + pick vertex-stage paths — a single atomic bytes-on-wire slice that must be pixel-identical across all scenes and revert as one clean commit. (B) **Per-tile persistent full buffers (no WGSL change):** storing each tile's full UB in its own persistent `GPUBuffer` and skipping re-upload when unchanged would break the healthy 99.66%-hit group-0 bind-group cache — that cache keys on (camera-page, tile-page) buffer IDENTITY with byte offsets riding as dynamic offsets (Batch 292); one persistent buffer per tile means one bind-group create per tile, regressing the exact cache the campaign relies on. Forbidden by rule (never regress a working path for a metric). Only a shared static slab with dynamic offsets (option A) keeps one buffer identity — and that needs the struct split. **The deeper blocker:** knowing WHICH tiles' static bytes changed (to rewrite only their slab ranges) is exactly the exact-revision-key per-tile packet store of `C9-11` Slice 1, whose retained-descriptor/wrapper/array foundation is itself **DEFERRED** (see the C9-11 entry above — landed only the byte-identical execute-closure hoist; the revision-keyed packet cache with the full invalidation tuple is unbuilt). Additionally, the win is on MOVING frames (settled frames already re-stage identical bytes the ring could in principle skip, but the acceptance's "settled frames" reduction still needs the same revision machinery). **Recommended phasing for a dedicated multi-batch run (each lands green + byte-identical off-path; mirrors the execution-guide G6 slices 0–4):** (S0) effects-handle hoist — already landed as `C9-13`/`NEW-GLOBE-EFFECTS-PER-VIEW-PREPARED-HANDLE` (Batch 677); consume its `_getOrCreateFrameEffectsBindGroup` handle. Do items (1)+(3) first as cheap independently-landable Earth-default-byte-identical de-riskers. Per-body LUT re-bake is nearly free (we already re-dispatch on sun-move/ozone-toggle; a body switch is one params-UBO swap, <1 ms; v1 = `lastProfileHash` re-bake key, v2 = per-body LRU slots ~1.4–1.7 MB/body). **Both backends** (Principle 5): WebGL params flow through existing uniforms once thickness is a uniform; no WebGL LUT needed. **License:** CLEAN — real prior art (Bruneton BSD-3, Hillaire/Epic MIT, Takram MIT+BSD-3+Apache stack, OpenSpace/Costa MIT, CosmoScout/Schneegans MIT) all permissive; **parameter VALUES are unprotectable facts** (our LUT chain is in-house so nothing is owed). ## NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-FLEET-LOG-DEPTH — pick mini-frame depth is fleet-wide hyperbolic; the P0-1 pick depth-plane gate is blocked on converting ALL pick producers to log frag_depth (2026-07-16)

Surfaced by `NEW-WEBGPU-DEPTH-PLANE-LOG-DEPTH-CONTRACT` (Campaign 9, audit P0-1). The scene-side half
of that contract landed (see `WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md` same date): `WebGPUDepthPlane.update` now
encodes its scene log depth against the full-frustum `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` stash like
every other scene producer, and the three-altitude horizon oracle's scene assertions went from
all-fail (Sol run) to pass at 500 km/5,000 km with only the sprite-above-limb residual at 20 km.
The pick-side half — re-enabling `PICK_DEPTH_PLANE_ENABLED` in `WebGPUSceneRendererPickPass.ts` — is
**blocked on a fleet-scale prerequisite** proven by two instrumented oracle runs on 2026-07-16:

- **The pick FBO contract today is uniformly hyperbolic.** Every native pick producer — globe
  `fragmentPickMain` (deliberate-design note at `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` ~L3048), all three Model pick
  entries, Billboard/Polyline/PointPrimitive pick shaders, all six `PrimitivePick*.wgsl` — writes
  standard rasterizer z, baked at UPDATE time against the camera's own frustum (native pick commands
  bind update-time camera UBs; the pick loop's per-slice `_updateFrustumUniforms` remap only reaches
  draw-time uniformState consumers such as the depth plane). Run 1 (log-variant plane pick pipeline):
  the plane's log frag_depth (~0.4-0.8) over-occluded EVERY hyperbolic pick (~0.999+) over the whole
  globe disk — even the visible front control returned null at 20/500/5,000 km. Run-1 variant with a
  per-slice hyperbolic plane pick pipeline mismatched the update-time bake the same way.
- **Hyperbolic depth cannot pass the oracle even when made consistent.** With every producer on the
  shared update-time camera projection (near ≈ 1 m, far ≈ 5e8 m), the plane-vs-marker separation at
  5,000 km is Δz ≈ n·Δ(1/d) ≈ 1.7e-8 — below one float32 ulp at z≈1.0 (6e-8) — and `less-equal`
  ties pass, so the beyond-horizon marker stays pickable. Only log-encoded pick depth has the
  far-field resolution the 20/500/5,000 km oracle demands (WebGL parity: upstream's LOG_DEPTH
  wrapper applies to every derived pick shader, so the WebGL pick FBO is log).
- **Therefore:** converting only the oracle participants (plane + points) to log breaks every other
  cohort at defaults (models/billboards/polylines/primitives over the globe would be over-occluded
  by the log plane, and log points would pick through hyperbolic models); keeping hyperbolic can
  never reject the far marker. The only correct end state is the WHOLE pick fleet writing log
  frag_depth with one encode (`_logDepthEncodeNearFar`), mirroring the scene contract: ~15+ pick
  WGSL entries (collections ×3, primitives ×6, model ×3, globe ×1, buffer primitives, vector-tile /
  voxel / splat / point-cloud / ellipsoid / classification renderers) plus per-renderer verification
  that the encode scalars reach each pick bind group, across HDR/MSAA/modes/resize/recovery.

Evidence: `Tools/visual-regression/output/performance/campaign9-c9-02b-depth-plane-horizon-oracle-2026-07-16.json`
(final-tree run: scene draws green, pick assertions honestly failing with the gate off) plus the six
read `campaign9-c9-02b-horizon-{near,middle,far}-plane-{on,off}.png` captures. Regressions green on
the landed scene half: `probe-point-pick-webgpu` PASS, `probe-collections-far-camera` PASS (includes
the below-ground occlusion negative control), `probe-logdepth-globe` clean. Also noted: the 20 km
"leak" (538 px) and 500 km residual (70 px) in the oracle are the screen-space sprite quad extending
ABOVE the horizon line where neither plane nor globe covers pixels — identical WebGL geometry; a
future oracle revision should count only below-limb marker pixels. `C9-02B` acceptance and the P0-1
gate flip stay paused behind this item.

### Phase-0 premise correction (C10-11, 2026-07-18) — the fleet is larger + one producer has NO log-depth infrastructure ⇒ all-or-nothing BLOCKED

Re-derived the exact native pick-producer fleet at HEAD (Batch 706) before attempting the conversion.
Two premise corrections vs the C10 guide H6 walkthrough:

- **Voxel is NOT Cohort A — it has ZERO log-depth infrastructure and is the hard blocker.**
  `WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts` has 0 occurrences of `LOG_DEPTH`/`logDepth`/`v_logDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth`/
  `frag_depth` (grep-confirmed). Its COLOR entry `fragmentMain` (`:760`) returns a bare
  `@location(0) vec4<f32>` (hyperbolic), and its two pick entries (`fragmentPickMain :1009`,
  `fragmentPickVoxelMain :1103`) do the same; both pick pipelines are `depthWriteEnabled:false`
  (`:2679`, `:2710`). The voxel UBO (`struct Uniforms :185`) carries `mvpRelativeToEye` but no
  near/factor/far log lanes. The renderer-wide log-depth epic (`NEW-WEBGPU-GLOBE-CLASSIFY-DEPTH-PRECISION`,
  §1565) converted "ALL GEOMETRY/**OPAQUE** PRODUCERS" only; the voxel (translucent volumetric, writes
  no depth) was **deliberately excluded** and is not among the tracked residuals (§1607 lists only the
  standalone point-cloud + splat, both since shipped). So the guide's claim that voxel's "module already
  carries LOG_DEPTH ifdefs + the `v_logDepth` varying from its color path" is false. Converting voxel
  pick cleanly is a mini-epic (grow the voxel UBO with log lanes, add `csm_vertexLogDepth`/
  `csm_writeLogDepth` + a `v_logDepth` varying, define plumbing, AND a design decision on what depth a
  volumetric first-hit pick writes — box-surface vs density-hit) that belongs to a voxel-color
  log-depth prerequisite (extend `NEW-LOG-DEPTH-REMAINING-PRODUCERS` to the voxel), NOT this pick slice.
- **Because the pick FBO has ONE shared depth attachment (INV-2) and Rule 3 forbids shipping a partial
  fleet, the voxel blocker STOPS the whole all-or-nothing landing.** No engine code was changed. The
  smallest unblock: land the voxel color→log-depth conversion first, then C10-11 converts the entire
  fleet (including both voxel pick entries) in one coordinated change.

### NEW-WEBGPU-VOXEL-PICK-LOG-DEPTH — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-18) — the voxel blocker is cleared; C10-11 is UNBLOCKED

The voxel pick log-depth prerequisite is done. `WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts` now has the full log-depth
infrastructure on both PICK entries, add-only and gated OFF by default so today's uniformly-hyperbolic
pick FBO is byte-identical:

- **Premise-verify verdict (no maintainer design call needed).** Both pick fragments already resolve a
  well-defined FIRST hit (`fragmentPickMain`: first `s.a > densityThreshold` sample; `fragmentPickVoxelMain`:
  first density hit / first alpha-saturating sample). The hit POSITIONS, however, are NOT Rule-4-liftable:
  `fragmentPickMain`'s `p` lives in the camera-CENTERED ±0.5 phantom box (`cameraPositionEC=0`,
  `minBounds/maxBounds=±0.5`) — `mvpRelativeToEye * p` gives a degenerate ~0.5 m depth, NOT the voxel's
  real distance; `fragmentPickVoxelMain`'s hit is in proxy/shape-local space (an absolute-ECEF f32
  reconstruction to lift it → Rule-4 violation). So BOTH entries use the **box PROXY geometry front-face
  log depth** — the `v_logDepth` varying the VS computes via the clean RTE clip path (`input.worldPos →
  mvpRelativeToEye`, then `csm_vertexLogDepth`), the task-sanctioned conservative default (the first hit
  is at or behind the entry face; the box is meters-scale vs the km-scale pick-depth-plane discriminator).
  This encodes the depth at which the pick ray enters the picked volume — a plausible, non-degenerate,
  monotonic log depth using the SAME encode as the scene fleet. The picked VoxelPrimitive/cell is
  UNCHANGED (determined by the ray-march, not the frag_depth).
- **Fix summary (file:symbol).** `WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts`: (1) UBO `struct Uniforms` — repurposed the two
  zero vec3 pads (`_pad0`→`logDepthNear` float 19, `_pad1`→`logDepthFactor` float 23; byte layout
  UNCHANGED so color/velocity are unaffected), packed from `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` (FULL
  frustum, preferred) with the `currentFrustum`/`oneOverLog2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne` fallback (identical
  recipe to `WebGPUEllipsoidPrimitiveRenderer.packUniforms`); (2) added `csm_vertexLogDepth`/
  `csm_updatePositionDepth`/`csm_writeLogDepth` + `VertexOutput.v_logDepth` + the `vertexMain` compute,
  all `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH`; (3) `fragmentPickMain` + `fragmentPickVoxelMain` now return a shared
  `VoxelPickFragOutput` struct that carries `@builtin(frag_depth) = csm_writeLogDepth(v_logDepth, factor)`
  under `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH` (the `//>>else` single-`@location(0)` struct is output-byte-identical to the
  historical bare-vec4 return; every discard/return site preserved for naga's NEW-4-E terminator analysis);
  (4) the two PICK pipelines compile the LOG_DEPTH module + `depthWriteEnabled:true` (distinct `[ld]`
  descriptor names) ONLY when the gate is active, with a flip-rebuild guard stamped alongside the
  format/MSAA generation. Gate: new `isWebGPUPickLogDepthActive(context, frameState)` in
  `WebGPULogDepth.ts` + `WebGPUContext._pickLogDepthWriteEnabled` (default **FALSE** — the pick-fleet
  master switch, SEPARATE from the scene `_logDepthWriteEnabled`, since the pick mini-frame's shared depth
  attachment is all-or-nothing).
- **Evidence.** `probe-voxel-pick.mjs` PASS (gate off — cell picks correct cross-backend, 0 errors →
  default byte-identical); `probe-voxel-parity.mjs` PASS (voxel COLOR footprint IoU 0.986, avg-color L1
  **0**, 0 errors → color path untouched); NEW `probe-voxel-pick-logdepth.mjs` PASS (gate FORCED on:
  `[ld]` pick pipelines bound with `depthWriteEnabled:true`; cell + object picks still return the correct
  voxel; a nearer "blocker" voxel correctly OCCLUDES a farther one in the shared pick FBO → positive proof
  the log frag_depth is WRITTEN, non-degenerate, and monotonic; 0 device/console errors → the LOG_DEPTH
  module and both pick pipelines compiled/built); `capture-and-diff --scene globe-default` PASS (crossBackend 0.46%,
  no collateral). Gates: `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, `gulp build` clean, `buildAllVariants` clean,
  `variant-smoke-test` all 3 PASS.
- **C10-11 (`NEW-WEBGPU-PICK-FLEET-LOG-DEPTH`) is now UNBLOCKED.** The voxel row below is done; C10-11
  converts the remaining ~22 pick entries and flips `_pickLogDepthWriteEnabled` true in one coordinated

## C9-07-DEMAND-OPEN-CANVAS-PASS latent findings (2026-07-16)

Surfaced (verified against live code, NOT fixed) while landing the FAR-405-C0 demand-open canvas
slice — each needs its own oracle before any code change (Principle 9):

- **`NEW-WEBGPU-RENDERCOMMAND-STALE-PASS-SLOT`** — `Renderer/WebGPU/RenderCommand.js:345`
  (`_executeWebGPU`) reads `context._currentRenderPass`, a property that does not exist on
  `WebGPUContext` (the real slot is `_currentRenderPassEncoder`), so the expression always falls
  through to `passState` and the immediate-mode RenderCommand WebGPU path never receives the active
  pass encoder. Latent and independent of the demand-open slice (pre-existing). Fix needs a consumer
  probe first — no current caller exercises the broken branch on the default route.
- **`NEW-WEBGPU-CANVAS-BACKGROUND-COLOR-PARITY`** — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01 (Batch 802).** The WebGPU
  context `_clearColor` was `(0,0,0,0)` from the constructor and was never fed
  `scene.backgroundColor`; the background `_clearColorCommand` targeting the default framebuffer was
  swallowed by the C9-07 / FAR-405-C0 deferred-canvas-clear return, so an EMPTY WebGPU scene
  presented transparent black while WebGL cleared to the scene background color. Root cause: WebGL's
  `Context.clear` records every requested value into GL clear-state (`gl.clearColor` /
  `clearDepth` / `clearStencil`) BEFORE issuing `gl.clear`, and the WebGPU port kept only the
  `gl.clear` half — so the deferral's premise that the pending first open "delivers the same
  `_clearColor`/`_clearDepth`/`_clearStencil` values" was false for colour.
  **Fix**: new `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUCanvasClearState.ts` owns the request interpretation
  (`isClearChannelRequested`) and the canvas-only, per-channel state capture
  (`canvasClearStateUpdate`) as pure functions; `WebGPUContext.clear` calls the capture BEFORE the
  deferral return and copies each non-`null` channel into `_clearColor`/`_clearDepth`/`_clearStencil`.
  Capture is restricted to clears resolving to the canvas swap view, so an offscreen clear (OIT,
  globe depth, pick, a post-process intermediate) can never repaint the page background.
  The module states an explicit absence contract — input is the inherited `ClearCommand` tri-state
  (`T | false | undefined`) collapsed in exactly one place, output uses `null` as its sole absence
  sentinel and never `undefined` — because three unstated spellings of "nothing here" is how a
  caller writes `if (update.color)` and drops the transparent-black capture this fix exists to keep.
  **Evidence**: `Tools/visual-regression/env-background-clear.spec.mjs` (21 tests: Part A proves the
  environment-demand predicate was NOT the defect, B/B' the module + its absence contract, C the
  frame timeline with a negative control reproducing the pre-fix transparent black, D the call-site
  ordering). Cross-backend pixel behaviour is gated by
  `Tools/visual-regression/probe-env-background-clear.mjs`, which has **not been run** — this
  landed as an extraction from a parked worktree and the probe needs a browser lane.
- **`NEW-WEBGPU-OIT-DEFERRED-SPLAT-CANVAS-RESUME`** — `WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts`
  (~L348) resumes the DEFAULT (canvas) pass after the OIT composite, mid-frustum-loop, and draws
  deferred Gaussian splats inline there; the comment says "resumed scene pass" but the target is the
  canvas, and the post-process blit later overwrites the canvas — likely invisible splats under
  OIT+splats scenes. Behavior unchanged by C9-07 (the resume now first-opens with clear instead of
  loading the beginFrame clear — identical bytes). Needs a splats+OIT visual probe before redirecting
  to `_resumeScenePass`.
- **`NEW-SCENEOCTREE-DIRTY-REVISION-REBUILD-AND-PVS-PROMOTION`** — C9-08 landed the default-path
  demand gate (material-sort maintenance is now zero-work with no consumer; SceneOctree/OcclusionCulling
  stay call-site-gated to zero work at defaults). The remaining C9-08 acceptance clause — "enabled
  SceneOctree uses dirty/revision rebuild and must beat ordinary PVS before any auto promotion" — is
  deferred because the octree is strictly **opt-in** (`scene.renderScheduler.octree.enabled`,
  default false) and is **never auto-promoted**, so it has zero default-path exposure. Today an
  enabled octree rebuilds every frame (`SceneOctree.build` clears + re-inserts). Before any auto
  promotion could be justified, add: (a) a revision/dirty signal so a static command set skips the
  clear+re-insert; (b) a measured comparison proving the enabled octree beats ordinary Scene PVS on
  the moving multi-altitude route with >200 primitive commands (`minCommandsForOctree`); (c) the
  on/off/restored oracle. Files: `packages/engine/Source/Scene/SceneOctree.js`,
  `packages/engine/Source/Scene/ViewportExecutor.js`. Regression probe already in tree:
  `Tools/visual-regression/probe-scheduler-octree-demand.mjs` (currently asserts default zero-work +
  demand-gate byte-identity; extend case E with a >200-command parity lane when this is picked up).

## NEW-CLUSTERED-ENABLED-ZERO-LIGHT-FRAME-ZERO-WORK (surfaced by C9-16 certification, 2026-07-16)

**Status:** deferred optimization, NOT on any default render path (Forward+ clustered lighting is default-off, `Scene.js` `_clusteredLightingEnabled=false`).

**Context.** `C9-16-CLUSTERED-LIGHT-ZERO-WORK-CONTRACT` was certified COMPLETE for the disabled/defaults path: with clustered lighting OFF the dispatcher allocates, uploads, dispatches, and submits ZERO clustered work per frame (proven by the new unit spec + the new `probe-clustered-zero-work-route.mjs` API-counter gate over the moving multi-altitude route). The enabled→disabled transition writes exactly one zero-count params update; settled disabled frames are no-ops.

**Residual gap (verified live in `WebGPUSceneRendererClusteredLighting.ts`).** When the feature is ENABLED but there are no effective lights (no punctual `scene.lights` survivors AND no area lights), each frame still does per-frame work: it allocates fresh `lights[]`/`areaLights[]` arrays (:198-220), ends+resumes the canvas render pass (:189/:379), and calls `dispatcher.dispatch(...)` which unconditionally writes the 32 B params UBO (`WebGPUClusteredLightingDispatcher.ts` :365) and re-allocates the buffers-stash object literal (:356-365). This is NOT reproduced at defaults (defaults use the disabled early-return path), so it is out of the C9-16 acceptance route.

**Fix (per CAMPAIGN9_OPUS_EXECUTION_GUIDE §C9-16 Step 1, ~40+10 lines).**
- Dispatcher: track last-written `(activeCount, areaCount)`; when both are zero AND the last write was already all-zero, skip the params `writeBuffer` and return 0.
- Hook: hoist `lights[]`/`areaLights[]` to module-level scratch reset with `.length = 0` (the dispatcher copies inputs out synchronously in `_packEyeSpaceLights`/`_packAreaLights` — no retention, verified); when the post-walk state is empty AND the dispatcher's last-written state is already zero, publish the identity-stable buffers stash (invariant 4 — do NOT flip real↔placeholder, it churns the effects bind-group cache), set `_clusteredLightingActive=false`, and return WITHOUT ending/resuming the pass or calling `dispatch`.
- Invariants to preserve: transition N-lights→0-lights still writes params exactly once; buffers stash identity is stable once a dispatcher exists; every enabled-path early return after `endCurrentRenderPass` must resume the pass (decide zero-work BEFORE ending the pass); keep `COPY_SRC` on the params buffer (probe readback); keep the module-level WeakSet keyed per host (multi-context). Gate zero-work on BOTH punctual (`_paramsData[4]`) and area (`_paramsData[5]`) counts being zero.
- The unit spec's "enabled with zero effective lights" case currently asserts today's behavior (one dispatch, buffers published); when the optimization lands, tighten it to assert zero writeBuffer / zero pass end-resume / stable buffer identity, and add the enabled N→0 transition-write case.

**Evidence to reproduce/verify:** `probe-clustered-zero-work-route.mjs` (add an enabled-zero-light phase asserting zero per-frame work), `probe-clustered-matsweep.mjs` + `probe-clustered-phong.mjs` (enabled-path visual byte-identity after the scratch-array conversion).
